glosses: A bus is a vehicle that carries a large number of people on roads.

examples.text: He ran to catch the school bus, which had stopped at a corner to pick up more kids.
This bus makes ten stops before arriving at Union Station.
I woke up late and missed my bus this morning.
Tourists didn't usually ride the local bus.
The bus driver took out tickets as we got on at the station.
The two young men boarded a crowded city bus to go home.
She was the first and only passenger at this bus stop.
Round-trip bus fare to and from the ferry terminal was $1.

glosses: A bus is part of a computer; it moves information.
If you bus people somewhere, you take them there on a bus.

examples.text: The children are bused to school every morning.

glosses: If you bus tables, you take away dirty dishes in a restaurant.
If you practise something, you do it again and again to improve your ability.

examples.text: The class was going to practise writing skills for homework.
When I got my first guitar, I practised until my fingers fell off.

glosses: If you practice something, you do it again and again to improve your ability.

examples.text: The class was going to practice writing skills for homework.
When I got my first guitar, I practiced until my fingers fell off.

glosses: If you practice a subject (specially law and medicine), you pursue it as a career.

examples.text: She practiced law for several years.

glosses: Practice is an activity you do again and again to improve your ability.

examples.text: I can go to the party because I have soccer practice that night.
My driving is getting better, but I still need practice.

glosses: Clothes, such as shirts, pants, socks, etc. are things that people wear on their body to cover it.

examples.text: He took off his clothes and got into the shower.
There was no money to buy clothes, so we got our cousins' old shirts and jeans with holes in the knees.

glosses: The third-person singular form of clothe.
The title of a book, movie, song, etc. is its name.

examples.text: "I just finished the best book." "Really, what's the title?"

glosses: A title is a word or name that describes a person's job or status.

examples.text: His title was Director of Science Education.
The proper title for an unmarried woman is "Miss".

glosses: A title is a legal document that proves you own something.

examples.text: He put the title to his house in a bank for safe keeping.

glosses: To give a title to someone or something.

examples.text: I titled my essay "The History of Japan".

glosses: If something is informal, it is friendly and casual; it is not official.

examples.text: Can we get together for some informal talks before the meeting?
School is generally quite informal. Many students even call their teacher by their first name.

glosses: If you give someone advice, you tell them what you think they should do.

examples.text: Thanks so much! I took your advice and it really helped me get the job.
Excuse me! I'm looking for advice on how to get a loan. Can you help me?

glosses: Engineering is a job or a science about designing and building things.

examples.text: She worked for a civil engineering company, that makes portable bridges.

glosses: The present participle of engineer.
When you program a computer, you use code to tell the computer what to do.

examples.text: The student can program the computer to calculate all of his statistics.
All of the math students know how to program.

glosses: A program is a number of steps that are followed to reach a goal or end.

examples.text: His new exercise program gets more difficult every week.
Oxford College has an excellent English language program.

glosses: A program is a guide to a dramatic or theatrical performance.

examples.text: After he entered the theatre, he bought a copy of the program.

glosses: A (television or radio) program is a broadcast.

examples.text: Star Trek is her favorite program.

glosses: A (computer) program is the code that tells a computer what to do.

examples.text: Microsoft Word is one of the most popular programs in the world.
The new program has a lot of problems. My computer crashes every time I try to run it.

glosses: When you programme a computer, you use code to tell the computer what to do.

examples.text: The student can programme the computer to calculate all of his statistics.

glosses: A (computer) programme is the code that tells a computer what to do.

examples.text: Microsoft Word is one of the most popular programmes in the world.

glosses: A loan is money that you borrow and pay back later. Usually, you take a loan from a bank.

examples.text: We've almost finished paying off our car loan.
We can't afford to buy the new TV without taking a loan.
I'd like to take out a loan for $5,000.

glosses: If you loan someone something, you lend it to them.

examples.text: Please loan me your lawn mower.

glosses: Loan in Hollywood studio speak means an actor is under contract to one studio and loaned to another studio to make one of their films.

examples.text: He was loaned to MGM to make MGM's newest movie.

glosses: A custom or practice of a society or community.

examples.text: The institution of marriage is present in many cultures but its details vary widely across them.

glosses: An institution is a large group of people who work together for a specific purpose. Examples include hospitals, universities, and banks.

examples.text: Banks, insurance companies and other financial institutions are already offering internet services.

glosses: A culture is a common history, set of beliefs, or way of life within a group of people.

examples.text: Rock and roll is a central part of American popular culture.
When I moved to China, it took me a long time to start to understand the culture.

glosses: If you culture bacteria or cells, you grow them.
The facilities in a building include the equipment, services, or places that are available.

examples.text: How much does it cost an employer to provide childcare facilities?
The hotel is cheap, but it still has a lot of facilities for guests.

glosses: The plural form of facility; more than one (kind of) facility.
A lecture is a talk about a specific topic. Usually, it is a planned talk and it often lasts a long time.

examples.text: My teacher is giving a lecture on human rights tonight at the university.

glosses: If you lecture someone, you teach them something.
If you lecture someone, you scold them.
An academic topic, lecture, idea, etc., is one that is connected to education.

examples.text: The academic staff at the college generally don't teach during the summer.
There is a lot of political disagreement about it, but there is general academic agreement.

glosses: An academic is a researcher or university teacher.

examples.text: The government has begun jailing journalists and banning academics from travel.
The book is very popular for one written by an academic.

glosses: Academics is the part of school related to learning.

examples.text: This class was strong in every aspect of their schooling, including academics, athletics and extracurricular activities.

glosses: The plural form of instruction; more than one (kind of) instruction.

examples.text: If you do not follow the instructions carefully you will make a mistake.
I'll never figure out how to build this shelf--the instructions aren't in English!

glosses: An instruction is a command or a step that helps you achieve a goal.

examples.text: Before he died, he gave the hospital instructions about how to deal with his body.

glosses: The instructions that come with a new machine, computer, or product tell you how to use the product.

examples.text: I couldn't figure out how to set the temperature in the fridge, so I read the instructions.

glosses: When you assign a job to someone, you tell them to do it.

examples.text: That teacher always assigns too much homework.

glosses: To attribute or sort something into categories.

examples.text: No firm dates can be assigned to this emperor's life.

glosses: A fee is the money you pay for some kinds of services, such as legal advice, education, or club membership.

examples.text: School fees have increased again this year.

glosses: An inheritable estate in land held of a feudal lord in return for certain services.

examples.text: He held his lands in fee of the Earl of Chester.

glosses: A computer is a machine that helps you store, organize, and use information.

examples.text: If you're looking at a web page, you must be using a computer.

glosses: A computer is a person whose job is doing computations.
If two things are similar, they are almost the same, or the same in many, but not all, ways.

examples.text: Canadian English is similar to American English, but there are some small differences in pronunciation, and spelling.
My sister and I have very similar ideas.

glosses: If two shapes are similar, they have the same shape, but might be different sizes.

examples.text: These two triangles are similar because they have the same angles, but they are not congruent because one is bigger than the other.

glosses: A definition is an explanation of the meaning of a word.

examples.text: The sentence before this one is a definition.
ESL students often check definitions in their dictionaries.
Can you give me a definition for "imprisonment"?

glosses: If someone is relaxed, they feel calm, they are not worried, and their muscles are not tight.

examples.text: I feel most relaxed when I'm fishing.
I really enjoy talking to her. She's always so relaxed and she has time to listen.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of relax.
A style is a specific look, design, or way of dressing or acting.

examples.text: I don't understand why the styles in fashion magazines are always changing.
We have a new manager, but her style is much more friendly than the old guy.

glosses: A style is a traditional or legal term referring to a person who holds a title or post.

examples.text: He styled himself the Count of Monte Cristo.

glosses: If you style something, you design and make it appear in a certain way.
If you require something, you need it.

examples.text: The job requires high level of math skills.
The new system will make the information available where it is required.

glosses: If you are required to do something, you have to do it.

examples.text: All men over the age of 21 are required to report to the army for service.

glosses: The structure of something is the way that it is put together.

examples.text: The structure of her writing makes it very easy to understand.
The social structure of a class is often very complex.

glosses: A structure is something that has been built or put together, especially something big, such as a building.

examples.text: The CN tower is the tallest structure in Toronto.

glosses: If you structure something in a particular way, you organise or build it that way.

examples.text: Prepare a list of questions to structure the interview.

glosses: Technology is the tools, equipment, and activities that come from scientific knowledge.

examples.text: Modern technology such as computers, robots, and wireless communications, can reduce the cost of doing business. (can make the cost smaller.)
The 1800s saw a gradual development (growth in small steps) of new technologies in farming and transportation.

glosses: A person who helps people who are sick, and looks after their health.
A person who can work very well about a particular thing and is given the title Doctor by a university, for example a doctor in psychology could be called Doctor John Smith.
If you doctor someone, you act as a medical doctor towards them.
If you doctor something or someone, you change them.
A grade is a letter or number that you use to show how good something is. Usually, teachers use it to show how good a student's test or assignment is.

examples.text: He got 97% on his test. It was the top grade in the class.
Our restaurant uses only the highest grade of meat.

glosses: In North American English, a grade is the school year.

examples.text: Most Canadian children start grade one when they are six years old and finish grade 12 when they are 18.

glosses: If you grade something, you judge how good it is.

examples.text: After the final exam, the teacher spent the whole weekend grading papers.
My friends goes to the farm to grade animals that are going to be sold.

glosses: A resource is something that is available and useful.

examples.text: We don't have enough time and resources to finish the job.
Canada has fewer natural resources, including trees, fish, and oil, than it did in the past.

glosses: If you resource something, you source it again.
A migration is a large movement, usually of people or animals, to a new living place.

examples.text: Every fall, the birds begin their migration from the cold northern areas to the southern regions where they will spend the winter.

glosses: Transport refers to how things are moved, or a system of transportation.

examples.text: I prefer my own means of transport.

glosses: A transport is a vehicle or vessel used to move things or people.

examples.text: On Tatooine, C-3PO thought he saw a transport in the distance.

glosses: If you transport something, you carry it from one place to another, usually on a truck, boat, or other large vehicle.

examples.text: One of the most important parts of doing business is transporting your materials from the factory to the shop.

glosses: Transportation is the system or vehicles used to move people or things from one place to another.

examples.text: In most of Canada, the main form of transportation is the family car.
The public transportation system in Tokyo is a mixture of busses and above- and below-ground trains.
The company is trying to reduce transportation costs by sending more goods by boat rather than airplane.

glosses: A community is a group of people living in the same area and having a similar background or similar interests.

examples.text: Most Libyan policemen were members of the community where they worked.
Within the business community, most people believe that taxes are too high.

glosses: If something varies, it is not always the same.

examples.text: The summer temperature in Toronto can vary from 12 degrees at night to over 30 degrees during the day.
"Do you enjoy your job?" "You know, it varies. Some days are good..."
Teachers sometimes need to vary the order and manner in which things are taught and learnt.

glosses: Your equipment is the things that you use to do a job or sport.

examples.text: Soccer is a popular game because you need very little equipment to play--just a ball and an open space.
The soldiers had to carry all their equipment on their backs.
The computer equipment was old and often broke down.

glosses: If you create something, you make or invent it. Usually, it's something that nobody has made before.

examples.text: Wiktionary editors create Wiktionary entries.
Initially, the company will create 200 new jobs, rising to 520 over the next few years.
A lot of problems have been created by the new government.

glosses: If an activity is legal it does not break any laws.

examples.text: In Canada, it is perfectly legal for a woman to walk down the street with no shirt on.

glosses: A legal problem, action, fee, etc. is related to the law or lawyers.

examples.text: After losing the court case, he had to pay over $30,000 in legal fees.
The government brought legal action against three cigarette makers.

glosses: A job is an activity that you do, usually, regularly and for pay.

examples.text: She got a good job as a manager in a book store.
She does the same job as George, and she does it faster and better.
Son, come here. I have a job for you before you start watching TV.

glosses: A job is a task that a computer performs.
A job is a plastic surgery that is done on someone. Usually used with another word to form a noun.

examples.text: John just had a nose job.

glosses: If something finally happens, it means there was a long wait before it happened.

examples.text: I finally finished university. Now, I can start my real life.

glosses: Finally is used, often at the beginning of a sentence, to show that this is the last thing or idea.

examples.text: First, I think that we should use less. Second, I think we should reuse the things that we have. And, finally, I think we should recycle more.

glosses: Technical problems, writing, or skills, are related to special knowledge that most people don't have.

examples.text: Doctors use a lot of technical vocabulary. I wish they would explain things more easily.
Our computers had some kind of technical problem, so we had to call somebody to come and fix it.
A prima ballerina must have great technical knowledge of dance movement.

glosses: Aid is the help that is given to people, usually by a government or institution.

examples.text: After the flood the UN sent $500 million of aid in the form of food, water, tents, and medical supplies.

glosses: An aid is a person or thing that helps you do an activity.

examples.text: The president's aid spoke to the newspapers today.
I can't see, but I have a number of aids, such as a cane, a dog, and a talking computer, that make my life easier.

glosses: If you aid someone, you help them.
If you do something formally, you do it in a formal way.

examples.text: They expect you to formally behave yourself. If not, I doubt you will get the job.

glosses: If you grant something to something, you give it to them, usually formally.

examples.text: The school has granted us permission to use a classroom in the evenings.

glosses: If you grant something, you accept that it is true.

examples.text: Yes, I'll grant you that the data is old, but I still think it's useful.

glosses: A grant is something, usually money, that is given to someone, usually by a government or institution.

examples.text: The professor received a research grant to study weather changes.
I got a $2,000 government grant to help me go to school.

glosses: Milk is a white liquid some animals make for their babies to drink. People often drink cow's milk.

examples.text: The boy had some fresh goat milk.

glosses: If you milk an animal like a cow or a goat, you take the milk out of it.
If something is warm, it is a nice temperature between cool and hot.

examples.text: It's good to come into a nice warm house on a winter's day.
She washed her face in the warm water.

glosses: If you warm something, you increase the temperature.

examples.text: At 7:30, the sun came up and warmed them a little.
Oh, the coffee's cold. Can you warm it up for me?

glosses: If you do something during something else, you do it at the same time.

examples.text: He often reads during dinner.
I'm always tired because I work during the night.

glosses: If something is cool, its temperature is between warm and cold.

examples.text: It's hard to keep the house nice and cool on a hot summer's day.
The air was cool, so he put on his jacket.

glosses: If you say something is cool you mean it is good and you like it.

examples.text: That's a really cool cell phone! Where did you get it?
Wow, your computer looks cool!

glosses: Someone who is cool is admired by others, someone of notably high social status.

examples.text: Jeffrey is the coolest guy in town.

glosses: If you cool something, you decrease the temperature.

examples.text: Blow on the coffee to cool it off.

glosses: If something cools, its temperature decreases.

examples.text: The soup was too hot, so he waited for it to cool a little.

glosses: If you talk about the health of a person or animal, you are talking about whether they are sick or not.

examples.text: The doctors believe that the disease will not be a serious danger to public health.
Before you start exercising, you should be in good health.

glosses: If you have health you are not sick (do not have disease) and are not hurt.
The temperature of something is how hot or cold it is.

examples.text: Today's temperature is 25°C.

glosses: An ocean is a large area of salt water.

examples.text: My great grandfather came across the Atlantic ocean from Scotland to Canada in 1882 on a sailing ship.
She stood on a beach in Japan and looked east at the sun coming up over the Pacific ocean.

glosses: Damaged means hurt or broken.
If A owes damages to B, A has to pay money because A hurt B or B's property.

examples.text: The reason his car hit another car was that he did something wrong, so he had to pay damages to the owner of the other car.

glosses: Damages means to hurt or break.

examples.text: All those cigarettes have damaged her health.
The factory has caused significant damage to the local environment.

glosses: A flood happens when there has been a lot of rain in a short time and the water covers the ground.

examples.text: The storm brought heavy rains, and the resulting flood caused $14 million in damage to crops.

glosses: If a place is flooded, the water covers the ground and often causes a lot of damage.

examples.text: In 2005, a hurricane brought so much rain that much of Louisiana was flooded, killing many people, and destroying large parts of the city.

glosses: To flood means to overwhelm.

examples.text: The market has been flooded with boy band recordings.
Stop flooding the editorial office with your complaints.

glosses: A storm is bad weather with high winds that disturbs the atmosphere.

examples.text: Small boats should stay off the water tonight because we are expecting a storm.

glosses: If you storm, you move fast and noisily like a storm, usually when angered.
If you storm a building or other fortification, you assault it with military troops.

examples.text: The sergeant and his platoon stormed the stronghold of the most wanted terrorist.

glosses: When something moves slowly or does something slowly, it takes a very long time to do it.

examples.text: She was very tired, and walked slowly up the stairs to bed.
He moved slowly, hoping that the bird wouldn't notice him.

glosses: If something is probably true, or will probably happen, it means there is a high chance of it.

examples.text: I'm not sure what I'm doing tonight, but I'll probably stay home and study.
"Is Ed here?" "Uh... he usually leaves at 4:00, so he's probably gone, but I'll go and have a look."

glosses: A subject is a branch of knowledge in school, college or university, such as English, math, science, and history.

examples.text: The subject of the class is English literature.

glosses: In English grammar, the subject of a sentence is usually a noun that comes before the verb. This noun is usually the thing that is doing the action, and it is usually the topic of the sentence.

examples.text: In the sentence, "Tom gave the box to Wilma", Tom is the subject.

glosses: A subject is a person who is governed by a king, queen, emperor, etc.
If someone or something is subject to something, they are likely to be affected by it or experience it.

examples.text: Home prices are even more subject to change than gas prices.

glosses: To make someone do something unpleasant

examples.text: They were subjected to intense labor.

glosses: You use her instead of the name of a person, to talk about a woman or girl. (used in the object position, never as a subject)

examples.text: This is Susan's book. Give it to her.

glosses: If you say something is her thing, you mean it belongs to a particular woman or girl.

examples.text: It is her book, not mine,

glosses: An object is a thing that you can touch, but it is not alive.

examples.text: We don't know what killed him, but it was a smooth, heavy object.

glosses: The object of an action or plan is the goal or the reason for it.

examples.text: The object of soccer is to kick the ball into the other team's net.

glosses: The object is a type of complement in a verb phrase or preposition phrase with the form of a noun phrase.

examples.text: In the sentence Yoko ate the bread, the bread is the object.

glosses: If you object to something, you don't agree with it.

examples.text: Most people will object to being asked to work too much.

glosses: If something happens suddenly, it happens very quickly when you don't expect it to happen.

examples.text: My son had been sitting in the chair beside me. Then, suddenly, I realised he was gone.

glosses: Your lungs are part of your body that is inside your chest. Your lungs allow you to breathe.

examples.text: Smoking for many years had damaged his lungs.

glosses: If you feel tired, you have no energy and you need a rest.

examples.text: After walking for 15 km, I was so tired, that I couldn't take another step.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of tire.
If something is electric, it uses electricity.

examples.text: My grandmother wrote her letters on a typewriter; my mother used an electric typewriter, and I use a computer.
We bought a new gas stove. It's much faster than our old electric one.

glosses: If something is in balance, it has equal amounts all around.

examples.text: She was walking on a thin line, but lost her balance and fell down.
This plan has a good balance of new and old ideas.

glosses: The balance in your bank account is the amount of money you have in the account.
A type of scale where there are two parts.
If you balance something, you make it have equal amounts all around.

examples.text: The bird balanced easily on the wire for a few moments before flying off.
A good manager has to balance the costs and benefits of doing business.

glosses: If something is wet it has some water or other liquid on it.

examples.text: I got completely wet in the rain.
I don't want to use this towel. It's already wet.

glosses: If a female is wet, she is sexually aroused and the vulva is moistened with vaginal secretions.
If you wet something, you put water or some other liquid on it.

examples.text: Please try not to wet the bathroom floor when you have a shower.

glosses: If you prefer something, you like it more than another thing.

examples.text: Sometimes I eat in restaurants, but I prefer to cook.
I generally prefer coffee to tea. I just can't enjoy tea.

glosses: If something is typical, it is normal, and not special. It's what you would expect.

examples.text: This rain isn't typical. We almost never get rain at this time of year.
These problems are just another typical example of how politicians only care about themselves.

glosses: Your brain is the part of your body that is inside your head.

examples.text: The brain is the part of the body that thinks and controls the rest of the body through the nervous system.
He has serious brain damage from falling off of his bicycle and hitting his head.

glosses: If a person, animal, or plant is sick, it has a disease and is not healthy.

examples.text: I'm sorry, I'm too sick to go to work today.
If you're sick, you should go and see a doctor.

glosses: A way of saying something is bad. (Could mean one or both of the following.)
If something is sick it makes you feel like vomiting. Usually this is not literal, but just means very bad.

examples.text: Oh sick! There is dog shit all over everything.

glosses: A way of saying something is bad. (Could mean one or both of the following.)
Sick can mean similar to person who is mentally ill (crazy), as an insult. This can also mean something bad that a crazy person might do.

examples.text: Killing children is just plain sick.
That guy is really sick in the head.

glosses: You say this about something that is cool. That is, something you like or see as very good.

examples.text: That song is sick!

glosses: The plural form of foot; more than one (kind of) foot.

examples.text: Please take your shoes and socks off of your feet.
My feet hurt from walking all day.
My friend is six feet tall.

glosses: The comparative form of bad; more bad.

examples.text: It is worse to lie to hide something than it is to lie to protect someone.
The weather this winter is worse than last year.

glosses: A park is an outdoor area where people can relax and play.

examples.text: We sat under the trees and had lunch in Central Park.
Algonquin Provincial Park is the oldest, largest park in Ontario, covering about 7,725 square kilometres.
I'm going to take the kids to the park to play on the swings.

glosses: If you park a car or other vehicle, you drive it to a place and let it stand there.

examples.text: She never parks her car under a tree.

glosses: Your breath is the air that you move into and out of your lungs.

examples.text: After running for just a minute, his breath was coming quickly.

glosses: A breath is the air that you move into and out of your lungs one time.

examples.text: Take a big breath and put your face in the water.

glosses: If something is global it includes the whole world.

examples.text: The weather is changing, and this is not just in one or two places. The change is global.
The Olympics and the world cup of soccer are the two largest global sporting events.

glosses: A period is a length of time.

examples.text: There was a short period when my computer stopped working.
During the first period, Germany scored two goals.
The dinosaurs lived from late in the Triassic period (about 225 million years ago) until the end of the Cretaceous (about 65 million years ago).

glosses: A period is the dot that marks the end of most sentences in English. This -> . is a period.

examples.text: Should I use an exclamation mark or a period at the end of this sentence?

glosses: A woman's period is the time each month when she passes blood.

examples.text: I have missed two periods now. I think I must be pregnant.

glosses: And nothing else; and nothing less; used for emphasis.

examples.text: When I say "eat your dinner," it means "eat your dinner", period!

glosses: A region is an area of land or of the body.

examples.text: The fishing problems have been happening only in the Atlantic coast region.
The southern regions of Japan are warm and tropical.
If we do an operation in this region of the brain, you may lose your ability to speak.

glosses: A region is any connected part of a space or surface. This definition is useful in geometry.

examples.text: In Euclidean space, a convex set is a region which has a geometric definition.

glosses: An area is a piece of land or space.

examples.text: This is the business area of town.
We have chosen a large forest area for the new park.

glosses: An area of study is a special subject, such as mathematics, grammar, music, or biology.

examples.text: Economics is quite interesting, but my area is more related to politics.

glosses: The area of a surface, is the size of the surface.

examples.text: The length is 10 cm and the width is 5 cm, so the area is 50 cm².

glosses: The plural form of man; more than one (kind of) man.
Contrasts are the differences you find when you compare something or someone.

examples.text: When comparing English and Japanese, there are many contrasts but also a large number of similarities.
Married life is a sharp contrast to the life of a single person.

glosses: If you contrast two things, you look for or explain the differences between them.

examples.text: It's difficult not to contrast the good things he says with the terrible way he acts.

glosses: Research is the process or result of trying to find an answer by reading, interviewing, watching, or doing experiments.

glosses: If you research a question, you try to find an answer, usually by reading a lot about it, or by doing experiments.

examples.text: I have to research the history of King Henry II for my English class.

glosses: If someone has depression, they have a condition which makes them very sad and makes it very hard for them to imagine being happy later.

examples.text: After Suzie's dog passed away, she fell into a depression for six months.

glosses: A depression is when the economy slows down by a lot.

glosses: If x affects y, then x causes a change in y.

Sigmund Freud's ideas were affected by the writings of Frederick Nietzsche.

examples.text: That music could be D minor or F major.

glosses: A major is a subject area that is the main study of a student at a college or university.

examples.text: My mother majored in English but I will major in psychology.

examples.text: Cindy was my boyhood crush.

glosses: You use me instead of your name, to refer to yourself.

examples.text: This is my book. It belongs to me.

examples.text: If I can help further please do not hesitate to contact me at 012-345-6789.

examples.text: Do you think we should fry the eggs or boil them?

glosses: Fried food is food that has been cooked in a pan with hot oil.

examples.text: I don't like fried chicken. It's too oily.

Marjorie has a habit of buying Christmas presents early, hiding them away like a squirrel, and then forgetting all about them.

examples.text: The monk's habit was black.

examples.text: Some corals grow with a branching habit.

examples.text: The rocks in this area are rich in minerals.

glosses: If something is convenient, you can get it or use it quickly and easily.

This is the most convenient route to take.

examples.text: Please close the door quickly. You'll let the cat out.
I hope the train gets here quickly. I'm late already.

glosses: A sauce is a thick liquid that you put on food to give it a special taste.

glosses: Rice is a white or brown grain that people boil and eat.

examples.text: Most North Americans get their grains from bread and pasta.

glosses: A grain is any very small piece of something, such as sand, salt, sugar, etc.

examples.text: One grain of salt is almost too small to see.

glosses: If you wait for someone or something, you do something (or nothing) until something else happens.

examples.text: I waited for you for twenty minutes. Where were you?

The form of a word that normally refers to other than one thing.

examples.text: The plural of the word "dog" is "dogs."

glosses: If a noun is singular in English grammar, it usually refers to only one thing.

examples.text: If I say, "one cat", that's singular, but if I say, "a lot of cats", that's plural.

examples.text: The singular appearance of the man caught his attention.

glosses: The plural form of lung; more than one (kind of) lung.

examples.text: Smoking for many years had damaged his lungs.

glosses: A bread and butter issue, is a basic and important one.

examples.text: If we want to win this election, we need to focus on bread and butter issues like jobs.

examples.text: Fixing shoes used to be our bread and butter, but today, nobody gets their shoes fixed.

glosses: If you butter something, you put butter on it.

examples.text: Would you like me to butter your toast for you?

glosses: A wolf is a wild animal, similar to a dog.

glosses: A chain of stores is a group of stores that all have the same name, such as McDonald's restaurants or GAP clothing stores.
If you chain things together, you connect them in a line.
If you chain A to B, you connect A to B with a chain.

examples.text: The dog was chained to the tree.

glosses: Amusement is the feeling you have when something is fun or funny or makes you laugh.

examples.text: Movies, video games and toys are amusements.
An amusement park has games, special food, and rides like a roller coaster and a merry-go-round.
Movie theaters, arcade and restaurants are good places for amusement.

glosses: An attraction is a force that pulls two things together.

examples.text: Magnets have an attraction to metal.
I feel a strong attraction to my husband.
I don't understand your attraction to rough men.

glosses: An attraction is a popular feature at an event or site.

examples.text: Elephants and lions are major attractions at many zoos.
Country western singer Vince Gill was a big attraction at the State Fair.
The Alamo is a tourist attraction in Texas.

examples.text: she has romantic ideas about sexual attraction

glosses: An offer is when you say you will do something or give something.

If I offer to do something for you, that means I will do it for you if you want.

glosses: House is a type of music.
If you house someone or something, you give them a home.

During the storm they were housed in the local school's gym.

glosses: When more than 2 things or people are together, they make a group.

glosses: To put people or things together to make a group.

A group of tools or instruments.

glosses: A problem.
A group of buildings with a common purpose, such as a university or military base.
A psychologically-based dislike or fear of a particular thing.

examples.text: Jim has a complex about working for a woman boss.

glosses: Cream is a soft white colour
A cream is a smooth oily substance that people put on their skin to make it soft or as a medicine.

To cream something is to make it turn into a cream-like color.

examples.text: The final score was 11-2, we creamed them!

examples.text: The restaurant had to close because there weren't enough customers.

examples.text: Although the beans from a single coffee may be sold unblended, in many cases, after roasting, beans from several different origins are combined to balance flavor

examples.text: She's put on a lot of weight since she went to university.

examples.text: To get your fishing line down to the bottom of the lake, you must weight it.

examples.text: Water freezes at 0°C.

examples.text: We want to use wind as safe, clean, non-polluting energy.

The police searched the car for drugs, but it was clean.
Her driving record was clean.

examples.text: Why don't you get a clean piece of paper and start over.

examples.text: My sister is such a pig. We bought a bag of sweets and she ate them all in one day.

examples.text: Would you like soup or a salad before your meal?

glosses: Tea is a light brown or green drink that is very popular around the world.

examples.text: I'm late for school. I don't have time for breakfast today.
"What time do you usually eat breakfast?" "Oh, I don't know, usually about 6:30."

glosses: An item is a particular thing that is separate from other things.

examples.text: When the United States doesn't like what a country is doing, it sends in its army. For instance, Vietnam was a problem, America started a war.

examples.text: He's the best salesman on our team, but he's only one element in our success.

glosses: If two ore more things are identical, they are exactly the same.

examples.text: The teachers teach from identical textbooks, but the ways they teach are quite different.

glosses: A category is a group of people or things that are the same in some way.

examples.text: This test can detect small changes in the chemical composition of water.

glosses: A topic is a general idea that someone is speaking (reading, thinking, etc.) about at a specific time.

glosses: If wind, air, etc. blows, it moves.

I could see some grass where the snow had blown away.
Her gray hair blew across her face in the wind.
Last fall, a storm blew through this town tearing up trees.

examples.text: I can't believe it. You almost had it, but you blew it.

If a tire blows, it gets a hole, letting out its air quickly.

glosses: If something is blown out of proportion, it is exaggerated.

examples.text: The team was dealt a terrible blow when goalie Ryan Francis was killed.
The final blow came when his wife left.
To soften the blow, the government will send one-time payments to everyone involved.
The town suffered a severe blow when the car factory shut down.

glosses: A blow is an action of blowing.

examples.text: He gave a quick blow on the whistle.

examples.text: A 90° angle is called a right angle.

examples.text: Mother, I'm afraid, please hold my hand.

glosses: A hand is a group of things that fit in your hand, like playing cards.

examples.text: He had a good hand but he still lost. He is not good at poker.

glosses: If I hand you something, I give it to you.

examples.text: Please hand me that tool. I can't reach it.

glosses: A glove is a piece of clothing you wear on your hand to keep your hands warm or safe.

examples.text: Police officers often wear gloves when working in crime scenes to avoid destroying evidence.
John is wearing gloves today because it's -5°C.

glosses: A market is a place where many people come to buy and sell things.

examples.text: It's time to take the cows to the market.

glosses: The market is the stock market.

examples.text: The market rose Tuesday on good results from the banking sector.
Cable stocks have lost an estimated market value of $ 6 to $ 8 billion.

glosses: A market is a group of people or businesses that might buy goods or services.

examples.text: The government is trying to help farmers find a new market for their grain.
The financial and oil markets continued to react negatively to the news from the war.

glosses: A market is the total amount or value of a particular kind of goods or services bought or sold.

examples.text: The company already has a 54-percent share of the commercial jet market.

glosses: If you market something, you make it available for sale and you try to get people to buy it.

examples.text: Manufacturers who spend millions to develop new drugs heavily market their products.

glosses: A card is a small, often rectangular piece of paper or plastic, usually with information.

examples.text: The police stopped me and asked to see my identity card.
"I don't have any money with me, can I pay with my credit card?"
The soccer player got a red card and left the game.
We spent the afternoon playing card games.
I think we sent them a Christmas card last year.

glosses: If you card someone, you check their ID cards, usually to see if they are old enough to enter a place or drink alcohol.

examples.text: They have to card anybody who looks 30 or younger.

glosses: If something is beautiful, it is very good to look at it.

examples.text: Look at that beautiful bird!
This magazine always has a picture of a beautiful woman on the front.

glosses: A horse is a hoofed mammal. It walks on four (4) legs. People often ride on horses.

examples.text: The horse likes to eat oats.

glosses: Feathers are the things which cover birds.

examples.text: The bird was covered in feathers.

glosses: If something declines, it goes down in number, quality, slope, or value.

examples.text: The Australian dollar has declined 3% against the Euro.
The number of students studying foreign languages continues to decline.

glosses: If someone declines an offer, they do not accept it.

examples.text: We asked Josh to come with us to the restaurant, but he declined.

glosses: A decline happens when the number, quality, slope, or value of something goes down.

examples.text: There has been a 3% decline in the Australian dollar against the Euro.
Every year we see a larger decline in the number of students studying foreign languages.

glosses: A decline is a hill or line that goes down.

examples.text: The truck crashed after picking up too much speed on the decline.

glosses: A conversation is when two or more people are talking informally.

examples.text: I had a really interesting conversation at work about how to improve things.
She is very good at making conversation with people she meets.

glosses: A plate is a hard flat thing, especially round ones that we put food on.

examples.text: He ate everything on his plate.

glosses: If you plate food, you place the food on a plate.
If you plate A with B, you cover the surface of A with a thin coat of B.

examples.text: This ring is plated with a thin layer of gold.

glosses: A host is a person or animal who makes a place for others and usually provides food and drink.

examples.text: The host of the party was so busy, she didn't have time to eat.
Some insects lay their eggs in a living host, which is eaten when the eggs hatch.

glosses: If you host a party or event, you make a place for it and you help to organise it.

examples.text: Germany hosted the 2006 World Cup of Soccer.

glosses: A finger is a long thin part of your hand that bends. Most people have four fingers and one thumb on each hand.

examples.text: He only uses one finger on the keyboard.

If a sound is loud, you can hear it very easily. If it's very loud, it might hurt your ears.

examples.text: Can you turn down the music, please? It's too loud.

glosses: If a person is loud, they talk too much or too loudly.

examples.text: After he has a few beers he gets really loud.

glosses: If colours, clothes, or other things you see are loud, they have too many bright colours or patterns and they don't look good.

examples.text: Thomas Edison invented the electric light bulb.

glosses: A thumb is the part of your hand that looks like a short, fat finger. Most people have a thumb on each hand.

examples.text: In many countries, pointing your thumb up means, "good".

examples.text: Please, don't interrupt me when I'm thinking.

examples.text: Don't interrupt me when I'm speaking. It's rude.

examples.text: Don't listen to Joseph. He's a joke. Nobody pays any attention to him.

examples.text: Everyone joked about how bad his tennis was.

The coach joked that he would fire his whole team.

examples.text: "She's forty-three." "Forty-three?! You must be joking. She looks like she's sixteen."

examples.text: There is a contradiction in saying that she is a widow who never married.

examples.text: He says he should be paid for fixing it, but he's ignoring the fact that it wasn't broken.

examples.text: There was a significant drop in the price of gas today, causing drivers to line up at the pumps to fill up.

examples.text: Zidane is an expert at penalty kicks.
The company has hired an expert in computer systems.
Today we heard an expert witness explain the details of the DNA analysis.

glosses: An expert skier, teacher, player, etc. is very skillful or experienced.

examples.text: She's an expert skier, one of the fastest and most beautiful on the hill.
My dog has become quite expert at opening doors.

glosses: The plural form of medium; more than one (kind of) medium.

examples.text: The media have been too accepting of the government's arguments.
The Japanese media often ignores international news.

glosses: A medium is a way of communicating information or art.

examples.text: We have to use music, pictures and other media to sell the product.

glosses: If you communicate an idea, you make someone else understand your idea, usually by using words.

examples.text: Parents have to work hard to communicate better with their children.

glosses: Communication is the process of sending and receiving ideas between two or more people.

examples.text: Teachers must regularly practice their communication skills to make sure students understand them easily.

glosses: Communications are the ways of sending and receiving information.

examples.text: The army is setting up a new communications network to improve communication.
Each time he sent a communication to Bidault it was held up by d'Argenlieu.

glosses: Classical ideas or styles are those that were very common at a time in the past and sometimes continue into the present.

examples.text: Classical theories in physics can't explain certain observations, which has led scientists to come up with new theories.

glosses: If you achieve success or a goal, you have completed what you planned to do or have a good result.

examples.text: She achieved a grade of 98% in her English class.

glosses: Logic is a system of careful step by step thought or argument that tries to explain truth.

examples.text: It wasn't easy to see the logic of her plan.

glosses: A contract is a legal agreement to trade goods, services and/or property. It's usually written down.

examples.text: If you would just sign this contract, the car will be yours.

You must look over the contract before you sign it.

examples.text: As the wood dries out, it contracts.

glosses: If you contract someone to do a job, you enter into a contract with them.

examples.text: We've contracted a cleaning company to take care of the office.
When there's too much work, there are a number of small firms to which we will contract it out.

glosses: If you contract a disease, you become sick with it.

examples.text: It's hard to understand why people risk contracting sexually transmitted diseases.
He contracted the flu.

glosses: An atheist is a person who does not believe in a god or gods.

examples.text: We have to do more to protect the environment from pollution.

glosses: Your environment is the situation or area that you live, work, or spend time in, including the people, buildings, vehicles, etc.

examples.text: When we moved to the city, we found ourselves in a comepletely new social environment.
This course will prepare students for a career in a software engineering environment in industry or research.
The learning environment can have a large effect on your grades.

glosses: If you export something, you send it out of the country, usually for business purposes.

examples.text: Canada will export up to 450,000 barrels per day of crude oil to China.

glosses: Export is the act or business of exporting things.

examples.text: A shipment of computers is being loaded on the ship for export to Singapore.

glosses: An export is something that you send out of the country, usually for business purposes.

examples.text: Bananas are Ecuador's largest export.

glosses: If you source something, then you obtain or receive it.

Church sources said four people were injured and 100 to 200 were taken away by the police.
The paper comes primarily from British sources.
CO₂ is the main source of global warming.

examples.text: In today's test, we will be assessing your ability to write clearly.

examples.text: The government is suggesting a significant change in economic policy.
In at least one case there was a deliberate policy decision not to involve the police.
The policy at the movie theater said we should turn on phones off and be quiet, during the movie.

glosses: If X is derived from Y, X comes from Y in the way that one idea comes from another.

examples.text: He derived a lot of pleasure from teaching.

glosses: A factor is one of a number of things that causes a result.

examples.text: The main factor in the success of our program is our excellent teachers.

examples.text: 2 x 3 = 6; 2 and 3 are factors of 6.

glosses: If you factor a number, you find all of its factors.
A procedure is a particular way of doing something.

examples.text: Because police did not follow procedure, the criminal was set free.

glosses: An assessment of a person, idea, skill, process, etc. is a judgement or measurement of them.

examples.text: The results of your recent job assessment are excellent.
The buyers have to make their own assessment of the value.

glosses: If you assume something, you think or believe something without having enough information to know that it's true.

examples.text: Oh, hello. I assume you're the new student, are you?
If I saw a man dressed all in black, holding a gun, and walking toward me, I would assume that the man is really a dangerous guy and I would run away from him.
I saw your car in the garage, so I assumed you were at home.

glosses: If you assume a role of office, you take on a new position that has more power or responsibility.
A theory is an idea that tries to explain an observation.

examples.text: The new information showed that his theory about growth was incorrect.
Nobody has disproved Einstein's theory of general relativity.

glosses: A benefit is something good that comes from something else.

examples.text: It was her idea, but she received no benefit from the new program.
With the new job comes many new benefits, such as dental and medical insurance.

glosses: If you benefit from something, you get something good from it.

examples.text: My health has really benefited from all the exercise I'm getting.

glosses: Evidence is facts or observations that support an idea.

examples.text: The gun is evidence that professor Pickle killed Mr. Mustard.

The police are still seeking evidence to find out who the murderer is.

glosses: In a courtroom, evidence refers to anything that is shown to the judge that is related to the case during a trial.

examples.text: Something good must have happened to her, as evidenced by the smile on her face.

glosses: A thesaurus is a book which lists synonyms (different words which have the same meaning).

examples.text: A thesaurus usually groups together synonymous words such as schadenfreude and epicaricacy together under a single heading.

glosses: If something used to happen, it happened often in the past, but it does not happen now.

examples.text: I remember when we used to stop by the beach every Sunday.
She started the exercise program, which we didn't use to have.
We don't go there anymore, but we used to.

glosses: If something used to be true, it was true for a long time in the past, but it is not true now.

examples.text: They're bigger than they used to be.
How bad did it used to be?

glosses: If someone is used to something, they know it and do not find it surprising or difficult anymore.

examples.text: It's hard at first, but after a while you get used to it.
He isn't used to being around children.
We get so used to seeing this that we don't even notice anymore.

glosses: To has no meaning. It is used with a bare infinitival clause.

examples.text: It's important for you to understand.
She told them to be quiet.
You want me to do it, but I don't have to.
To finish quickly, we must work fast.
To continue like this would be foolish.
I don't know how to get there.
He got the keys to open the door.
It's too small to see.

He arrived only to find that everyone had gone home.

glosses: To shows where something goes, the goal of movement.

The train returned to the station.

They went to school together and played in the same soccer team.
A squad car took him to hospital where he died.
Many people came to me with suggestions.
I wonder why you keep going to sea when you know it's dangerous.

glosses: To shows the receivers of an action or object.

examples.text: The goods were sold to customers at the downtown store.

Right now it's ten minutes to four.

glosses: To shows how two things are connected.

glosses: To shows a belonging or relationship.

To whom does it belong?

I can't remember the password to this account?

examples.text: It feels good to me.
To their surprise, she got up and left.

examples.text: Since the printer is back online, you should be able to again print from it.

examples.text: I'm writing a new book.

glosses: A subject in school where you write stories and poems.

examples.text: She is taking a class in creative writing.

glosses: If A is above B, A is higher than or before B, but not touching B.

Only children aged 5 and above may enter.
That office is on the floor above.
Our blessings come from above.
The passage above is easy to understand.

examples.text: Please see the above discussion of the problem.

glosses: An option is a choice.

examples.text: He has the option to go to university or join the army.

glosses: If something is ordinary, it is normal and not special.

examples.text: Today is an ordinary day, just like the last 256.

glosses: If you establish something, you start it with the idea that it will last for a long time.

glosses: To put a stop to something.

examples.text: The movie ends after this scene.

glosses: The last one of a group. Or, the last part of a thing, the place where it stops.

examples.text: I tied a knot in the end of the rope.

examples.text: Labour won the election.

examples.text: He laboured over the food all afternoon to get ready for dinner.

examples.text: Over the summer a change occurred in my friend’s behaviour.

glosses: If something occurs to you, you suddenly think of it.

examples.text: It occurred to me that I was in trouble.

glosses: About or relating to the economy, business, money, etc.

examples.text: The reduction in unemployment and continued economic growth are good news for workers.

One interpretation of the poem "Cross" by Langston Hughes is that "Cross" symbolize the speaker's mixed race.
The hospital offers interpretation services between English and French, Spanish, and Punjabi.

examples.text: The theory is consistent with the data.
His behavior is consistent with his words.

glosses: Income is the money that you get from working.

glosses: Income is what you get for selling products you make or grow.

examples.text: He was installed as Chancellor of the University.

examples.text: I installed myself in my usual chair by the fire.

examples.text: I think freedom of speech should be a constitutional right for everyone because everyone should have right to speak out.

American has an elaborate system of constitutional checks and balances.

examples.text: He's nearly 80 and still takes a constitutional every morning.

examples.text: His stubborn constitution led him into a number of conflicts he could have avoided.

examples.text: The distribution of the new iPad was very fast because Apple had invested a lot on advertisement.

The test scores averaged 50% and had a normal distribution.

examples.text: I met Sylvia at a church function last week.

examples.text: Her heart stopped, but her brain continued to function.

examples.text: In this sentence, "sentence" functions as the subject.

Of course, millions of dollars in targeted advertising does tend to increase sales.

examples.text: My artwork tends towards the modern.

examples.text: The price of gold has tended upward for about three years.

Care is the act of helping someone, especially sick people, the very young or the very old.

We take the kids to child care during the week.

examples.text: You're going to need someone to take care of you when you get older.
We'll be taking real good care of you. I promise.

examples.text: The equation of women with maids and cooks must stop.

glosses: An impact is the act of one object hitting another.

The environmental impact of such increases in efficiency, however, depends on how you generate the power.

glosses: If something flows, it moves in a smooth and regular way.

glosses: A survey is a broad look at a topic or place.

glosses: A land survey involves photographing and measuring the land to make a map of it.

examples.text: Before building the train tunnel, extensive geological surveys were carried out on the British side of the Channel.

glosses: A survey paper/book is a general description of a topic, often introductory.
A survey is the act of reading a broad range of books and articles on a particular subject.
If you survey something, you look at it to try to see or understand the whole of it.
If you survey people about their thoughts or personal information, you ask a large number of people in a formal way, often using a questionnaire.
If you survey a place, you look at every part of it, often from a high spot.
If you survey books and articles, you read a large number on a particular topic.
A decision is a sudden thought, with purpose, before someone does something. After a person makes a decision, the person has knowledge about a thing the person will do.

examples.text: After much thought, the person made a decision to go to the meeting.
A person sees two roads. The person needs to go on one road or the other. The person makes a decision and goes on one of the roads.

glosses: A decision is the end of a process in a committee. After a committee makes a decision, a record in writing says the important thing.

examples.text: After much discussion, the committee made an important decision about insurance.

glosses: Beauty is the quality of being nice to look at.

examples.text: Beauty makes things attractive.
There is a beauty in the night sky that is hard to explain.

glosses: A beauty is something or someone that is good to look at.

examples.text: She is a beauty.

glosses: Chronology is the science of finding out what events came in what order

examples.text: Chronology can help historians find out why an old empire ended.

glosses: Chronology is text or graphics that show what events happened in what order

examples.text: The chronology at the back of the book shows the Kings and Queens of England.

glosses: A potential customer, benefit, problem, etc. is one that might happen in the future.

examples.text: Realistic goals can then be set to prevent potential problems from becoming actual ones.
To grow, a business must identify potential customers and their needs.

glosses: If x has potential for y, then it might change toward y or cause y.

examples.text: Technology has the potential for improvement as well as for harm.

glosses: If something has or shows potential, they will likely be very good in the future.
The potential is the difference in voltage between two points on an electrical circuit.
A cultural background, difference, identity etc. relates or belongs to a particular group of people.

examples.text: Teachers should think about the cultural background of their students.
The difference between the cities are both cultural and economic.

glosses: Cultural things are related to art, music, books, etc.

examples.text: The new art museum has become the cultural center of the town.

glosses: A wound is a cut in skin with pain and blood, a burn, or other similar mark on someone's body.

examples.text: I dropped a knife on my foot, but the wound was minor, so I didn't need to go to the hospital.

glosses: When you wound someone, you cause an injury (a wound) to the person.

examples.text: The sharp blade wounded the man.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of wind.

examples.text: He wound the rope around the post.

glosses: A wise person has much knowledge and makes good decisions.

examples.text: Say your question to the old woman, because she is wise and will tell you good ideas about things to do.

glosses: If you wise up, you get informed; you learn something.
A wire is a long, thin metal thing, mostly for the purpose of making a connection from electric power to a machine.

examples.text: A person cut the electric wire and all the machines in the building stopped.

glosses: To join a wire to something.

examples.text: They wired up all the machines in the building.

glosses: A wing is the long flat part of a bird, insect or other flying thing. It is used to fly.

examples.text: This bird can fly very high very quickly because the bird uses strong wings with many feathers.
He looked out the window of the plane and saw the sun shining on the wing.

glosses: A wing is part of a building, usually not the main part.
A wing is part of a political group.
To fly with wings.
If you wing it you do not have a plan—you are making up what you do while you do it.
Wind is the moving air.

examples.text: The wind blows so strongly now that a person's hair goes in the person's face.

glosses: If you wind something you wrap it around and make it tight.

examples.text: You need to wind the string around the stick.

glosses: If you wind a clock or watch you tighten a spring inside it. This is done by turning knob. The spring powers the clock or watch as it unwinds (stops being tight).
If something winds it twists around in different directions.

examples.text: The road winds for miles.

glosses: If something winds down, it runs out of power and gets slower. (Like a watch that is unwinding.)
How something winds up is how it becomes in the end or after something happens.

examples.text: I wound up lost after I made the wrong turn.

glosses: If something is wide, it is long from one side to the other side.

examples.text: This box is 30 cm long and 20 cm wide, but only 10 cm high.
It's a very wide river, but not very deep.
The road was built wide enough to fit four lanes of traffic.
He cast a wide net into the sea.

glosses: If there is a wide range, variety, or world, there is a lot of it.

examples.text: The store offers a wide range of products.
He has traveled to wide and varied places.
The news received wide coverage across all media platforms.
There is a wide variety of choices available.

glosses: If you give something or someone a wide berth, you avoid them by a lot.

examples.text: He gave the barking dog a wide berth.

glosses: If something is wide open, it is open to its full extent.

examples.text: She opened her eyes wide in surprise.
The door was pushed wide open.

glosses: If you are wide awake, you are completely awake and alert, often when you would prefer to be asleep.

examples.text: Despite the late hour, the children were wide awake and eager to open their presents.
After drinking three cups of coffee, I was wide awake all night.

glosses: If two things are wide apart, there is a lot of space between them.

examples.text: "It was this big," she said, spreading her hands as wide apart as she could.
He was a big man with dark eyes placed wide apart.
He spread his arms wide to embrace her.

glosses: If something goes wide of the target, it misses the target.

examples.text: The soccer ball went wide of the goal.
Her first shot was wide, but the second struck his shoulder.
He put it wide of the mark.

glosses: If the ball or a player is/plays/goes wide, they are near the sides of the field or court.

examples.text: He ran wide and got tackled near the sideline.

glosses: A whistle is a sound like music. A person makes a whistling sound by blowing air when the person's mouth is in a little circle.

examples.text: The whistle of the wind in trees was low and sad.

examples.text: When you are in danger, blow your whistle loudly and someone will run and help you.

glosses: To whistle is to make a whistling sound with one's mouth.

examples.text: A happy person is able to whistle and work at the same time.

glosses: A whip is a long, thin leather instrument. A person uses it, with very quick motion, to give pain. A person uses it on a horse or another person as punishment.

examples.text: When the horse sees the whip in the person's hand, the horse gets scared and runs far away.

glosses: A whip is a member of a political party who is in charge of enforcing the party's policies in votes.
If you whip something, you hit it with a whip.

examples.text: Jockeys whip horses to make them go faster.

glosses: If x happens while y happens, they happen at the same time.

examples.text: He fell asleep while sitting at his desk.

glosses: A while is a short time.

examples.text: After a while I will stop working and cook food for us.

glosses: If you while away the time, you spend it doing something not very productive.

examples.text: On Sundays, I like to while away the hours by reading.

examples.text: Now the weather is colder and the freezing level is lower than it was in the summer.

glosses: The snow level is like the freezing level. The snow level is a measure of how high up on a mountain snow or ice is able to be. Lower than the snow level, the mountain is warmer and no snow is there.

examples.text: In the summer, the snow level is near the top of this mountain.

glosses: A ventriloquist is a person who does a trick to make the person's voice seem to be coming from a different direction. The ventriloquist talks but does not move the mouth. People think the ventriloquist is not talking and they think a thing or an animal or a different person is talking.

examples.text: People laughed when the ventriloquist made a shoe talk to a hat.

glosses: A watch is a little clock on a person's arm near the person's hand, to measure time.

Will you walk me home?

glosses: A tail is a long, thin part on the back end of an animal.

examples.text: The dog wags his tail (moves his tail quickly from side to side) when he sees his friend.

glosses: If you tail someone, you follow them without them noticing; you observe them.

It was cheap, so it seemed like a deal.
Our son is at school near here, so that's another reason for not moving.

examples.text: She's very like her mother.
Japan is becoming more like the U.S.
They were dressed in like manner.

examples.text: When you have only a hammer, all things seem like nails.

examples.text: He hammered so hard that the building moved a little.

glosses: Receive or obtain.

glosses: If things are even, the top or surface of each is as high as the others.

examples.text: The top of the wall is even because the bricks are all the same size.

examples.text: 2, 4, 6 and 8 are even numbers. 1, 3, 5 and 7 are not even numbers; they are odd numbers.

examples.text: India was leading 2-1, but Australia evened the score in the last minute.

glosses: If you even a problem out, you solve it.

examples.text: I went down and evened it all out. Everyone's happy now.

glosses: A dress is a loose cloth covering a woman's body. The lower part is like a skirt. The top part is like a shirt.

glosses: To put clothes on something.

examples.text: I dressed my little sister for school this morning.

glosses: To put clothes on yourself.

examples.text: I just need to dress and then we can go.

examples.text: That cut looks really bad. Here, let me dress it

Cloth is a thin, flat material, often made from cotton or polyester.

examples.text: The person used a wet cloth to wash the table.

glosses: (In or to) what place or situation.

examples.text: Where do you live?
Where did the man go?
I wonder where they will take us to.

glosses: (In or to) the place or situation in which.

examples.text: The room where the people cook the food is not cold.

I'll go where you go.

This is where I live.
That's where you are wrong.
Stand over here where the light is good.
Sit where I can see you.
You'll be right here where you belong.
