glosses: An occupation is a hobby or something else that you do to pass the time.

examples.text: Her favorite occupation is reading.

glosses: About the citizens of a country, especially as opposed to the government, army, police, religion, etc.

examples.text: One of the most important civil rights is freedom of speech.
In the Civil War, the Red Army had blocked off the northern part of Ukraine from the hungry south.
The state is connected to civil society through aspects other than its role in administration
The government had run out of money to pay civil servants.
This comes under civil, rather than criminal, law.
The bridge would be one of the largest civil engineering projects in the country.

glosses: If someone is civil, they are polite but not friendly.

examples.text: Mum had been civil to me since the fight but something had gone between us.

glosses: Your status is your level, role, or situation in a group or society.

examples.text: Mike Hooper has retained his status as Liverpool's current No 1 goalkeeper.
With the change in employment status came changes in responsibilities and pay.
In many countries, the ability to speak English is a sign or high social status.

glosses: The status of something is its situation at a particular time.

examples.text: What is the status of the repairs?

glosses: A goal is something you want to do or be able to do.

examples.text: I want to go to university and this will help me achieve that goal.
Scientists' ultimate goal is a theory of everything.

glosses: A goal is a place that you want to be or that you are moving towards.

examples.text: Our goal is Paris.

glosses: A goal is the area where you want to put the ball in certain games such as soccer or hockey.

examples.text: It's unclear whether the regular keeper will start in goal.

glosses: A goal is scored when the ball enters the goal.

examples.text: They beat second-placed Cambridge 2-1 with Mutch scoring the winning goal in the 82nd minute.

glosses: A hypothesis is a guess about what will happen, usually in scientific experiments.

examples.text: We will test the hypothesis that the change will have no effect.
The results of the experiment support the hypothesis.

glosses: A guess with no evidence to support it.

examples.text: This idea is purely a hypothesis. It has not been proven

glosses: About a job such as doctor, lawyer, accountant, etc.

examples.text: The group offers free professional advice on legal matters and housing.
The government has established a new professional body to regulate doctors.

glosses: If someone is professional, they do their job seriously and with much skill.

examples.text: We employ friendly, professional staff who can offer the benefit of many years' experience.

glosses: If someone is professional, they are paid for their job, sport, art, etc.

examples.text: After playing amateur tennis for years, he turned professional at the age of 25.

glosses: A professional is a person who is paid for doing their job, sport, art, etc.

examples.text: More and more the Olympics are allowing professionals to compete.

glosses: A professional is a person who does a job such as doctor, lawyer, accountant, etc.

examples.text: Professionals often spend years and hundreds of thousands of dollars in school.

glosses: A professional is a person who is serious and skilled in their work.

examples.text: You should get him to fix your car. He's a real professional.

glosses: A series of events, meetings, experiments, etc. is several of them that happen one after the other and are related.

examples.text: Three weeks ago troops and helicopters launched a series of attacks on Kurds in the region.
There has been a series of changes at the newspaper that began with the new editor.
The school will be hosting a series of lectures relating to poverty.

glosses: A TV or Radio series is a number of programs usually with the same setting and characters.
A series is a sporting event in which many teams compete for a championship.

examples.text: Tonight is the final game of the Stanley Cup series.

glosses: If something is connected in series, electricity passes through each point before going to the next point.
within or inside

examples.text: Doctors had to operate to stop the internal bleeding.
Grammar is mostly concerned with the internal structure of words and sentences.
The company has been weakened by ongoing internal conflict.
The police are conducting an internal investigation after officers shot two people.
They've painted the internal walls but left the outside as it was.

glosses: If you retain something, you keep it.

examples.text: After the election, the government retained control of the lower house, but lost the upper house.
The company retains the right to change the price at any time.
They joined the group but still managed to retain their independence at the same time.

glosses: If you retain someone (usually a professional), you pay them to do a job.

examples.text: Since being charged by police, Black has retained a lawyer.
With better wages abroad it is becoming increasingly difficult to retain employees.

glosses: A sum is an amount of money, usually a large amount.

examples.text: The company had been spending large sums on publicity and advertising.
It allows the corporation to pay its workers a lump sum of up to £37,000 on leaving.

glosses: The sum is the total of adding or subtracting several numbers or amounts.

examples.text: The total output doesn't equal the sum of the inputs because the system is not 100% efficient.
The sum of the three numbers will always equal 10.

glosses: If you sum up, you conclude or bring together the main points.

examples.text: She sums up the situation by saying that the new family is never the same as the biological family.

glosses: A mechanism is the way something works

examples.text: This research should help us to understand the mechanisms of memory.
This agreement sets out detailed mechanisms for solving disagreement between the two countries.
These two features combine to create a new data retrieval mechanism.

glosses: A mechanism is one moving system within a larger, more complex machine or organism.

examples.text: The body has a control mechanism to bring down blood-sugar level when it begins to reach unhealthy peaks.

glosses: If you impose something on someone, you force it on them, even if they don't want it.

examples.text: Egypt has imposed travel restrictions which will make it harder to enter the country.
The law imposes a duty on all employers to provide safety training.

glosses: If you impose on someone, you ask or expect them to do something for you that is difficult or inconvenient.

examples.text: Could we impose on you to explain that again more slowly?
I'd like to visit her, but I don't want to impose.

glosses: If x happens despite y, it is surprising that x happens because y usually stops it.

examples.text: Despite their best efforts, the ministers have not been able to come to an agreement.
Despite all the problems, I think this project is a success.
We hope that there will soon be changes despite the fact that the leaders are still the same old people.

glosses: If you do something despite yourself, you didn't plan or want to do it.

examples.text: She hated him, but when he spoke she laughed despite herself.

glosses: A parameter is a boundary or a limit.

examples.text: The machine should run only within operational parameters; temperature, water flow, etc.
The federal government sets financial parameters within which local authorities will have to work.

glosses: An approximate number, length, time, etc. is close to the real one but may not be equal to it.

examples.text: "How many people are on the team?" "I'm not sure, but I can give you an approximate number."
If we knew when he left here, it might help us identify the approximate time of death.

glosses: be or become near a value, position, or characteristic.

examples.text: Computers are getting better at approximating human speech.
Women's salaries in the company have approximated to male salaries.

glosses: The principal thing is the main or most important one.

examples.text: Canada's principal trading partner is the USA.
Presumably most of us work for the same principal reason – in order to live.

glosses: In American English, a principal is the head of a school. (headmaster in British English)
The principal is the most important person in a business, or an artistic group such as a dancers.
Principal is the money that you borrow and must pay back. It does not include interest.
Something which stays on or near the surface of water or another liquid.
A buoyant used to help balance in water or another liquid.

examples.text: Attach the float and the weight to the fishing line, above the hook.

glosses: A nicely decorated vehicle, to show in a parade or pageant.

examples.text: That float covered in roses is very pretty.

glosses: When you float, it means that your density is lower than the density of the liquid you are in, which makes you be at the surface of the liquid.

examples.text: As I have a light body, I always float when I go swimming.

glosses: If you predict something, you say that it will happen before anyone observes it.

examples.text: It is still difficult to accurately predict the weather more than two days in advance.
As predicted by analysts, Toyota has increased the price of the Lexus LS400 by £3000 for 1993.
Darwin's theory predicts that animals will try to maximise the number of their children.

glosses: A summary is a short explanation of a longer idea, article, story, etc.

examples.text: In this short time, I can provide only a summary of the work we have done.
So, in summary, our research shows that exercise is most efficient in the late afternoon.
Two things are clear from this very brief summary of the content of the Convention.

glosses: done quickly and without following standard procedures
brief, and short; without details
If you undertake something, you take responsibility for doing it and you start to do it.

examples.text: He is in charge of this project and has undertaken this work largely single-handed since July.
After a common two years, some students undertake industrial or professional placement in their third year.
Britain has apparently undertaken to review its own aid to Vietnam.

glosses: A cycle is a number of regular things that happen again and again.

examples.text: Right now we are in an upward-moving part of the business cycle.
Although women's monthly cycles vary in length from person to person, the average length is about 28 days.
Most car engines have a 4-part cycle.

glosses: A cycle is a short way of saying bicycle or motorcycle.
If you cycle somewhere, you go there by bicycle or motorcycle.

examples.text: The rain was falling harder than ever as I cycled home down the Banbury Road.
It took me less than 7 minutes to cycle the whole trail.

glosses: If you cycle a machine, you run it through one cycle.

examples.text: The test will cycle the computer through ten start ups.

glosses: A conference is a large organised meeting to discuss a particular topic or area.

examples.text: FMBRA will be holding a conference on diet, health, and the food industry on 19 March in Barcelona.
Some of the world's top scientists attended an important conference in 1983, to study the effects of nuclear weapons.

glosses: A conference is a meeting.

examples.text: Contact the teacher or coach and ask for a private conference without your child's presence.

glosses: If you attribute x to y, you say that x is the creation or result of y.

examples.text: He attributes his success to the love of his parents.
The famous phrase is usually attributed to Winston Churchill, though some believe he never actually said it.

glosses: An attribute is a part, feature, or characteristic.

examples.text: A good sense of humour is an essential attribute for a doctor to have.

glosses: If something is annual, it happens every year.

examples.text: The 1992 Annual General Meeting was held at Bristol University, on Saturday April 11 and Sunday April 12.

glosses: An annual is a kind of plant that only lives for one year.
If something is obvious, it is easy to see it, think of it, or understand it.

examples.text: It is obvious that you can't spend a lot of money and save at the same time.
For obvious reasons, the people of Hong Kong have long been reluctant to speak their minds.
Jason & Maria were always together, and it was obvious to family and friends that they would be married some day.
There's an obvious crack in the wall of the house.

glosses: An implication is a result that may be expected or predicted.

examples.text: This change has big implications for health planners and for those caring for people with AIDS.
It seems a very technical matter, but it is one with important practical implications.
She said all that, and the implications was that she didn't want to go.

glosses: An implication is a meaning that can be understood but is not given directly.

examples.text: Even if you did not call me a liar, the implication is there.
When I say gold is a metal, I say by implication that gold must resemble any other metals.

glosses: An implication is when somebody appears to be involved in something, usually something bad or illegal.

examples.text: The implication of Judge Lyman in the affair of Green and young Hammond has raised many questions.

glosses: If something is apparent, it is easy to see, realise or understand.

examples.text: When she was nine, for no apparent reason, she began to dislike the classes.
They had found many useful ideas, some immediately apparent but others that took more time to think through.

glosses: appearing or seeming to be a certain way.

examples.text: The difference was more apparent than real.
The government's apparent lack of concern for the poor is very upsetting.

glosses: A commitment is a formal promise or agreement.

examples.text: Actually I can't come on Saturday, I have family commitments.
You don't have to make a firm commitment but we would like to know when you can probably start work.
Police management retain their commitment to improving community relations.
Both men have demonstrated their great commitment to Wales over the last nine months.

glosses: happening after sth else.

examples.text: When he came the first time, he was very quiet, but on subsequent visits, he was much more talkative.
The child began to walk early but subsequent development, such as speech, was unusually late.

glosses: If x is subsequent to y, x happens after y.

examples.text: The government called a press conference subsequent to the agreement.
Subsequent to her appearance on TV she received many bookings.

glosses: A line that is upright is called a vertical.

examples.text: Please draw a vertical that intersects the circle.

glosses: The fully upright position is the vertical.

examples.text: The builder used a string to make sure the frame was on the vertical.
When the plane lands all seats should be on the vertical.

glosses: Something that is standing straight is vertical. In a vertical direction means straight up or down.

examples.text: The radio mast was vertical on the horizon.
A vertical shaft went down to the mine.
Vertical stripes on a shirt make a person look thinner.

glosses: A debate is an exchange of ideas looking at different sides of an issue.

examples.text: We will explore this idea through an analysis of the public debate on marriage and divorce.
The government's spending programme is the subject of much heated debate.

glosses: If you debate something, you consider its positive and negative points, often by talking with other people in a formal situation such as government.

examples.text: The AHA had in fact been debating the issue of the future of the hospital for some years.
Few subjects are more hotly debated in curriculum committees.

glosses: A dimension is a part of a problem, issue, or situation.

examples.text: We need to consider some of the dimensions of the likely future needs for health care among older people.
The baby has added a new dimension to our lives.

glosses: A dimension is a direction of measurement in space time, usually width, depth, and height.

examples.text: The new viewer lets you examine the image in three dimensions.
The dimensions of the football pitch can actually vary quite considerably with the length being anywhere from 90 m to 120 m.

glosses: If you promote someone or something, you help it to get bigger, higher, or more popular.

examples.text: The environment provided by the school promotes the reading development of all students.
Remember too that sleepiness is promoted by a warm, quiet environment.

She became assistant manager and was then promoted to general manager within two years.
Antonym: demote
She's on tour promoting sales of her new book.

glosses: Output is what is produced by a worker, machine, computer, etc.

examples.text: We have increased our total output from 4,500 to 7,500 barrels per day of oil.
Of course, any problems with the program will affect the output.

glosses: If you output something, you produce it.
The past tense and past participle of output.
To be alive; to have life.

examples.text: He's not expected to live for more than a few months.

glosses: To have permanent residence somewhere.

examples.text: I live at 256 Oak Avenue.

glosses: To survive, to continue.

examples.text: Her memory lives in that song.

glosses: Having life; something alive.

examples.text: The post office will not ship live animals.

glosses: A live firearm or explosive is able to cause harm.

examples.text: The air force practices dropping live bombs on the uninhabited island.

glosses: Charged or energized with electricity, usually meaning that the item can cause an electric shock or electrocution if someone comes in contact with it.

examples.text: Use caution when working near live wires.

glosses: A live bet is a bet that can be raised by the person betting.

examples.text: Tommy's blind was live, so he was given the option to raise.

glosses: A live event is an event that happens in real time; direct.

examples.text: The concert was broadcast live by radio.

glosses: The solution of a mathematical equation.

examples.text: The result of 1 + 1 is 2.

glosses: The situation at the end of a process, its outcome.

examples.text: The result of losing the presents was that everyone was sad.
The result of the race was that Peter won.

glosses: If x results in y, it leads to or causes y.

examples.text: A lot of digging results in a deep hole.

glosses: If x results from y, it comes for or is caused by y.

examples.text: A deep hole resulted from all the digging.

glosses: A long and narrow piece of land between two places. Usually, cars drive on it, and it is often paved.

examples.text: The taxi is parked on the side of the road.
The road between the two villages is made of sand.

glosses: The path which one takes to reach a certain place.

examples.text: It is a long road to the top.
The road from Warsaw to Paris leads through half of Europe.

glosses: If you have access to something, you can use it, look at it, enter it, etc.

examples.text: As a student, you have access to all our facilities including the library and computers.
We will seek to provide greater access to personal records held by government.

glosses: If you access something, you get information from it, usually using a computer.

examples.text: The product enables multiple systems to access a single database.
Users of PCs can access images from the photo CDs using any CD-ROM input device.

glosses: Boyfriend normally describes a boy or a young man, who is in a love relationship with another person, when they aren't married yet.

examples.text: I didn't have a boyfriend, and I thought that it was because I was too fat.

glosses: Boyfriend can also simply mean a friend who is male.
A code is a set of rules or laws.

examples.text: Children usually learn their parents' moral code.
Section 244(1) (a) of the Canadian Criminal Code defines assault.

glosses: A code is a way of storing or sending information, often secretly or in a way that is readable by computers.

examples.text: Microsoft has also licensed Windows source code to companies such as Citrix Systems.
In World War II, mathematicians and scientists broke the enemy's secret code.

glosses: If something is coded, it is written or stored in a code.

examples.text: The completed questionnaires were coded by two people.
The wide variety of proteins in the cells are all coded for by the genes in the nucleus.

glosses: A girlfriend is a girl or young woman who is in a romantic relationship with another person.

examples.text: Jeremy had been having trouble with his girlfriend.
Koo Stark, a former girlfriend of the Duke of York, was being kept in hospital last night.

glosses: A girlfriend can be any friend who is female.
A phase is stage in a process.

examples.text: We will look at very basic ideas during the first phase of training.
As the war enters its final phase, the role of the UN will probably become more important.
Teenagers often go through a phase of being attracted to someone of the same sex.

glosses: If things are in phase, they are working, moving, or changing together.
If you phase something in, you introduce it step by step.

examples.text: Over the next few years, all farm support was slowly phased out.

glosses: If something happens prior to something else, it happens before it.

examples.text: In this recipe, most of the work is actually done prior to cooking.
Prior to 1917 most people had lived on private farms.

glosses: occurring before

examples.text: We learned that police had prior knowledge of the attack.
Few of these workers have any substantial prior experience in industry.

glosses: You use granted to say that you accept that something is true, often before you adding contrasting information.

examples.text: He's a good student and usually does well. Granted, he did fail that one test, but I think there were good reasons for that.
"You haven't been a very good father." "Granted."

glosses: You use granted that x, y to mean y is true because of x.

examples.text: Granted that he has done nothing wrong, he should be set free.

glosses: If you take something for granted, you believe it without really knowing or thinking about it.
The past tense and past participle of grant.
Stress is emotional pressure that makes you worry because things are not going well.

examples.text: Death is a time of great stress for family and friends.
Plants under stress from lack of water or disease are the most likely to attract problem insects.

glosses: Stress is physical pressure that gradually can cause things to break

examples.text: Sitting puts an unnatural stress on the back and shortens the neck.

glosses: Stress is extra attention or importance that you put on something.

examples.text: Psychology has put a lot of stress on the childhood roots of adult problems.

glosses: Stress is extra loudness that you use in a word or in music.

examples.text: Put more stress on the first syllable of the word.

glosses: If you stress something, you say that it is very important.

examples.text: I have repeatedly stressed the importance of hard work, but luck is also helpful.

glosses: If you stress a word, part of a word, or a note in music, you make it louder than other words or notes.
A resolution is a formal decision, often after a vote.

examples.text: The U.S. may be willing to support a Security Council resolution backing the return of inspectors to Iraq.

glosses: Resolution is the amount of detail that you can see in an image.

examples.text: This camera is cheaper, but, of course, the resolution is much lower.

glosses: A resolution is a solution to a disagreement or difficult situation.

examples.text: The school holds classes in nonviolent conflict resolution.

glosses: A resolution is a personal decision (not) to do something.

examples.text: My New Year's resolution was to quit smoking.

glosses: Resolution is the power to try even when things are difficult.

examples.text: Her resolution to be honest never weakened.

glosses: If something is adequate, it is good enough.

examples.text: It is very hard to provide a simple but adequate explanation.
She left her other job so that she could devote adequate time to the school.
A small knife is adequate for this purpose.
By 1922, the single school-room was no longer adequate to meet the needs of the town.

glosses: A tot is a very young or small child.
A total is the final amount of something. It is a term used in math.
If you total something, you add them up.
If something totals something, it adds up to that; it amounts to.

examples.text: The total of your purchase comes to $53.

glosses: If you total something, you destroy it; you wreck it.
If something is total, it is complete; it is finished.

examples.text: He is a total failure

glosses: If something is total, it is entire.

examples.text: The total book was very bad.

glosses: Whole is used to describe every part of an object.

examples.text: I ate the whole meal, leaving nothing left.

glosses: The whole of something means the entire part of it.

examples.text: The whole of the Middle East is pretty messy at the moment.

glosses: A half is 1/2 of a whole; 50%.

examples.text: Sales were down from January to June but jumped in the second half of the year.
Half a year later, the baby was born.
A half minute after the game started, the rain began.
It took us an hour and a half to get the bike working again.
The city was about half the size of Vancouver.
More than half the money came from the government.
It's cost us three and a half thousand dollars.
We'll meet at half past two.
It's two and a half times as big as the old one.
The coach changed the goal keeper at half time.
The same car might cost about half as much again as in Britain.
These cookies are not half as good as the ones your mum makes.
The apples are half price today.
When I phoned, he was still half asleep.
The glass was half full.
Since the early 1980s the army's strength and budget have been cut in half .
The car was half on the road when it was hit.

glosses: A half is one part of a game that is divided into two parts.

examples.text: At the end of the first half, Japan is leading Iran by two points.

glosses: A half is one end of a sports field.

examples.text: He kicked the ball deep into New England's half.

glosses: A half is a player who plays in the middle part of the field in sports like football, rugby, etc.
A veterinarian (sometimes shortened to vet) is a doctor that treats animals.

examples.text: The veterinarian treated the dog.

glosses: If you alter something, you change it, usually in a small way.

examples.text: The design can be easily altered by selecting new colours, materials, etc.
But not even a good cleaning would alter the fact that the room was dark and unfriendly.
Because he was so short, he always needed to have his pants altered to fit him.

glosses: Stability is the property of being firm and constant.

examples.text: Investors, especially foreign ones, want political stability to go with economic growth.
He may need handrails on either side for stability and safety.
People began to wonder and talk about the stability of the fairy-tale marriage.

glosses: Energy is the ability to do work: move, give off heat, give off light, etc.

examples.text: Unlike coal or oil, atomic energy production creates little air pollution.
Higher electricity prices should help promote energy efficiency.
The amount of energy in 100 g or 100 ml of food is much higher for foods with a lot of sugar.
She's all full of energy and she can't sit still.
This problem has taken up most of her time and energy for over a year.

glosses: If you are aware of something, you know about it.

examples.text: I am fully aware of the need for security, and will make the necessary changes.
I'm quite aware of the fact that you're here. You don't have to keep reminding me.

glosses: Providence is the careful management of resources.

examples.text: His providence in saving for his old age is a good example for everyone.

glosses: Providence is God.
Providence also means God's will, or a power that some people think to be controlling our lives and the things that happen to us.
A station is a place where many trains or buses stop and people buy tickets and get on.
A station is a place where a person stays in one place and works.
If you station someone, you place them to do a task.

A society is a large number of people and the way they live, talking together, working with each other and making rules and ways to live. A society can be a town, country or more than one country together, with many people living the same ways.
A society is an organization or club that people can join.
To sort is to divide one group of things into smaller groups of things, so that the things in one smaller group are the same as each other in some way.

examples.text: He sorted the apples, putting red apples in one basket and green apples in the other basket.

glosses: A sort is a kind or type.

examples.text: Red and green are two sorts of apple.

glosses: A small person or thing is not big. It doesn't have much size.

examples.text: A mouse is a small animal. A baby mouse is very small.

glosses: Something is slow if it takes a long time to move. It is not fast.

examples.text: A snail is a very slow animal. It moves slowly.

glosses: If something is slow, it does not happen in a short time.
If someone is slow, it takes them a while to understand something.
If you slow someone or something, he, she, or it does not move as quickly as he, she, or it did before; you lower the speed of something.
If you slow, you do not progress as quickly as you did before.
A slope is one side of a hill.

examples.text: We will have to climb up this slope to get to the top of the hill.

glosses: The slope of a line is how far up it goes divided by how far along it goes.
A slope is an extremely offensive word for an Asian.
If something slopes, it goes either up or down.

examples.text: The hill slopes down at this point.

glosses: A long thing is slanting when one end is higher up than the other end and also further along. To be on an angle or sloping.

examples.text: The piece of wood is slanting from the ground up to the door so that a cart with wheels can roll up it.

glosses: A slant is the way a long thing is when one end is higher up and further along than the other end. The way a ramp is.
Enforcement is the act of making people follow a law, rule, or decision.

examples.text: It is not a problem which can be solved by law enforcement alone.
There simply hasn't been enough enforcement of the rules during this tournament.

glosses: When something slides, or moves a small distance while touching what it's on, we say it slips.

examples.text: The hat slipped down until it covered her eyes.

glosses: When someone or something moves without wanting to move, we say it slips.

examples.text: My foot slipped when I stepped on some ice, and I almost fell.

glosses: When someone moves quickly and quietly so that other people won't see them move, we say the person slips.

examples.text: I slipped into the kitchen to start washing dishes while people were talking.

glosses: A slip is a small mistake.
A slip is a piece of clothing like a small white skirt, that a woman sometimes wears hidden under her skirt or dress.
A slip is a small piece of paper.
A draft is a piece of writing which has been or may be edited.

examples.text: In the first draft of the story the characters names are all different.
Check final drafts for misspellings, using a dictionary or computer spelling checker.

glosses: A draft is when the military or a sport team chooses its members.

examples.text: Many Americans moved to Canada to avoid the draft during the war.
The Tigers' first choice in yesterday's draft was pitcher George Berlin.

glosses: Depth of water needed to float a ship; depth below the water line to the bottom of a vessel's hull. (UK spelling: draught)

examples.text: The ship had a draft of 6 feet.

glosses: Draft is beer that is served from a large container called a keg. (UK spelling: draught)
A draft is a wind that blows inside a building. (UK spelling: draught)

examples.text: Close the window! That cold draft is making me sneeze.

glosses: If you draft a letter, memo, agreement, etc., you write one that has been or may be edited.

examples.text: You should have the contract drafted by a lawyer.

glosses: If a state drafts someone, it chooses them to be in the military.

examples.text: I was drafted when I was 20 and spent two years fighting in France.

glosses: If a team drafts someone, it chooses them to play on the team.
If something is precise it is correct and exact.

examples.text: Young children are often unable to give a precise definition for words they know very well.
The precise nature of the tax changes has not been decided.

glosses: If someone is precise they always act and speak very carefully.
The sky is what you see when you look up when you're not inside. It's blue with clouds in it. At night it's black with stars in it.

examples.text: The night sky was full of stars.

glosses: If you pursue a job or hobby, you do it for a long time.

examples.text: The band motivated her to pursue a career in music.

glosses: If you pursue someone or something, you try to reach, catch or get it.
If something is symbolic, it has or is used as a symbol.

examples.text: In many religions, the number 3 has a symbolic value.
The apology was purely symbolic and did nothing to change the situation.
It was dirty and dark in a way that was very symbolic of New York.

glosses: If something is marginal, it is not very large, important or central.

examples.text: But this discussion is marginal to the real issue.

glosses: (in finance) The marginal profit, tax rate, etc. is the percent earned or paid on one more unit of production or income.

examples.text: Large scale economies tend to mean that the marginal cost of serving an additional customer is either zero or very small.

glosses: If something is marginal, it is low quality, almost unacceptable.

examples.text: His writing is marginal at best. I don't think he'll pass.

glosses: If something is marginal, it is written in a margin.

examples.text: I can't read the marginal notes.

glosses: A strong soft material that cloth is made of. A certain type of silk worms make it.

examples.text: This shirt is made of silk.

glosses: A flat thing with a few words or pictures on it to tell people something.

examples.text: I saw a stop sign, so I stopped the car.

glosses: When someone signs a piece of paper, they write their signature on it.

examples.text: They signed a contract saying exactly who would do the work and how much money they would be paid.

glosses: If a company signs someone, they hire them to work.
A side is a straight edge of an object.

examples.text: A square has four sides.

glosses: A side is the left part or the right part of something.

examples.text: This car has only one door on each side.

glosses: A side is an area next to or near something else.

examples.text: The statue is on the east side of the school.

glosses: A side is one surface of a sheet of paper.

examples.text: Please write on both sides of the paper.

glosses: A side is one possible way of looking at or thinking about a concept (usually positive or negative).

examples.text: On the plus side, my car is fixed.
Try not to look at the down side of things.

glosses: A side is one team of players in a game.

examples.text: Which side is winning?

glosses: A side is country or a group of countries fighting together in a war.

examples.text: In the second world war, the Italians were on the side of the Germans.

glosses: (US) A side is a side dish of food that is not the main dish.

examples.text: Do you want a side of french fries with your hamburger?

glosses: (usually with "with") To side with someone is to be in an alliance with them.

examples.text: Who will you side with, Bob or Rachel?

glosses: The capacity of a container, room, etc. is how much it can hold.

examples.text: The capacity of the bottle is 500 ml.
The capacity of the hard drive is 120 GB.
I'm sorry, this pool only has a capacity of 100 people and I can't let any more in.
If you fill it to capacity, you won't be able to carry it.

glosses: The capacity of someone or something to do something is the ability to do it.

examples.text: I was impressed by his energy and capacity for hard work.
Since the head injury he has lost his capacity to learn new names.

glosses: The capacity of a factory or business is how much it can produce.

examples.text: It will soon be necessary to increase capacity at our Toronto plant to meet Canadian demand for the product.

glosses: If someone does something in a particular capacity, they are doing it in that role.

examples.text: I am not writing to you in my capacity as your doctor, but as a friend.
Sometimes I make decisions in my capacity as father that I don't like in my capacity as husband.
He's been hired in a temporary capacity.

glosses: If x has exposure to y, x is not hidden or protected from y.

examples.text: Staying out of the sun between 11am and 3pm can reduce exposure by 60 per cent.
Prolonged exposure to cold and wet may increase the chance of disease.
As a child of a Canadian father and Japanese mother, he had exposure to many different viewpoints.
The exposure of his crimes was the end of his career.
She had multiple exposures to the gas before becoming ill.
The campers died of exposure after two weeks in the cold.

glosses: The exposure is the amount of time that a film is hit by light.
One exposure is one section of film that is hit by light at one time.
If you modify something, you change it, often only in small ways, and often because you want to use it in a different situation.

examples.text: Both penalties and rewards can be used to modify children's behaviour.
It is also possible to modify the original by adding or removing parts.
We found some new problems and modified the program accordingly.

glosses: If a word, phrase, or clause modifies another, it is an optional word, phrase, or clause that gives more information about the other.

examples.text: The adjective "big" modifies the noun "bridge" in the expression "big bridge".

glosses: Something that is external is not on the inside.

examples.text: Both internal and external stairs need to be modified to allow wheelchairs into the building.
There are many influences upon the child external to life in school.
I wondered if there were any external pressures that led your husband to make the change.
Other sources of external debt arise where non-residents purchase local bonds.

glosses: If something is fundamental, it is basic and important.

examples.text: The loss of her legs has caused her to undergo a fundamental change in how she looks at life.
Respect is fundamental to a strong education system.
There is no more fundamental question than "why are we here?"

glosses: The fundamentals of something, are the main ideas or parts that it is built on.
A flash is a sudden bright light.

examples.text: He used the flash on his camera.

glosses: A flash is a very fast period of time.

examples.text: The tall man disappeared in a flash.

glosses: If something flashes, it shines brightly and suddenly.

examples.text: The fountain flashed in the sunshine.
It rained hard. Lightning flashed and we heard thunder.
The light from the car flashed through the window into the house for a second when the car drove past.

glosses:
:
 This short section needs someone to add to it.
A ratio is the comparison in size or number between two things. It is written x:y and read x to y. It is the same as the fraction x/y.

examples.text: The ratio of men's jobs to women's is 8 to 1.
But Germany now has one of the highest ratios of spending to GDP in the European Community.
The low student/teacher ratio makes this a great school.

glosses: When someone moves a door so that people can't go through it, the person is shutting the door. When someone puts their lips together so that no air or food can go in or out of their mouth, the person is shutting their mouth.

examples.text: The wind was too cold, so I shut the window.

glosses: Two shoes are two things that someone wears on their feet. Shoes have a hard, flat bottom.
If you shoe, you put shoes on your feet. We usually use this verb as a past participle: We say say someone is shod if they have shoes on their feet.

examples.text: He was dressed and shod, ready to go out.

glosses: If you shoe a horse, you put horseshoes on the horse.
To put protection on something so that it does not get worn down.

examples.text: Let's shoe that cane before you get a splinter in your hand!

glosses: A shock is the way it feels when a heavy thing suddenly hits another thing.
A shock is a sudden change that surprises people.
Shock is the way a person is when the person has lost some blood or has been hurt, and their heart is beating very fast and weakly.
A shock is a painful feeling that someone gets when electricity flows through their body.
A shock is a brief zap that someone gets after being in contact with static electricity.
Someone is shocked when they are surprised at something

examples.text: He was shocked at how much she had changed since he had last met her.

glosses: If someone has been shocked, they got a painful feeling due to electricity flowing through their body.
If someone has been shocked, they have gotten a brief zap due to contact with static electricity.
A shelf is a flat thing that people can put books or other things on when they are not using them.
Someone feels shame when they know they did something wrong.

examples.text: The boy felt shame and gave back the candy he had taken.

glosses: If you shame someone, you make them feel shame.
To shake is to move from side to side many times quickly.

examples.text: She shook the bottle to mix the drink.

glosses: A shake is a type of beverage.

examples.text: They were known for their shakes.

glosses: A shake is when something shakes.
A shade is a shadow of a tree or another big thing that blocks some of the light and heat of the Sun.

examples.text: She rested in the shade of the tree because she felt hot.

glosses: A shade is the slight difference between colors.
If something is shaded, it is shielded from light.

examples.text: The old tree shaded the animals from the sun.

glosses: If something is shading, it is approaching something slightly.

examples.text: The grassland was green, shading towards brown in the drier areas.

glosses: If you shade something in a drawing, you darken it.

examples.text: Mary started shading in the outlines of the house in her drawing.

glosses: When we say one thing versus another thing, it means the two things are on different sides, going in different directions, or against each other.

examples.text: Tonight's game has Toronto versus Montreal.
A lot of people see America as poor versus rich versus a middle class.
It's a simple story of good versus evil.
The difference between students with high versus low levels of English is growing every year.
We had to talk about how much time I spent doing homework versus how much time I spent playing games.
What do you think of going to a movie versus to a restaurant?

glosses: A terminal is the end of a train track or bus route. It is the station or the last stop.

examples.text: The bus drove into the terminal and all the people got off.

glosses: A computer screen and keyboard, which are at the end of a wire joining them to a computer.

examples.text: She sat at the computer terminal and typed some words.

glosses: A terminal is a building in an airport where passengers transfer to the facilities that allow them to board airplanes.
The last. At the end, in time or in space. A terminal illness is a sickness that will make the person die.
The takeoff is when an airplane moves from the ground into the air.

examples.text: Put on your seat belt to be ready for takeoff.

glosses: When an army stops fighting and lets the other side win, we say that the army surrenders. Sometimes people wave a white flag to show that they are surrendering.
To submit to a person who has more power.
A surrender is the act of surrendering.
You use whereas to show a contrast between two things or ideas.

examples.text: Many kinds of roses have little or no scent, whereas others are well known for their beautiful smell.
School A has about 25 percent Asian students, whereas for school B the Asian students make up over 60 percent of the school population.
Whereas only about a third of local residents paid full rates in the past, now most adults will pay the charge.

glosses: Because.
If you enable something or someone, you make make it able to do something or you help it.

examples.text: The program enables users to share data, collaborate and automate tasks without writing any extra code.
Night or instrument flying enabled us to fly twenty-four hours a day and in poor weather.
The data will not enable the identification of individuals to take place.
This switch will enable the song-sharing function.

glosses: A version is something that exists in different forms.

examples.text: Tomorrow, IBM is launching OS/2 2.0, the new version of its OS/2 operating software for personal computers.
The North American version of the car will have a larger engine.

glosses: A perspective is a way of looking at or thinking about something.

examples.text: The British media give a completely different perspective from CNN.
He has to look at everything from an international perspective.
The book provides a fresh perspective on the lives of young airmen during the war.

glosses: Perspective is the ability to think about things in a reasonable way.

examples.text: He's lost all perspective when it comes to this job.

glosses: Perspective is a way to show three dimensions in a two-dimensional image.
A network is a group of connections between a number of points.

examples.text: Electronic systems control the busiest parts of the rail network.
This is the first national TV network that is 100% sports.
We conduct much of our overseas banking business through a network of some 3,500 worldwide branches.
You can connect to the Internet through a wireless local network system.
I don't have a good social network in my new job.

glosses: If you network, you make or use social connections, usually for business purposes.

examples.text: I spent most of my time at the conferences networking with other sales people.

glosses: Someone's welfare is their health, safety, and other things the make them happy.

examples.text: Children need to exercise each day, for both their physical and psychological welfare.
This group has tried to promote the welfare of old people throughout the United Kingdom.
It is clear that the issues the environment and animal welfare have become very important recently.
Few countries have the same level of social welfare that we have in Canada.

glosses: Welfare is money paid by the government to poor people.

examples.text: The government is reviewing the welfare benefits which single parents receive.
He lost his job and his home and has had to go on welfare.

glosses: A transition is a change from one place or situation to another.

examples.text: Diana has made the transition from girl to woman.
The transition from ice to water occurs at 0°C.
They want at least a five-year transition period.

glosses: If something transitions, it changes from one place or situation to another.
An amendment is an addition or change to a document; also the process of making this change.

examples.text: This law can only be changed by constitutional amendment.
We are considering an amendment to the Water Bill which required compliance with EC rules by 1993.
He agreed to accept amendments to reduce the standard rate of income tax in his Finance Bill.

glosses: A hole or body of water is deep if it goes down a long way.

examples.text: Do not dive into this swimming pool because it is not deep enough.
Some oil wells must be drilled deeper than others to reach the oil.

glosses: Something is deep if it is far below or inside.

examples.text: The Earth's iron core is deep beneath its crust.
The Japanese style of poetry called haiku is simple on the surface, but it should also have a deeper emotional meaning.

glosses: A deep voice has low-pitched tones.

examples.text: In opera, the bass singer has the deepest voice.

glosses: With actions that make something smaller, we say deep to mean they make them much smaller.

examples.text: This furniture store offers deep discounts on beds.
The new budget makes deep spending cuts in education.

glosses: An idea is called deep if it has an important meaning that is not easy to see.

examples.text: A: 'I think you like heavy metal music because your parents don't approve of it.' B:'Wow, that's deep!'

glosses: If you reject an idea or belief, you decide that you do not believe it.

examples.text: We reject the idea that English is somehow "better" than other languages.
The court rejected his arguments that he should be set free.

glosses: If you reject a person, you refuse to care for that person.

examples.text: Often people who are infected with AIDS are rejected by family and friends.

glosses: If you reject an object, you refuse to take it or keep it.

examples.text: Consumers have the right to reject problem goods and demand a refund.

glosses: A reject is something that has been rejected.
A reject is a stupid person.
A clause is a section in a contract or other legal document.

examples.text: The author's contract contained a clause giving him creative control over the films.

glosses: A clause is a group of words that usually includes a subject and a predicate. In English, the subject usually comes before the predicate.

examples.text: The last clause in the sentence is hard to understand without knowing some background.

glosses: A predicate is the head of a clause and says something about the subject.
If you predicate something, you state or assert it.
If you predicate that something is true, you state that it is true.

examples.text: The article predicates that the market collapse was caused by weakness of the dollar.

glosses: If something is prime, it is best, most important, most suitable, or in some way number one.

examples.text: Canada is a prime example of a multicultural country.
He was the prime suspect in the murder investigation.

glosses: The prime is the best part of something.

examples.text: He was killed at the prime of his life.

glosses: A prime is a number that can be evenly divided only by one and itself.

examples.text: The first six primes are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, and 13.

glosses: A prime is something that primes something else.
If you prime something, you get it ready to do something.

examples.text: The coach has primed them for the game.

glosses: to manipulate, in a subtle manner, people's decision-making by use of symbols, location, etc.
An objective is something that you are trying to do.

examples.text: The main objective of our visit was to climb Mount Kenya.
I share the objective of everyone in Britain who want our soldiers home.
Sometimes a team is more successful than an individual in achieving challenging objectives.
We plan to extend the network with the objective of connecting up 3 million more homes by 1990.

glosses: An objective is a place you want to get to.
If something is objective, it is based on facts and things we can see and touch without using people's feelings.

examples.text: It is hard to find objective measures of artistic ability.
Newspapers try hard to publish objective stories.

glosses: If someone is objective, they are thinking about things logically based on facts.

examples.text: Watching the play on TV can help an actor to be more objective about his performance.

glosses: If something is sustainable, it can be continued for a long time, especially without using up resources.

examples.text: The oil-based lifestyle of today is not sustainable.
The government is trying to balance sustainable development with economic growth.

glosses: If two things are equivalent, they are of equal value or acceptability.

examples.text: Dolphins have very large brains, roughly equivalent to the size of a human brain.

glosses: An equivalent is something of equal value of acceptability.

examples.text: Living in Thailand costs the equivalent of just £10 per day.

glosses: If something is liberal, it allows for change, flexibility, and free thought.

examples.text: The Church should take a more liberal view of sex.
Japanese schools are quite different from what you see in our more liberal education system.
Any attempt to put a liberal democracy in Iraq will fail.

glosses: If something is liberal, it has few limits.

examples.text: He was quite liberal with his kindness.

glosses: A liberal is a person who believes in liberal ideas.
A notion is an idea about something.

examples.text: The film questions the standard notions of right and wrong.
We have to reject this strange notion that some languages are better than others.
I made my way home each night with at least some notion of hope.

glosses: A substitution is the act of replacing one person or thing with another.

examples.text: The accidental substitution of one medicine for another can be deadly.
They had no extra players, so were unable to make any substitutions.

glosses: If you generate something, you create it.

examples.text: On the hottest summer days, we are unable to generate enough electricity.
Apple is great at generating interest in their computers and other products.
They gave away 100 percent of the income generated by their songs.

glosses: Revenue is the money that a business receives for doing business, and government receives from taxes.

examples.text: Higher oil prices should raise government revenue by 13%.
Individual taxpayers today provide a bigger share of our tax revenues than they did before.
The company earned 20% of its revenues from services such as consulting, software and management.
The City is happy because a new source of revenue has been located.

glosses: A compound is a material made of a number of other materials.

examples.text: The new chemical compound has far less smell than the original substance.
There is a group of gases that do not easily form chemical compounds.

glosses: A compound is a mixture.

examples.text: The new CD is a compound of North American rock music and Middle Eastern religious songs.

glosses: A compound is a group of buildings surrounded by a fence or wall.
If something is compounded, it is added to.

examples.text: Her troubles were now compounded by the rain.

glosses: If interest is compounded, it is paid on earlier interest payments.

examples.text: Interest is compounded monthly.

glosses: Evolution is the process of slow change. It is most used in biology to refer to the way living things change over long periods of time in order to adapt to their surroundings.

examples.text: The theory of evolution is the basis of modern biology.
For the first time, the evolution of some bacteria has been observed.
Evolution is the reason animals and plants of today are different from those of long ago.
He believed that the evolution of society followed certain laws.
Creationists are people who deny that evolution is real, because it contradicts their religious beliefs, which are that God made everything.

glosses: An evolution is a change that happens over time.

examples.text: Over the last ten years, there has been an evolution in the way we think about this disease.

glosses: Discretion is the ability and power to decide.

examples.text: The judge made a mistake in exercising his discretion to end the trial early.
The money will be offered at the discretion of the Environmental Health Department.

glosses: Discretion is the ability to do something in a way that does not upset people.
Discretion is the ability to keep a secret.
A servant is someone who works for a person or for a family, doing things like cooking and washing. Often the servant lives in the house where they work. A servant works for the same family all day.

examples.text: This rich family has three servants working for them in their big house.

glosses: A problem or situation is serious if it is not funny or comical, but important.

examples.text: This is a serious problem. We must do something.

glosses: A person is serious if the person is not laughing or joking, but saying what they mean.

examples.text: I see. When you said the room was empty, you were serious!
The woman's face looked serious, so I knew she was saying something important.

glosses: Sense is any basic ability or understanding.

examples.text: She has a great sense of fashion.
She uses good sense when choosing her friends.
Why did you do that?! Where's your common sense?!

glosses: Sense is the ability to understand a situation or emotions.

examples.text: I sensed you were upset before you said anything.
I sense you don't want to be with me.
Do I sense a chance for success in your game plan?

glosses: The way something seems to be is the way you think it is when you look at it, hear about it, think about it, etc.

examples.text: It seems unlikely that they will remember your name after meeting you once.
As odd as it may seem, the girl's best friend is an eighty year old man.
It was a terrible night, but somehow it doesn't seem so bad this morning.
It is still raining on him, but he doesn't seem to notice.
The bad smells did not seem to bother them.
The young man seemed to have forgotten all his promises.
They really seemed to be enjoying what they were doing.
The changes seem to suggest that the police have new information.
It seems to me that we ought to try again.
It seemed like forever, but I think it got there in about 12 to 15 minutes.
It seemed like a crazy idea; it had never been done before.
You seem like a very nice guy.
The very air he was breathing seemed as if it were on fire.

glosses: To send something is to make the thing go somewhere without the person. A person sends a letter by putting it in a mailbox. A person can send another person somewhere by telling the person to go there.

examples.text: She needed to send a letter to her mother to say she had arrived safely.
Could you send Roger into see me please?

glosses: A person makes a selection when a person chooses a smaller number of things from a larger group of things.
A selection of things is different things that have been chosen or that you can choose from.

examples.text: The window of the store shows a selection of the things you can buy in the store.

glosses: Selection is a process where the best adapted life forms survive and the others die out.

examples.text: Charles Darwin was a scientist who wrote about natural selection.

glosses: In Australia, a selection was an area of land which a farmer could choose to buy.
