glosses: A class act is high quality .

examples.text: Most high school coaches are class individuals, and they should get our thanks.

glosses: Someone polishes something when they rub it with a cloth to make it smooth and shiny. Sometimes wax or a special liquid is used.

examples.text: A wooden floor should be polished with floor wax.
Silver needs to be polished to make it shiny.

glosses: Polish is a special liquid used for polishing things.

examples.text: I need to buy some polish for polishing my wooden table.

glosses: Pleasure is a nice feeling we have when we do something that's fun or that feels good.

examples.text: Being at this party and seeing my friends again is a real pleasure.

glosses: If you pleasure someone, you do something for someone to make them feel good.
We say "please" when we want to ask someone politely to do something.

examples.text: Pass the salt, please.

glosses: Someone pleases someone else when they do what that person likes or wants.

examples.text: Giving her these flowers will please her.

glosses: A plant is something that lives and grows in one place. Plants usually have green leaves and roots. Flowers and trees are plants. Plants and animals are the main kinds of life.
A plant is a factory.
To put a seed or plant in soil for it to grow.

examples.text: I planted some flowers last week and I hope they will grow and blossom.

glosses: A pin is a small, sharp thing used for holding things together.
When you pin something, you are fastening it with a pin.

examples.text: We should pin this poster to that wall.
She pinned the dress pattern to the fabric.
Joey pinned the tail on the donkey and won the prize.

glosses: If you pin someone, you force someone firmly onto the ground to prevent them from moving.

examples.text: A term in wrestling meaning to force an opponent's shoulders to the mat and holding them there for three seconds.

glosses: Peace is the way a country is when there is no war.

examples.text: The people lived in peace for thirty years.

glosses: Peace is when there is silence or quiet. There is no noise and nothing happening suddenly.

examples.text: Will you please go away and leave me in peace?

glosses: A payment is some money that someone is giving to someone else when they're buying something.

examples.text: I sent the things they wanted, but I haven't gotten the payment for them yet.

glosses: Payment is the act of paying.

examples.text: I usually use my credit card for payment.
Late payment of fees will end the contract.

glosses: A point is a position with no size, or a small dot.

examples.text: These two lines meet at this point.

glosses: A point is the sharp end of a knife or other sharp thing.

examples.text: He used the point of the knife to make a hole in the can.

glosses: The point of something is the reason or purpose for it.

examples.text: The whole point of coming here was to plant this tree, so let's not go home without doing it.

glosses: A point is a dot between two numbers. To the dot's right, you find a decimal.

examples.text: You need a point between the one and the zero.

glosses: To point at something is to hold one finger (or a stick, arrow or other long, thin thing) in the direction of the thing so that people will look at the thing.

examples.text: He pointed her toward the gate.

glosses: You use point to introduce decimals in a number that is not an integer.

examples.text: The price has gone up by two point five percent (2.5%).

glosses: Paste is a thick liquid for sticking (attaching) things together. Paste is like glue, but glue is more liquid and paste is more solid.

examples.text: He mixed flour and water to make a paste for sticking the paper together.

glosses: Any very thick liquid, almost solid.

examples.text: Tomato paste is good in sauce to put on rice or spaghetti.

glosses: If you paste something in a computer program, you cut or copy it from one place and put a copy of it somewhere else.
To stick things together using paste.

examples.text: She pasted the pictures onto the wall.

glosses: A package; a box wrapped in paper; a thing bigger than a letter that is sent in the mail.

examples.text: On my birthday, I got a parcel in the mail.

glosses: A parcel of land is a piece of land that was part of a larger piece.
If you parcel something out, you divide it into small parts to give to different people.

examples.text: The set of books was parcelled out among the people who were there.

glosses: If you parcel something off, you divide it into small parts to be sold to different people.
If you parcel something up, you make it into a parcel by wrapping it up.
The owner of a thing is the person who owns the thing: who has the thing or who should have the thing. A thing belongs to its owner.

examples.text: Who is the owner of this coat that was left on a chair?
You have to give it back to me. I'm the owner.

glosses: An oven is for cooking food. It's hot and people put food inside it.

examples.text: Leave the cake in the oven for thirty minutes.

glosses: An ornament is something that is put onto something or someone just to look beautiful and for no other reason.

examples.text: One ring on her finger was the only ornament she wore.
We put ornaments on the Christmas tree.

glosses: If you ornament something, you decorate or add to it.

examples.text: Let's ornament the tree with lights to make it more festive.

glosses: Order is when things are where they should be.

examples.text: I need to take some time to put my things in order.

glosses: The order of some things means which thing is first, which one is second, which one is last, etc.

examples.text: The children will take turns in order of age.

glosses: An order is a group of religious people, such as monks or nuns, who follow certain rules.

examples.text: St. Ignatius Loyola founded the Jesuit order in 1537.

glosses: To order something is to ask someone to sell it to you.

examples.text: At the restaurant, she ordered chicken and potatoes.

glosses: To order someone to do something is to tell the person that they must do it.

examples.text: The father ordered his children to be quiet.

glosses: To order things is to put them in a certain order.

examples.text: We need to order them alphabetically.

glosses: The other people or things, are those apart from the ones we have or were talking about.

examples.text: No, don't put it on this table. Put it on the other table.
The people inside are OK, but the other people are getting wet.
He sat on the other side of the table.

glosses: more

examples.text: There are many other kinds of problems.
Do you have any other questions?

glosses: different

examples.text: There were some other cars at their house the other day.

glosses: Others are those apart from the ones we have or were talking about.

examples.text: Thanks for the books. I'll get the others tomorrow.
Wow, this is a lot. How many others are there?
We need this one and one other.

glosses: no more than; no other than; just

examples.text: There are only three schools in this town.
You can get this only in Canada.
I'm only able to go on Monday.
He comes only once a year.
She only eats vegetables.
This is only what we got.
He's not only nice, but also good looking.
We will stop only to rest.
Things will only get worse.
Only call me if you have to.

glosses: Just one or just a few; this and no other; no more than this.

examples.text: She is the only woman doctor in this city.
These are the only coins I have.

glosses: An only child, son, girl, etc. has no brothers or sisters.
You use only to introduce a fact that prevents a statement from being completely true.

examples.text: They probably could do it, only you never let them try.

glosses: Observation is the act of carefully seeing things that happen.

examples.text: To learn, you must be good at observation.

glosses: An observation is something someone saw, heard etc.

examples.text: In science, we record our observations so we can think about them later.

glosses: A note is a single sound in music.

examples.text: In this song, every word is on a different note.

glosses: A note is a short letter; something written on a small piece of paper.

examples.text: If you go out, leave me a note to tell me where you went.

glosses: You note that something happened when you see that it happened and remember it.

examples.text: I noted that you weren't wearing shoes.

glosses: North is the direction towards the top of the Earth, opposite to south; If you are looking north, the sun sets on your left.

examples.text: Canada is the biggest country in North America.

glosses: North is the end of a magnet that points north.
The north is the area of land north of the speaker; Also the Arctic.
In the direction north; towards the north

examples.text: The place you want is two miles north of here.
It's colder here because we're further north.

glosses: News is information about things that happened a short time ago, especially on the radio, TV or in newspapers.

examples.text: Did you hear the news that the war just ended?
Do you have any news about Paul's sickness?

glosses: A net is a thing made of ropes or string that lets small things through but keeps big things in.

examples.text: I forgot my fishing net. What will we use to catch fish now?
The tennis player hit the ball into the net.

glosses: To net something is to catch it in a net.

examples.text: He netted a big fish.

glosses: A company's net income is its profits minus its expenses.
A nerve is a cell in the body that sends signals. The brain is made of nerves.

examples.text: She can't feel anything with this arm, and can't move her arm, because the nerves were cut in an accident.

glosses: Nerve is confidence: a feeling of being able to do something.

examples.text: He didn't have the nerve to ask her to dance.
You had a lot of nerve, saying that to me! Go away!

glosses: A needle is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing with a hole in it, used for sewing.

examples.text: She used a needle and blue thread to fix the hole in the shirt.

glosses: A needle is a long, thing, sharp metal thing for putting drugs into a person through the skin.

examples.text: The doctor used the needle to inject the medicine into the patient.

glosses: To tease; to make fun of.

examples.text: Billy needled his sister incessantly about her pimples.

glosses: A compliment is a few words of praise: saying that someone or something is good in some way.

examples.text: William gave me a compliment and that made me feel good. He told me my hair was nice.

glosses: Compliment means to praise someone.

examples.text: She complimented him on his clothes because they looked good.

glosses: A conjunction is a word used to join words, phrases, clauses, or sentences.

examples.text: The word or is a conjunction because it can join two words: Tell me if you see a red or blue car.
The word that can be used as a conjunction: I think that you are right.

glosses: Three common conjunctions
A conviction is when a court finds a person guilty of doing a crime.

examples.text: There was a conviction in his case, so he went to jail.

glosses: A conviction is a strong belief that you think is true.

examples.text: Because of their strong conviction, I begin to feel that they may be right.

glosses: A place or person is peaceful when there is silence or quiet. There is no noise and nothing happening suddenly.
If you need something, you want it and must have it.

examples.text: Everyone needs food and water.

glosses: If you need to do something, it is very important for you to do it.

examples.text: Sir, you need to leave now.

glosses: If you need do something, you have to do it.

examples.text: Need you do that all the time?
You needn't keep telling me. I heard you the first time.

glosses: If you have a need for something, you must have it; something necessary or required.

examples.text: I've always tried to have few needs beyond food, clothing and shelter.

glosses: Something is necessary if people need it. It must happen or there will be a big problem.

examples.text: It's necessary to stop when you see a red light.

glosses: A necessary is a bathroom.
Something is natural if people didn't make it.

examples.text: Animals, plants and rocks are natural things.

glosses: Something is natural if it's the way it usually is, without people changing it, or is a way that is not a surprise.

examples.text: It's only natural for you to think that.

glosses: A nail is a small, long, thin sharp metal thing for holding wood together. People put it into the wood by hitting it with a hammer.

examples.text: I need some nails to fix the roof.

glosses: A nail is the thick, hard part at the ends of fingers and toes.

examples.text: I broke the top off my finger nail and it was very painful.

glosses: If you nail something to something else, you use a nail to join them.

examples.text: He nailed the set of shelves onto the wall.

glosses: When someone gets an idea just right, we say they nailed it or "hit the nail on the head".

examples.text: I think you've nailed the reason why this isn't working.

glosses: A muscle is a part of the body of a person or animal. It's a part that pulls to make parts of the body move.

examples.text: He can lift heavy things because he has strong muscles.

glosses: To muscle is to use strength or muscles to do something.

examples.text: He muscled his way into the room between the people who were trying to stop him.

glosses: The moon is the shining white and grey object in the sky at night. It appears to change shape from round (a full moon) to a crescent and back again. It's like a small planet that goes around the Earth.

examples.text: I was able to see the road because there was a full moon that night.

glosses: A moon is a thing like a small planet that goes around another planet.

examples.text: Galileo saw four moons of Jupiter: Callisto, Europa, Ganymede and Io.

glosses: If you moon someone, you show them your bare buttocks.

examples.text: Someone in the car pulled down their pants and mooned us as they drove past.

glosses: A monkey is a primate with a long tail that climbs trees.

examples.text: We saw Vervet monkeys in the Zoo.

glosses: If you monkey something, you make changes to it.

examples.text: I foolishly monkeyed with the control panel and it ended up exploding.

glosses: A minute is a short time equal to sixty seconds. There are sixty minutes in one hour.

examples.text: He ran the race in 1 minute and ten seconds.

glosses: A minute is a short time.

examples.text: Please wait a minute while I get my coat and then I will come with you.

glosses: Minute things are small.

examples.text: The pictures appear similar, with only a few, minute differences.

glosses: Someone's mind is the part of them that thinks.

examples.text: In my mind I know I must go, but in my heart I want to stay here.
We will solve this problem. We have the best minds in the country working on it.

glosses: If you mind some action or thing, you feel negatively about it.

examples.text: "Do you mind if I sit here?" "No, not at all"
"It's raining outside. You should take an umbrella" "It's OK, I don't mind the rain"

glosses: If you mind someone or something, you look after it.

examples.text: "Could you mind the children while I go to the bathroom?"

glosses: If something is military, it is a characteristic of people in the armed forces.

examples.text: Sick soldiers go to the military hospital.

glosses: If something is military, it is about armed forces such as the army, marines, navy, or air force.
If something is military, it has to do with war.
If something is military, it has to do with armies and ground troops.
A military is armed forces.
The military is the United States armed forces in general.

examples.text: It's not the job of the military to make policy.

glosses: The place that is between two things; the place that is halfway between two ends of something.

examples.text: Cut the wood exactly in the middle to get two pieces of equal size.
The middle of the three books is the one you want.

glosses: When someone remembers something, we call the thing they remember a memory.

examples.text: I have very nice memories of the time when my children were young.

glosses: The part of the mind that remembers; the act of remembering.

examples.text: When we get older, our memory isn't as good.

glosses: The part of a computer that holds information.
A meeting is when a group of people come together to talk about something important.

examples.text: The meeting will be in the green room after lunch. I hope you'll be there.

glosses: The present participle of meet.

A man and a woman are married if they are husband and wife to each other. Usually when two people are married they live in the same house and they often have children. Two people have a special day to become married.

examples.text: I don't need to meet more young men—I'm already married.

glosses: If two things are married they have been made into one thing.

examples.text: Music and television are married in music videos.

glosses: The past and past participle of marry.
A mark is a single line left by a pen or pencil, or any small bit of color that got onto something.

examples.text: You have a mark on your shirt from that tomato sauce you were eating.

glosses: If you mark something, you put a mark on it.

examples.text: The big rock marked the side of the car a little when she drove too close to it.
I marked the boxes so we would know which ones are mine.

glosses: If you mark something, you notice it or pay attention to it.

examples.text: Mark my words!

glosses: When someone loves another person, they feel good about the person and want the person to be happy.

examples.text: I love Colin.
Mothers love their children very deeply.

glosses: The feeling of loving someone and caring for them.

examples.text: Is my love for him a real love that will last a long time?

glosses: To love someone or something means to like someone or something very much.

examples.text: I love the simple English Wikipedia.

glosses: A tennis player who has scored love has a score of zero.

examples.text: (From a sports commentator) Fifteen-love!

glosses: A loss happens when something goes where people can't find it. People don't know where the thing is or they don't have it any more.

examples.text: The loss of my keys means I can't go into my house today.

glosses: Loss is when someone's loved one dies. When someone dies, they are no longer with you.

examples.text: I loss both of my grandparents from old age.

glosses: A loss (shown as L) is charged to the pitcher of the losing team.
Someone looks at something when they move their head or move their eyes so that they can see the thing.

examples.text: Look at this picture! Isn't it beautiful?

glosses: The way that something looks is the way that it appears.

examples.text: A new car looks very nice until it gets dirty.
That doughnut looks delicious.

glosses: A lock is a metal thing on a door (or on a window, drawer, etc.) that stops people from opening the door unless they have the right key to open it.

examples.text: No one will take things from my house. I have a very strong lock on the door.

glosses: A lock is two or more gates (doors) in water to let boats move from lower water to higher water or the other way.
Someone locks a door when they close the lock with a key so that no one can come in.

examples.text: Remember to lock the door when you leave the house.

glosses: The present participle of live.
A way of earning money.

examples.text: What do you do for a living?

glosses: A living thing is a person, animal or plant that is not dead—it is still able to function and grow.

examples.text: Living things grow and make more living things like themselves.

glosses: Linen is a material that some cloth is made of. It comes from the flax plant, and in the past, bed sheets were often made from it, before cotton was used.

examples.text: This shirt is made of linen.

glosses: Linens are something made from linen, especially bed sheets.

examples.text: Would you like to change the linens on your bed?

glosses: A line is a mark that is long, straight and very thin.

examples.text: She drew a line down the middle of the page to divide the page into two parts.

glosses: A line is a row.

examples.text: Put the buttons in a straight line on the front of the shirt.

glosses: A line is a row of people who are waiting for something in order; a queue.

examples.text: You got here last, so you have to stand at the back of the line.

glosses: Someone lines things up when they put them in a straight line or row.
Someone lines something up when they put it just in the right place or at the edge of something.

examples.text: Line up the end of the piece of wood with the edge of the table.

glosses: Someone lines up when they start waiting in a line (queue) with other people.

examples.text: Everyone line up here, please, and I'll help you one at a time.

glosses: Someone lines something when they mark it with one or more lines.

examples.text: Please line the pitch before the match.

glosses: Someone lines something when they add an inside layer of material (liner) to it.
Someone lifts something when they use their hands to make the thing go up.

examples.text: He lifted the little boy onto his shoulders.
She lifted the heavy box from the floor onto the table.
He is lifting some suitcases.

glosses: If you give someone a lift, you drive them somewhere, usually in your car.
A lift is a machine that lifts people up or down to different parts of a building.
Even, flat, straight, smooth, horizontal. Having all parts equally as high as all other parts.

examples.text: This table is not level: things are rolling off it.

glosses: If one thing is level with another, they are at the same height.

examples.text: The bookshelf is level with the top of the door frame.

glosses: A level is a place that is higher or lower than some other places.

examples.text: The room you want is on the third level of this building.

glosses: A tool for finding out whether a surface is level.

Someone laughs when they make a sound with their mouth because they think something is funny. It can sound like "ha ha", "ho ho", "hee hee", etc.

examples.text: That was a really good joke. I've never laughed so hard!

glosses: The sound of someone laughing, or the action of laughing.

examples.text: We had lots of good laughs at the party.
I heard a laugh in the other room and went to see what they were laughing at.

glosses: Happening or coming after all other similar things or people.

examples.text: I was the last person to go there: when I went, the others were all already there.
My house is the last house at the end of the street.
At last, after twenty hours on the boat, they arrived at their destination.

glosses: To endure, continue over time.

examples.text: Summer seems to last longer each year.

glosses: To hold out, continue undefeated or entire.

examples.text: I don't know how much longer we can last without reinforcements.

glosses: Last week, month, year, etc. is the one that comes before this one.

examples.text: I didn't see you last week.
I haven't seen him since the summer before last.

glosses: An interest is when a person wants to know more about someone or something or likes someone or something or likes to do something.

examples.text: She has a strong interest in art. She is going to go to an art school.
What are your interests?

glosses: An interest is when someone or something is important to a person, or if good things happening to the thing are good for the person.

examples.text: Because I own a house on this street, I have an interest in keeping the street clean.
I'm doing this to look after my own interests.

glosses: When someone borrows money, they have to give back more money than they borrowed. The extra money they have to pay is called interest.

examples.text: The bank gives me two percent interest per year on the money in my account.

glosses: If a person is interested, they are curious and want to find out about someone or something.

examples.text: I am interested in researching flowers.
Does maths interest you?

glosses: The limit is the edge of how far something can go. It can go up to the limit but no farther.

examples.text: This fence is at the limit of my property.
The heater sets a limit to how cold it can be in the house; it can't get colder than that.
There is no limit to what we can do.

glosses: To make something stay inside a limit.

examples.text: The fence limits the cows from going out of the field.

glosses: If you limit someone, you reduce or take away their freedom.
ordinal twentieth) The number 20.

examples.text: I was in university when I was twenty years old.

glosses: A twenty is a 20 dollar bill.

examples.text: I'd like my $50 as 1 twenty, 2 tens and 2 fives.

glosses: "Twenty" is short for 10-20, meaning location.

examples.text: Jason, what's your twenty?

glosses: ordinal thirtieth) The number 30.

examples.text: I had my first child when I was thirty years old.

glosses: The number 30.

examples.text: Three tens is thirty.

glosses: The scope of a book, a law, a duty, etc. is how much is included or how far it can go.

examples.text: The small budget has limited the scope of the research.
There are plans to expand the scope of the department's activities.
This kind of art allows the greatest scope for individual expression.
It is not within the scope of this book to talk about them all.

glosses: A scope is an instrument for looking at things, e.g., a telescope or a microscope.
If you scope something (out), you look at it carefully.

examples.text: I scoped out the place last week. It seems nice.

glosses: If you enhance something, you make it bigger or better.

examples.text: He can greatly enhance his reputation by winning tonight.
Our aim is to enhance the quality of life for the British people.

glosses: If you have control over someone or something, you can make it do what you want.

examples.text: He should try to take control and tell the other handlers what to do.
Driving in the rain, he had lost control on the wet surface and spun off the road.
The country fell under the direct control of the army.
They are trying to keep tighter control over spending.
The government will demand improved pollution control systems for all factories.
Most companies devote some resources to quality control and product testing.
Unless birth control methods are used, sooner or later the woman is likely to get pregnant.
The continuing Soviet desire for arms control led to a SALT II treaty.
The brain's control systems tend to decline with age so that, for instance, our balance gets less good.
The experimental group took the medicine while the control group took a sugar pill.
Suddenly the airplane went out of control and started diving.

glosses: A control is a button, switch, dial, etc. that lets you make a machine do what you want.

examples.text: If you turn off your TV with the remote control, it continues to use a quarter of normal power.
She touched the volume control and the sound dropped.

glosses: If you control something, you make it do what you want.

examples.text: Too many people are overweight because they can't control their eating behaviour.
The company is controlled by a New York businessman.

glosses: If you control something, you do not let its numbers or size grow too much.

examples.text: The new plan should control inflation.

glosses: If something is high, it is a long way up.

examples.text: The airplane flew very high.

glosses: If something is high, its top is a long way up.

examples.text: That is the highest mountain near here.

glosses: If something is high, it is very good. It might be better or more important than other things. This can often means someone has more power.

examples.text: The Supreme Court is the highest court in America.
Brian Boru was called the high king of Ireland.
Meeting my girlfriend was the high point of my year.

glosses: If someone is high, that person's mind is affected by drugs.

examples.text: John was high from marijuana last night.

glosses: A lead is a wire or strap attached to something.

examples.text: The dog can't go far because it's on a short lead.
Attach this lead to one end of the battery.

glosses: Lead is a very heavy gray metal. It's a chemical symbol is Pb.

examples.text: This box is so heavy, it feels as if it's full of lead.

glosses: Someone is leading other people if the person is going first and the other people are following or coming after.

examples.text: Please lead us to the house, because you know how to go there.

glosses: Showing or telling other people what to do.

examples.text: He moves that little stick in the air to lead the people making music.

glosses: A written record of a saying or action of the Prophet Muhammad. Used as a basis for conduct in Islamic practices.
Insurance is an agreement where someone pays a small amount of money, and if something bad happens, they get money to help them.

examples.text: I have fire insurance for my house.

glosses: An instrument is any thing people hold in their hand and use to do something.

examples.text: A hammer is a heavy instrument.

glosses: An instrument is something used to play music.

examples.text: I enjoy playing music, my favorite instrument is the guitar.

glosses: To grow; to become bigger.

examples.text: The amount of money in my bank account is increasing.

glosses: The amount which something has grown.

examples.text: There was an increase in movie releases last year.

glosses: An industry is a kind of work that makes things.

examples.text: Many people in this country have jobs in the clothing industry.

glosses: Industry is the quality of working hard, trying hard and doing it well.

examples.text: Because of her industry, she made a lot of money.

glosses: Humor is ideas that make people laugh: jokes, funny things.

examples.text: I like the stories she tells because they're full of humor.

The word how is used to ask about the way something happens or the way people do things.

examples.text: How will we ever solve this problem?

glosses: The word how is used to tell about the way something happens or the way people do things.

examples.text: I know how we can solve this problem.
This is how to make this machine work.

glosses: The word how is used to show that you feel strongly about something.

examples.text: How old he looks!

glosses: You use how to ask if something was good or bad, or what qualities it has.

examples.text: How was the movie?
How are you feeling?

glosses: You use how to tell that something happens, is done, or is true.

examples.text: She told him how it wasn't fun anymore.

glosses: A horn is a long, sharp thing that grows on the head of some animals such as goats and sheep.

examples.text: The goat used its horn to break the fence.
They used a cow's horn as a cup to drink out of.

glosses: A horn is a musical instrument that you blow and usually made of metal.
When someone hopes that something will happen, it means that they want it to happen and they think it may happen.

examples.text: We hope that more women will decide to join the course.
It was hoped that the job would be filled by a local person.

glosses: A hope is the idea in someone's mind when they're hoping for something.

examples.text: All of my hopes came true!

glosses: A hook is a curved, sharp thing, usually made of metal and often small. Someone can put the hook through a hole in something to grip it so that they can pull the thing.
If you are hooking something, you are attaching it to a hook.

examples.text: Hook the bag here, and the conveyor will carry it away.

glosses: History is what happened in the past.

examples.text: China has many old books about its history.
The restaurant is close to the city's history and art museums.

glosses: History is the study of what happened in the past.

examples.text: He is a professor of history.

glosses: If somebody or something makes history, they do something very important that will not be forgotten.

examples.text: She made history by becoming Africa's first elected female president.

glosses: If somebody or something goes down in history, they are remembered by people because they were very important or well known.

examples.text: She'll go down in history as one of our greatest writers.

glosses: A history is a book recording things that have happened.

examples.text: He was reading a history of Ancient Rome.

glosses: If somebody or something has a history of something, it's very common for them.

examples.text: She has a history of cheating on tests.

glosses: If you say something is history, you mean it's finished, over, dead, or not important any more.

examples.text: OK, that game's history.

glosses: If you say the rest is history, you mean you don't have to tell about because everyone already knows.

examples.text: They just happened to run into each other at the right time, and the rest is history.

glosses: If you help another person do something, you do things to make it easier for them to do the thing, or you do part of it for them.

examples.text: Will you please help me wash the dishes?

glosses: If you can't help doing something or can't help but do it, you cannot avoid it. You do it even without wanting or planning to.

examples.text: When I look at the class, I can not help feeling that something has gone wrong.
They agreed that it was good, but I can't help wondering, "good for who?"

glosses: Help is the act of helping.

examples.text: Will you please give me some help? This is hard for just one person to do.

glosses: The help is people who work in a home cooking, cleaning, etc.

examples.text: The help arrives as 9 o' clock.

glosses: A healthy person is someone who is not sick. They are strong and will probably live a long time.

examples.text: I need three young, healthy people to help me.
She gets sick frequently. She's never very healthy.

glosses: Healthy things leads to better health.

examples.text: Healthy food is full of vitamins and minerals.

glosses: A harbor is some water in a curve of land where it's safe for boats because there are no big waves.

examples.text: A ship in the harbor is safe -- but that is not what ships are for.

glosses: To provide a harbor or safe place for something or someone.

examples.text: The old docks once harbored all kinds of ships, but they have been closed for years now.

glosses: To take refuge or shelter somewhere.

examples.text: The ships harbor in the bay during the winter months.

glosses: To hold onto an idea.

examples.text: Sam has harbored resentment against Joe since Joe got the job they both applied for.

glosses: A drop is a very small amount of a liquid.

examples.text: A drop of water weighs 0.1 grams.

glosses: A drop is the fall of something.

examples.text: There was a drop in the prices last week.

glosses: To fall, or to let something fall.

examples.text: He dropped from the roof when he was running.

glosses: Heat is a kind of energy. It is the quality things have when they are warm or hot.

examples.text: This is a good coat. It keeps the heat in.
The heat from the sun is making me feel hot and tired.

glosses: To make something hot.

examples.text: I just need to heat up the food and then we can eat.

glosses: A gun is a weapon that sends bullets through its metal tube.

examples.text: John F. Kennedy was shot by a gun.

glosses: To make an engine work fast by opening its throttle.

examples.text: I gunned the engine and passed his car.

glosses: If someone is gunned down, they are shot by something, usually a gun.

examples.text: He was gunned down by a hitman.

glosses: A garden is a place where flowers and other plants grow where people want them to. Frequently it is a small place with a wall around it, near a house. It may have rocks and other things in it to look beautiful.

examples.text: She spends a lot of time taking care of the flowers in her garden.

glosses: If you garden, you work in a garden, especially your own garden around your house.

examples.text: He joined his mother when she gardened and talked to her flowers.

glosses: When something is from someone, the person gave or sent it.

examples.text: I got a gift from my grandmother today.

glosses: When someone is from a place, that's where they started.

examples.text: I am Chinese. I come from Hunan province.
Sorry I'm late. I just came from school.

glosses: You use from to talk about distances between thing in space or time.

examples.text: Saturn is far from earth.
School is 5km from my home.
The year 2515 is a long time from now.

glosses: The existence of a thing is the quality of being real, of being in the world, of just being.

examples.text: Do you believe in the existence of God?
The existence of a mark on my shirt is the reason I didn't go to the party.

glosses: Usual; about most things. An idea is a general idea if it's about many things or about most things, not just about one specific thing.

examples.text: First I will talk about general problems of farming, and then I will talk about the specific problems of wheat farming.
In general, I enjoy pizza.

glosses: General is approximate, not exact; maybe a little different; close but maybe not the same.
A general is the leader of an army.

examples.text: The president told the general to bring the army home.

glosses: If you give something to someone else, you had the thing and you let the other person have it. Maybe you use your hands to put the thing in the other person's hands. Usually after that, the thing is the other person's thing.

examples.text: Give me that book, please; I want to read it.
My mother gave me this stone when I was young.

glosses: If you give a speech, you talk to a group of people.
To move towards a place or into a place; to move to the place where the person who is talking is.

examples.text: Come to my house and I will give you something to eat.
Come here to me.
Twenty people came to the party.
He came here, but he went away again before you came here.

glosses: The past participle of come.
When something happens or arrives.

examples.text: We'll talk again come January.

glosses: Semen.

examples.text: (also spelled cum)

glosses: If you go, you move in space, especially to or through a place.

examples.text: I go to the seashore every summer.
Kathy goes to the seashore every summer, too.
I went to the seashore last year.
She's gone to the seashore.
I'm going to the seashore next year.

glosses: If you go, you move in time, often in your mind.

examples.text: You have to go back to 1911 to find a wetter day.
Marty McFly jumped in the time machine and went to 1965.

glosses: If you go, you move on the computer, the internet, or in the memory.

examples.text: Then go to the C: drive.
His mind went to the last time he saw her.

glosses: If you go, you move a certain distance or a certain way.

examples.text: We've gone 10 kilometers today.
Sandra is going in circles.

glosses: If you go, you leave or move away.

examples.text: Please don't go.
People have been coming and going all day.

glosses: If you go bad, wild, blind, etc., you become like that.

examples.text: Jim went blind.

glosses: A clear idea is an idea that is easy to understand.

examples.text: OK, so you need the key. I see. That's clear now.
Now it's clear as a bell to me why you want to stay here.

glosses: If it is clear that something is a certain way, there can be no mistake about it.

examples.text: The women made it clear that they were doing this only because they wanted to.
It soon became perfectly clear that he was not going to get better.
It's clear from looking at you that you couldn't lift it; you're too small.
This is a clear example of an idea that works.

glosses: If you are clear about something, you understand it well.

examples.text: Mike, I want to be clear about what you said, so can you tell me again.
I'm sorry, but I'm not clear about what I'm supposed to do.

glosses: If you are clear about something, you make it easy for people to understand you.

examples.text: The coach had been very clear about what he wanted them to do.
They haven't been so clear about how much water is in there.

glosses: If your head or your thinking is clear, then you can think well.

examples.text: After his coffee and a quick walk, his head felt clear.
On Monday, he looked confused and didn't say much, but the next day, his thinking seemed more clear.

glosses: If something is clear, people can see through it.

examples.text: The window is made of clear glass.
The water wasn't clear enough to see the bottom.

glosses: If something is clear, it has nothing that gets in your way.

examples.text: I try to drive to work only when the roads are clear.
It's supposed to be clear and sunny today.
That table's not clear yet. Can you get the stuff off it?
The skies were clear of clouds.

glosses: If something is clear, it is easy to see or hear.

examples.text: The picture wasn't clear enough to see whose face it was.
At first, the radio was noisy, but we moved and then we got clear, rich sound.

glosses: If your skin is clear, it has no spots on it.

examples.text: Her deep honey skin was clear except for the small mark on her left cheek.

glosses: If your eyes are clear, they are healthy, bright, and lively.

examples.text: His eyes were sharp and clear, and full of fun.

glosses: Clear profit is profit after tax.

examples.text: These are priced so high that the manufacturers pocket $8,000 clear profit per $30,000 unit.

glosses: If you have a clear conscience or your conscience is clear, you do not feel guilty.

examples.text: I sleep perfectly at night. I have a clear conscience. I don't have blood on my hands.

glosses: If you clear something, you move or remove things that you don't want there.

examples.text: You clear the table and I'll get coffee ready.
We'll have to clear out the garage to make room for the new car.
My grandparents cleared this land so that we could live and farm here.
I worked for ten minutes to clear a path in the snow from the door to the road.
About 13 million hectares of forest were cleared each year.

glosses: If something clears, it becomes clear.

examples.text: After the fire, it took some time for the air to clear.
Above her, the black sky cleared, until she could see the thousands of stars all across it.
The window fogged and cleared as she breathed on it.

glosses: If something clears, it goes away, leaving the place it was clear.

examples.text: After the fire, it took some time for the smoke to clear.
He couldn't see well as car drove up the dirt road, but after the dust had cleared, he could see it was his father.

glosses: If you clear your throat, you cough lightly to make speaking easier.

examples.text: Tears filled her eyes again, and she cleared her throat. "As soon as I can, I'll get on a plane and meet you."

glosses: If you clear the air, or if the air clears, you talk about a problem so that nobody has doubts or bad feelings.

examples.text: I think it's important for me to tell you what has happened and clear the air about this matter.

glosses: If you clear somebody to do something, you give them permission.

examples.text: His personal plane had been cleared to land at the airport.

glosses: If your head, mind, thinking, etc. clears then you become able to think well.

examples.text: The coffee helped to clear her head, and she sat down to think.

glosses: If you clear something, you get over it without touching it or without a problem.

examples.text: The bike got air and cleared the water by a meter.

glosses: If you clear somebody of something bad you show that they did not do it.

examples.text: After clearing him of any wrongdoing, the police set him free.

glosses: If you clear a hurdle, you solve one of a number of problems.

examples.text: The case has many more hurdles to clear before it can go to trial.
The winner had to clear plenty of hurdles before beating Clement.

glosses: After the dust clears is some time later, when there is no more trouble or confusion.

examples.text: It took a few weeks, but after the dust had cleared, and everybody had gone home, he realized he had enjoyed it.

glosses: If a cheque clears, then the money is ready to be used.
If you clear a certain amount of money, you make that as profit (after expenses).
If you clear the ball or puck, you move it away from your own goal.
Out of, away from, especially too far away to be noticed or caught.

examples.text: After a short walk, we were clear of the town.
The fish was so heavy that he couldn't get it clear of the water.
After their fight, he steered clear of her for a week.
It was so crowded that they had to fight their way out and clear of the people.
So far, the company has stayed clear of trouble.
Two more wins would put them clear of the Giants.
Just clear of the school yard, students were smoking.

glosses: Completely, without limit.

examples.text: You could see clear across the water, all the way to the church 60 km away on the other side.

glosses: Something that is covering another thing is on top of (or over) the other thing in a way that stops people from seeing it.

examples.text: I cover myself in two blankets at night to stay warm.
Remember to cover the pot with a lid while you're cooking something.

glosses: A cover is something that usually covers something else.

examples.text: The cover of the book has a picture on it under the name of the book.

glosses: When something cracks it breaks along a line, maybe not a straight line. It might break into two pieces, or it might break but the two pieces are still attached.

examples.text: She cracked an egg and put the inside of the egg into a bowl.

glosses: A crack is the line where something is breaking.

examples.text: There is a crack from the edge of this plate to the middle. It will break soon.

glosses: A loud sound like the sound of something breaking.

examples.text: It was raining, and she saw a flash of lightning and heard the crack of thunder.

glosses: A strong, fairly cheap form of cocaine; crack often comes in the form of a rock and it is usually smoked in a crack-pipe.

examples.text: "I wouldn't use it, if I was going to use it I can afford real cocaine. Crack is wack." - Whitney Houston

glosses: Someone grips a thing by holding it tightly in their hand.

examples.text: He gripped the rope and pulled.

glosses: A hold or a way of holding something

examples.text: It's good to have a firm grip when shaking hands.
The ball will move differently depending on the grip used when throwing it.

glosses: A handle or a place to grip.

examples.text: There are several good grips on the northern face of this rock.

glosses: A bassist is someone who plays a bass instrument or sings bass.

examples.text: The bassist sat his guitar down.

glosses: no person

examples.text: Nobody would do something like that.
Almost nobody lives on Greenland.

glosses: A nobody is a person who is not important.

examples.text: Bob called Alice a nobody.
Don't worry. People won't listen to him. He's a nobody.

glosses: Humour is ideas that make people laugh: jokes, funny things.

examples.text: I like the stories she tells because they're full of humour.

glosses: To humour someone is to agree with them only to make the them happy.

examples.text: A ship in the harbour is safe -- but that is not what ships are for.

glosses: To provide a harbour or safe place for something or someone.

examples.text: The old docks once harboured all kinds of ships, but they have been closed for years now.

examples.text: Sam has harboured resentment against Joe since Joe got the job they both applied for.

examples.text: All the Wilsons ladies' clubs incorporate features designed to help women players improve and enjoy their game.
The systems would try to incorporate some of the ideas of Hayes and others.

glosses: If you incorporate x into y, you make x part of y.

examples.text: Please incorporate these changes into the final book.

glosses: An incorporated company is a corporation. Often written Inc. as part of a company name.

examples.text: We were a partnership for many years, but we incorporated last year.
Mona Doyle was hired as president of Consumer Network Inc.

glosses: The past participle of give.

examples.text: On any given day, you're likely to see her there.

glosses: Given x means if x is true, happened, exists, etc.

examples.text: Given our current problems, I don't think we can spend any more.
Given a number, we can find another number that is bigger.

glosses: Given that-clause means in consideration of the fact that-clause.

examples.text: Given that they are inexperienced, they've done a good job.

glosses: If someone is given to doing something, they do it regularly.

examples.text: My father's given to making long speeches about when he was a boy.

glosses: If someone is given to something, they wear, use, or do it often.

examples.text: When she got older, she was given to elegant clothes and long speeches.

glosses: A given is something that you accept as true.

examples.text: We need to make a decision about where we will live after this, but selling this house is a given.

glosses: A subsidiary is a company that is owned by a larger company. {[ant|parent}}

examples.text: This company owns three subsidiaries that make different kinds of machines.

glosses: If something is subsidiary, it is connected, but lower in importance, rank, or level, etc.

examples.text: Surprisingly, the subsidiary company became more successful than the parent company.
At some point work became subsidiary to music for her.

glosses: The input is the information that is put into something.

examples.text: Everyone who is affected should have a chance to provide input.
You can put a mask over your eyes and plugs in your ears, but it's impossible to block out all sensory input.
The input to the amplifier should be digital.
Teachers should welcome input from their students.
It is important to avoid errors during data input.

glosses: If you input something (often into a computer) you put it in.

examples.text: If the text has been correctly input to the computer, there should be no problems.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of input.
If something is abstract, you cannot touch it, and it is difficult to imagine or think about.

examples.text: A lot of abstract painting uses harsh shapes and most people do not like it.
More abstract ideas like "democracy" are not possible for animals.
Houses and books are things you can touch. Honesty, patience and courage are abstract.

glosses: If something is abstract, it is general.
If something is abstract, it is thought of as apart from any other use with an object; it is removed from it; it is separate or abstracted.
If something is abstract, it is not practical or realistic; it is not concrete; it is theoretical; it is vague.
If something is abstract, it does not have all of the facts; it is not factual.
An abstract is a short text that tells you the main ideas of a longer text, especially of scientific papers; it is a summary of something longer.

examples.text: The abstract of Isaac Newton's laws of gravity may be no more than 150 words.

glosses: An abstract is an abstraction; it is an abstract word.
An abstract is a piece of art that is made in the abstract fashion of art.
An abstract is a powdered solid extract of a vegetable that is then mixed with the sugar of milk.

If you abstract something, you separate it; you remove it.
If you abstract something, you withdraw it.
If you abstract something, you make abstractions of it in art.
If you abstract something, you take it away from someone without permission; you steal it.
If you abstract something, you think about it separate from everything else; you consider it abstractly.
If you abstract something, you go through the process or abstraction.
If someone or something is capable of something, they can do it.

examples.text: This system is capable of providing food for about 400 people.
I'm quite capable of looking after myself and I don't need you to tell me how.

glosses: If someone is capable, they can do a particular thing well.

examples.text: I'm confident I can leave everything in your capable hands.
I may be young but I can assure you I'm quite capable.

glosses: Someone is learning ideas if they didn't know the ideas before and they are starting to know them.

examples.text: I'm learning to speak French by reading lots of French books.

glosses: Learning is the action of someone learning something.

examples.text: Lots of learning happens at school. That's what school is for.

glosses: Someone has something if the thing is in their hands. The person is holding or gripping it.

examples.text: Do you have a spoon, or do you need me to give you one so you can eat the soup?

glosses: If you have to do something, you must do it.

examples.text: I have to go.
John had to pay a fine.

glosses: Someone has something if the thing is that person's thing: the person owns it; it belongs to the person.

examples.text: The rich family has a big house.

glosses: If you have you hold something in the mind.

examples.text: I have a doubt about him.

glosses: If you have you join something.

examples.text: We have lunch at 13:00.

glosses: You use have to say that you suffer from something or to tell the experience.

examples.text: I have a defective vision. (I don't see well.)
He had a wonderful time with his friends.

glosses: You use have to form the perfect.

examples.text: I have closed the window. (Also: I've closed the window.)
I had already eaten before. (Also: I'd already eaten before.)

glosses: A gal is a girl or woman.
Gal is an abbreviation for gallon, which is a unit of measurement for volume.
If you save something, you keep it; you do not give it or toss it away.

examples.text: Please save that book for me.

glosses: If you save someone, you keep them safe or help them survive.

examples.text: You saved my life.

glosses: If you save information, you put it on a disk or into some kind of long-term memory.

examples.text: He saved the resumé on the floppy disk.

glosses: A save is when something was saved. This term is used in sports.

examples.text: Due to a great save at the end, the game ended 0:0.

glosses: All of x save y describes only that part of x that is not y.

examples.text: The night air was still and silent save for the voice of a female dispatcher over his police radio.
All my cats are white, save one.
We know little of her background, save that she was born in Mississauga.

glosses: When you sell something to someone, you give something to someone and the person will give you money for it.

examples.text: I sell good shoes for a small amount money.

glosses: A person

examples.text: I heard someone at the door.
You should ask someone who knows more about it.
I'm hoping to meet someone special at the dance.

glosses: To hear and then fully know what was said, know enough to do it. To know the meaning of something.

examples.text: He understood what I said to him.
She didn't understand. She thought I meant the meeting was today.

glosses: A person moves a comb through their hair many times to make their hair look nice.

examples.text: Joe always had a comb in his pocket.

glosses: To move a comb through hair.

examples.text: I washed and combed my hair.

glosses: To look carefully for something.

examples.text: The police combed the forest for the person but didn't find him.

glosses: A container is full of things if there are many of the things in the container and no more can go in.

examples.text: The cup is full of water. If you try to put more water in, the water will fall onto the table.
My life is full of problems.

glosses: A full moon is when the moon is a round circle because the sun is shining on the side we can see.

examples.text: I can see the road, because there's a full moon tonight.

glosses: A person is full when they are satisfied, usually with food.

examples.text: The meal was so large that I was full all day.

glosses: Something is full when it is total and completed, does not need any additions
The destruction of a thing is the act of breaking the thing; the end of existence of the thing. Before the destruction, the thing is there. After the destruction, there is no thing any more.

examples.text: The destruction of the house was necessary because the walls were not strong and people were not safe from falling bricks.
The earthquake caused a lot of destruction.

glosses: to come before.

examples.text: A precedes B in the alphabet.
More change has happened in the last 20 years than in the preceding 100.
Each of the above exercises should be immediately preceded by taking a deep breath.

glosses: A display is an exhibition, an arrangement, or a show.

examples.text: Mom thought the department store's display of lingerie was indecent.
Little Jimmie toppled the display of model airplanes.
The ceramic, wood, and fabric art displays are very attractive.
Too many displays will confuse our customers.

glosses: A display is a computer screen.

examples.text: The output is visible on the display.

glosses: If you display something, you arrange it so that people can see it. Display means to exhibit, or to show.

examples.text: The players will display their best skills at tonight's game.

glosses: Two people are friends of each other if they like being together and they like helping each other, but are not related.

examples.text: I only have three close friends.
She's been a friend of mine for many years.
Some friends are coming to our house for dinner tonight.
I stayed awake until the middle of the night talking with some friends.
Our house burned down, but some friends helped us build a new one.

glosses: A cushion is a pillow; a soft item that people can sit on or put their head on when they lie down.

examples.text: Here's a bed with sheets, a cushion and a blanket.
Here's a soft chair with two cushions to make it even softer.

glosses: To stop one item from making hard contact with another item.

examples.text: Mats were laid down to cushion the gymnast's fall.

glosses: My favourite brand is the brand I like most.

examples.text: Ford is my favourite brand of truck.

glosses: A favourite is a thing or person that someone likes the most. It is a thing that someone prefers, or likes more than any other.

examples.text: Chocolate ice cream is my favourite.

glosses: When kings and other royalty have favourites, these are people they trust.

examples.text: He was a favourite of the king.

glosses: If you express yourself, you say something about how you feel.

examples.text: Sam expressed his feelings.

glosses: Very fast.

examples.text: To mail the letter, Anna used the express service.

glosses: An incentive is something that makes you feel like you want to do something.

examples.text: Companies should give their workers financial incentives to take the bus to work.
The government is cutting taxes to provide incentives for investment.
Doctors have a lot of incentive to see many patients and little incentive to spend much time with each one.

glosses: When someone makes a comparison between two things, the person thinks about how the two things are the same and how they are different, which one is bigger etc.

examples.text: I need to make some comparisons between different houses before I make a decision about which house to buy.
A careful comparison will show that this cup has a little more water than the other cup.

glosses: An inhibition is a feeling that makes you want to avoid (stay away from) something.

examples.text: He threw off his inhibitions and went dancing.
Alcohol can take away inhibition.
When the cat was absent, the mouse showed no such inhibition.
She stays home all day—she has a lot of inhibitions.
I feel an inhibition about going onto an airplane.

glosses: Inhibition is the act of stopping or reducing a process, especially a natural or chemical process.

examples.text: When there is no sugar, there is inhibition of cell growth.

glosses: A curve is a line that is not straight. It is like part of a circle. It starts in one direction and turns.

examples.text: The edge of the flower petal is a beautiful curve.

glosses: To move in a curve.

examples.text: The car curved around the corner.
This piece of wood is not good. It is curved.

glosses: Copper is a metal that is a red-brown colour. Sometimes coins of small value are made from copper. The symbol for copper is Cu with an atomic number of 29.

examples.text: Water comes into our house through copper pipes.

glosses: A copper is a penny, a coin of small value made of copper.

examples.text: Could you give me a copper? I have almost enough money to buy that thing.

glosses: A copper is a police officer.

examples.text: The copper arrested him for stealing.

glosses: Made of copper.

examples.text: The copper statue has turned green.

glosses: Having the reddish-brown colour/color of copper

examples.text: The copper couch will look really nice with that wallpaper.

glosses: The floor is the flat part at the bottom of a room. People stand on the floor.

examples.text: Don't drop your milk on the floor.
The children are sitting on the floor to play.

glosses: A floor is a level of a building.

examples.text: To get to room 302 you have to go up three floors.

glosses: If you floor a house, you cover or furnish it with a floor.
If you floor when driving, you push the accelerator pedal down to the floor.
A trace of something is a very small amount, almost too small to find.

examples.text: We've found traces of an earlier painting underneath this one.
No trace of the original material remains.
The last trace of cloud had disappeared from the sky.
He said it without a trace of sadness.
The fact that each coin has different trace elements provides clear evidence that they were made at different places.

glosses: A trace is a line on a paper drawn by a machine that shows the ups and downs of something.

examples.text: The trace shows a very irregular heartbeat.

glosses: A trace is a path that tells you where something came from.

examples.text: We've got a trace on the call.
The fox was able to follow the trace the rabbit left on the ground.

glosses: If you trace something, you follow information to find where it came from or where it went.

examples.text: Also, both the church and the farm can trace their origins back to the 1500s.
The police soon traced the couple's movements and found they had made a number of telephone calls to Paris.
The disease has been traced back to some bad eggs.

glosses: If you trace a line, you draw it.

examples.text: He traced a line in the sand.

glosses: If you trace a picture or a shape, you draw it by putting a piece of paper over it and drawing what you see underneath.

examples.text: She traced the Chinese characters carefully, the way you do before you learn to read.

glosses: An exchange is when a person or a group of people trade an item or service with another person or group of people.

examples.text: The children can exchange toys so that each child has a new toy to play with.

glosses: An exchange is the act of exchanging.

examples.text: I did well in that exchange. Now I have three good new books, and I only paid a little money.

glosses: The distance between two things is how far apart they are. A short distance means they're close to each other, and a long distance means they're far apart.

examples.text: The distance from the Earth to the Sun is 93 million miles.
The distance from my house to the store is 2 kilometres.
The two girls were sitting a short distance apart, so they could hear each other whisper.

glosses: If you distance yourself from someone, you move away from something or someone.
Flight is the act of flying: moving through the air using wings.

examples.text: Birds have had flight for millions of years.
The flight of the bird was beautiful.

glosses: A flight is a trip on an airplane.

examples.text: The flight to Boston leaves soon.
This flight is going to New York.

glosses: Flight is the act of running away and hiding.

examples.text: The flight of the man just after the crime made the police think he was guilty.

glosses: A flight is an air force unit.
The part you can see in fire.

examples.text: We saw the flames burning the house.
The firefighter's hat is as bright as a flame.

glosses: A flame is a lover that only lasts for a short time.

examples.text: He brought his flame to yesterday's party.

glosses: A flame is a strong comment on the internet to insult (hurt) someone else, making them angry.

examples.text: Today, someone in our forum started posting very mean flames.
I posted that someone's idea was a bad idea, and I got a lot of flames for that.

glosses: To make flames.

examples.text: The pot in the kitchen started to flame when it was left to cook for too long.

glosses: To write an insulting (hurtful) message on the internet to make people angry.

examples.text: My school peer started flaming in my email.
Everybody in the newsgroup flamed me for saying that.

glosses: To have a fear of someone or something means to be scared of someone or something; to be afraid of someone or something.

examples.text: He was struck with fear when he thought he saw a ghost.
She has a fear of spiders.

glosses: Fear is the chance that something might happen.

examples.text: There's no fear of her being on time. She's always late.

glosses: Fear is a feeling of very high respect, usually towards a god.

examples.text: Christians who worship in churches have a fear of God.

glosses: If a person fears something, they are afraid of it; a person who is scared of something.

examples.text: I fear the worst will happen.
She feared for his safety.

glosses: A person fears something when they’re giving someone bad news.

examples.text: I fear that I am last on Earth.

glosses: If a person fears something, usually a god, you show great respect towards it.

examples.text: Christians in churches fear God.

glosses: Unwise. A person who is foolish does not have good sense or judgement. They do things without thinking carefully; they do things that are bad ideas.

examples.text: The person who saw and copied my homework today is being foolish.

glosses: Foolish means someone who is usually foolish. They have the characteristic (quality) of being foolish.

examples.text: Being foolish once in a while does not make a person a foolish one.

glosses: When something or someone falls, it moves down quickly down through the air because nothing is holding it. It moves to a lower position because of gravity.

examples.text: The apple fell from the tree.
The bridge is falling down.
He tripped on a banana peel and fell down, hurting his leg.

glosses: When someone falls, they can mean coming down to the ground on purpose, lying with the face down.

examples.text: He fell to the floor and begged for mercy.

glosses: Falling is when someone or something has been defeated.

examples.text: The Romans fell to the Goths in 410 AD.

glosses: Fall is the name for autumn used only in North America, named after the falling of leaves during the season. It is the season when the weather is getting colder, after summer and before winter.

examples.text: These plants are growing big and they will be ready to eat in the fall.

glosses: A fall or falls or waterfall is a part of a river where water is falling.

examples.text: We went to the falls to eat lunch outside and watch the water falling.

glosses: A fall is when people suffered a loss of greatness or status, such as the fall of Rome.
A fan is a thing that moves air to help people stay cool; either a small paper thing a person holds in their hand, or a machine with a part that turns fast to push the air.

examples.text: She held the fan in front of her face so people wouldn't see her smile.
Turn on the fan! It's hot here!

glosses: A fan is a person who supports another person or team.

examples.text: John is a fan of that soccer club.
When he kicked the ball into the goal, all his fans cheered loudly.

glosses: To blow air on something, often with a fan.

examples.text: We had to fan ourselves with our programs because it was so hot and crowded in the auditorium.
We enjoyed standing at the edge of the cliff, being fanned by the wind.

glosses: usually to fan out) To move or spread in many directions from one point, similar to the shape of a hand-held fan.
If you fold something thin such as paper, you bend it so it touches itself.

examples.text: A type of art where paper is folded to make different models is called origami.
She folded the letter and put it into the envelope to mail it.

glosses: In poker, if you fold, you stop betting and withdraw.

examples.text: After three people folded, there were only two people left in the game, betting against each other.

glosses: If you fold on ingredient into another, you stir it gently and carefully with a folding action.

examples.text: Fold the egg whites into the batter.

glosses: A fold is a bend or a crease.

examples.text: There was a fold down the middle of the paper.

glosses: A fold is a small place with a fence around it where people keep sheep.

examples.text: After the sheep eat grass all day in the fields, they come home to the fold where it's safe for the night.

glosses: Form is the shape or structure of a person or a thing.
A thing that makes shapes to other things, as in a mold.
A form is a blank document which is to be filled in by a person.

examples.text: To join with the club, please fill in this application form.

glosses: If you form something, you give it shape or structure.
A delicate thing is something that can break easily. It is usually beautiful but people need to be careful if they touch it.

examples.text: Flower petals are delicate.
I don't want a child to hold my delicate glasses.
The things in this box are delicate. Please don't drop them.

glosses: A detail is a small part of something that is not as important as the whole thing.

examples.text: I've written a book, but I still need to change some details in it.
Writing your name at the top of the page is a small detail, but it's important.
This is a very clear picture. You can see every detail.

glosses: A detail is a job or duty.

examples.text: He's on floor-cleaning detail today.

glosses: When someone details something, they tell all the details about it, or record the details.

examples.text: Would you please detail this project for me?

glosses: When two people fight against each other, they hit each other and try to hurt each other.

examples.text: Two children were fighting over a toy, and one child got hurt and started to cry.

glosses: When two people fight against each other, they want different things and they try to get what they want. They might yell, or they might just try hard.

examples.text: When that husband and wife fight with each other, they don't hit. They just yell at each other.
I'm fighting to get more money for the work I do.

glosses: A fight is when people are fighting.

examples.text: There was a fight in the bar last night and three people had to go to the hospital.

glosses: An event is frequent if it happens many times in a short time.

examples.text: Broken toys is the most frequent reason children ask for help here.
Seeing a lion is not a frequent event around here.

glosses: Someone frequents a place if they go there regularly.

examples.text: I frequent some of the restaurants on this street.

glosses: The incidence of something is how often it happens.

examples.text: Regular blood pressure checks would reduce the incidence of heart disease and sudden heart attacks.
There is a surprisingly high incidence of theft in book stores.

glosses: If you hear something, you use your ears to get a sound from it.

examples.text: Are you hearing the music clearly enough, or must I make it louder?

glosses: The act of hearing or the quality of being able to hear.

examples.text: I'm worried about my son's hearing -- maybe his ears were hurt by music that was too loud.
Hearing is necessary to be a sign language interpreter.

glosses: A trial in a court of law or another kind of event where a group listens to people and makes a formal decision.

examples.text: Next week I have an immigration hearing to decide whether I can stay in this country.

glosses: A fowl is a bird: an animal with feathers that can fly, especially a kind that people eat.

examples.text: This farmer keeps sheep and two kinds of fowl: chickens and ducks.

glosses: Something that is feeble is very weak.

examples.text: The old man is feeble.
I was very feeble that day because I was sick.
That's a feeble excuse.
Don't listen to her; she's feeble-minded.

glosses: A parenthesis is a symbol that looks like ( or ). A person may see parentheses when reading books. Most of the time, they are not used to tell the main story, but gives the reader extra information so they can understand.

examples.text: Billy and Bob wrote their papers (Billy wrote about karate, and Bob wrote about dogs).
*The quote inside the parentheses, "Billy wrote about karate, and Bob wrote about dogs", is put inside parentheses because it would be a run-on sentence if there were no parentheses.
*You can also use commas as parentheses, but you need to write the sentence differently.

glosses: A massacre is when many people are killed. This is especially true when those killed appear to be innocent civilians not linked to the war in progress. Very often, the term is also applied if the killings were done in a brutal way.

examples.text: Many people were killed in the My Lai Massacre during the Vietnam War.

glosses: To kill many innocent people without much resistance; to slaughter people.
Something is elastic if it can stretch or bend and go back to the way it was.

examples.text: She held the papers together by putting an elastic (rubber) band around them.
A metal spring is elastic: it gives back the energy that was put into it when it was pushed.

glosses: In a cooperative effort, project, etc., a number of people work together to do something.

examples.text: Development of the machine became a cooperative effort between university and industry in the UK.

glosses: If someone is cooperative, they listen and try to help or work with you.

examples.text: He was very hard to work with, but recently has become much more cooperative.

glosses: A cooperative is a type of business that is owned by the people working there or by its customers.

examples.text: Mountain Equipment Co-op (MEC), a retail co-operative, is Canada's largest supplier of outdoor equipment and has more than two million members.

glosses: If you reveal something, it was hidden and you show it or make it known.

examples.text: A new study reveals that car makers have made little or no gains in fuel economy.
It was revealed yesterday that the president has decided to step down.

glosses: An index is an alphabetical (A to Z) list, usually at the back of a book, where you can find the pages in a book that talk about particular things or words.

examples.text: Look in the index to see where they talk about Chomsky.

glosses: An index shows the level of prices, wages, etc. so you can compare them with those of an earlier date.

examples.text: On Wall Street, the Dow Jones index closed 10 points up at 2,731.23.

glosses: If you index something, you make an index (guide) for it.
If you index something to a certain price level, you make it go up or down with that level.
Discrimination is the act of treating someone unfairly just because of their skin colour, religion, sex, etc.

examples.text: Even in 2007, there's still too much sex discrimination at the higher levels of big business.

glosses: Discrimination is the ability to notice differences.

examples.text: At this small size, discrimination is very difficult.

glosses: Discrimination is the ability to recognise high levels of quality.

examples.text: The clothes were chosen by someone with discrimination.

glosses: If something is overseas, it is in a different country, usually across the ocean.

examples.text: After university she went overseas to teach.

glosses: The overseas markets, students, etc. are in or from a different country, usually across an ocean.

examples.text: Wang is an overseas student from China.
Canada needs to do more for overseas development, especially in Africa.
With the college taking in more overseas students, more attention is being put on language issues.

glosses: Something that goes against the rules in a sport.

examples.text: After a bad foul, a soccer player has to leave the game

glosses: Bad, or having a bad smell.

examples.text: We left the meat too many days, and now it is foul and we can't eat it.
There's a foul smell in the bathroom.

glosses: An event is anything that happens.

examples.text: The event of her walking into the room happened before the event of the book falling off the table, so she saw it fall.
In the event that the machine breaks, read this to know what to do.

glosses: An event is when many people come together at a time they choose for a reason or for fun.

examples.text: At the event tomorrow we're going to have balloons and music.

glosses: A drain is a hole, sometimes in the bottom of a basin, to let water flow out, and a pipe attached to the hole.

examples.text: After you wash, you should drain the water from the bath.

glosses: Someone drains something when they take the water or other liquid out of it.

examples.text: She drained her cup in one gulp.
The workers drained the wet land to make it a dry place to build houses.

glosses: A drawer is a box made of wood that is part of a piece of furniture (such as a desk); drawers can slide in and out so that people can put things into them.

examples.text: I keep my socks in the top drawer of the chest.

glosses: A drawer is a person who draws.

examples.text: Did you draw this picture? Wow, you're a really good drawer.

glosses: A person who writes a bank draft, check, or promissory note.

examples.text: We'll have to have a drawer draw up the promissory note.

glosses: A company is an organization for doing work for money.

examples.text: He works for a big company.
I own this company, so it's a problem for me if people don't buy what we make.

glosses: Company is people who are visiting other people; people who are in other peoples' house so that they can talk to the other people, or people who are walking with other people or being somewhere with other people.

examples.text: I can't talk to you on the phone right now, because I have company. (people in the house.)

glosses: When someone keeps someone else company, they stay with the person.

examples.text: Will you keep me company while I go to mail this letter?

glosses: A company' is a unit of an army, it usually consists of two or three platoons to form a battalion.
A force is the act of a thing pushing on another thing, or how strongly it pushes.

examples.text: The force of the hammer hitting the nail pushes the nail into the wood.
In science, energy is force times distance.
He pushed his shoulder against the door with great force, but was not able to open the locked door.

glosses: A group that aims to attack, control, or constrain.

examples.text: police force

glosses: Someone forces something to happen when they make it happen.

examples.text: He forced his way into the room.
The large size of our family forced me to buy a bigger house.

glosses: Someone who is cruel is mean. They hurt other people and don't care, or they like hurting other people.
