examples.text: The cruel guard pushed the prisoners so hard that some of them fell down.

glosses: An action is cruel if only cruel people would do it.

examples.text: It's cruel to make children work 10 hours a day.

glosses: A miner is a person who works in a mine. They go into a deep tunnel in the earth to get diamonds, coal, silver, gold or other minerals.

examples.text: It was difficult for the miners to come out of the mine after some rocks fell in the tunnel.

glosses: You use x minus y to show that y is taken away from x.

examples.text: Five minus three is two. (5-3=2)
The TV is $299 minus a 10% discount.
The margin of error is plus or minus one per cent.

glosses: A minus sign, negative sign, or minus is the symbol "－". It is used in more than one situation:

examples.text: before a number, to indicate that it is a negative number.
in a math problem 3-1=2 to indicate subtraction.

glosses: A minus is a problem or some negative aspect.

examples.text: He's nice, but the way he dresses is a real minus.

glosses: A nephew is the male child of someone's sister or brother, and is a part of their extended family.

examples.text: My sister just had a baby boy. He is my nephew.

glosses: You need justice when you have been treated unfairly, cheated, hurt, or denied your basic rights by others.
Justice means fairness in how people are treated and how rules are applied. It is the idea that everyone should get what they truly deserve.

examples.text: To have justice means treating every single person the same way, no matter how they look, where they come from, or what they believe.
When someone does something bad to another person, justice ensures the wrong is corrected and the person who caused harm faces the consequences.

glosses: If something is explicit, it is clearly said or shown, not hidden or just suggested.

examples.text: It is very important that the company write an explicit statement of workers' responsibilities.
Sometimes it helps to be more explicit when speaking to children.
The problem is made explicit in the letter sent last July.

glosses: The aggregate is the number or amount when everything is put together.

examples.text: Although demand was up in certain areas, aggregate demand was down.
When each day's time is put together, he's been running for an aggregate of over 762 hours.

glosses: Aggregate is the small stones that are used to make concrete.
If you aggregate something, you put or bring it together.

examples.text: You shouldn't aggregate the various costs. Look at them individually.
The students' income should be aggregated with the parents'.

glosses: A flag is a piece of cloth, usually marked with a colourful symbol or sign.
A flag flown by a ship is to show the presence on board of the admiral (the leader of a group of ships); the admiral himself; or his flagship.
The use of a flag, especially to show the start of a race or other event.

examples.text: Be ready to start running immediately at the flag.

glosses: On a computer, a flag is a variable or place in the computer's memory that keeps a true-or-false, yes-or-no value, usually either recording the fact that a certain event has happened or asking for a certain action to happen if it's an action that doesn't always happen.

In a command line interface (a place on a computer screen for people to type commands for a computer to do), a sign telling the computer to do something it does only sometimes, or a sign changing in some other way the action of the command being typed.
If you mark with a flag, it shows the importance of something.
(often with down) To signal to, especially to stop a car that's driving past, etc.

examples.text: Please flag a taxi down for me.

glosses: When a person flags, the person becomes weak, tired or feeble.

examples.text: His strength flagged toward the end of the race.

glosses: To signal or mark something that happened.

examples.text: The compiler flagged three errors.

glosses: To set the value of a variable in a computer program to true.

examples.text: Flag the debug option before running the program.

glosses: A living thing's gender is its sex: male (man, boy), female (woman, girl), both, or neither.

examples.text: There are gender differences in everything from physical size to play style.
The effects vary considerably according to such factors as class, race and gender.

glosses: Gender is a way of grouping nouns in some languages, for example: masculine, feminine & neuter.

examples.text: In French, the gender affects everything from the choice of le or la to the adjective endings.

glosses: Someone's gender is whether they behave like a boy or girl. This is called masculine or feminine, and not the same as male or female.

examples.text: His gender was not traditional, he was a very feminine boy.

glosses: The gender of a cord, cable, or plug tells how it connects. If it has a hole (a socket) that can be plugged into, it is female. If it plugs into a hole, it is male.

examples.text: The microphone was the wrong gender for the computer's sound card.

glosses: If x underlies y, x causes y; x is the reason for y.

examples.text: Poor education underlies much of the crime and violence in our society.

glosses: If x underlies y, x is the basis for y or the most important part of y.

examples.text: The basic principle underlying the argument is that we can know what each of the parts is.

glosses: If something is brief, it is for a short time.

examples.text: Today there will be brief periods of rain.
Today's meeting should be very brief.
The ceremony included a brief speech by the president.
She arrived when she was 13 months old and, except for one brief period, she never left.
During the brief interview I was asked why I wanted to work for UPS.

glosses: If a piece of clothing such as shorts or a skirt is brief, it is short.

examples.text: One of them was naked, the other wore only a pair of brief shorts.

glosses: A brief is a short piece of writing or a short talk.

examples.text: They've been asked to file briefs, stating why they think the case should not be heard.
My father was at work, reading through a pile of legal briefs.

glosses: Briefs are short underpants.

examples.text: Could you tell whether he was wearing briefs or boxers under his trousers?

glosses: You use in brief to show that you will speak or write in a short way.

examples.text: In brief, the results suggest that coffee is not harmful in small amounts.

glosses: If you brief someone, you tell them the most important information about something.

examples.text: Army General David Petraeus briefed the president on the progress of the plan.

glosses: Dear is something that is precious or greatly valued to someone. They love the thing or the person.

examples.text: My large stamp collection is very dear to me.
Dear George, Thank you for your letter of August 1.

glosses: Dear is something very expensive. It has a higher price; costs a lot of money.

examples.text: That diamond ring is too dear -- we can't buy it.

glosses: A kind, loving person.

examples.text: My cousin is my dear because she gives me flowers very often.

glosses: A domain is a field or area of knowledge or skill, or of where a rule is in force.

examples.text: The question of whether there is a god or not is not within the domain of science.
The copyright is expired and the book is now in the public domain.

glosses: A domain is a large area owned by a person or controlled by a government.

examples.text: The Royal Domain of Drottningholm stands on an island in Lake Mälar in a suburb of Stockholm.

glosses: A domain (name) is a group of internet addresses or URLs that share the same last section (e.g., http://simple.wiktionary.org/wiki/domain is in the wiktionary.org domain.)

examples.text: If you want to set up a web site, the first step is probably to register a domain name such as amazon.com or google.com.

glosses: A sacrifice is something that a person gives up in order to help him or somebody else. A person who makes a sacrifice for a friend will do something that he might not want to do in order to help his friend.
A sacrifice is an offer given as a gift to a god.

examples.text: People in the Old Testament offered a lamb as a sacrifice to God for forgiveness.

glosses: If you sacrifice someone or something, you give them up for other things.
If something is rational, it makes sense and is based on reason.

examples.text: Driving without a seatbelt is simply not rational.
Use of clean fuels is a healthier and more rational approach to meeting our energy needs.
Science is more linear, logical and rational than art.
I don't know what happened, but I'm sure there's a perfectly rational explanation.

glosses: If someone is rational, they are calm and not emotional.

examples.text: It's often difficult to remain rational when people are telling you you're terrible.

glosses: An outer piece of clothing that covers the upper part of the body and the arms.

examples.text: The woman wore a fur coat.
It's cold today, so you need to wear a coat when you go outside.

glosses: A covering of material, such as paint.

examples.text: He applied a thin coat of paint to the wood.

glosses: The fur or feathers of an animal.

examples.text: The bear's coat was thick for the winter.

glosses: Around the mast or bowsprit of a ship, some canvas painted with thick tar to keep water from running down the sides into the hold (now made of rubber).
To cover with a coat (2) of some material

examples.text: A person can buy coated frying pans, which are much easier to wash up than normal ones.

glosses: To cover as a coat (2).

examples.text: Thick paint coated the wall.

glosses: The parts of a building that are strong and that hold the other parts up.

examples.text: Now that the frame is done, we can start on the walls.

glosses: The strong parts (bones) of a person's body.

examples.text: His starved flesh hung on his frame.

glosses: Something, often made of wood, around the outside of a picture.

examples.text: The painting was in a beautifully carved frame.

glosses: The outer part of a stamp's image, usually decorated.
A part of a strip of photographic film, the size of one image.

examples.text: A film projector shows many frames in a single second.

glosses: A way of understanding, a point of view.

examples.text: In this frame, it's easy to ask the question that the investigators missed.

glosses: A game of snooker, from break-off until all the balls have been potted.
A chunk of data sent over the wires of a network.
In bowling, a set of balls whose results are added for scoring.
A division of time on a multimedia timeline, such as 1/30th of a second.
People frame a building when they put together the strong parts while they're building or constructing it.

examples.text: Once we finish framing the house, we'll hang tin on the roof.

glosses: Someone frames a picture such as a painting or photograph when they add a decorative border.
Someone who is taking a picture with a camera frames something when they carefully put it inside the edges of the picture in a nice way.

examples.text: The director frames the fishing scene very well.

glosses: To put together words to make a point of view (way of thinking) for understanding or interpretation.

examples.text: How would you frame your accomplishments?
The way the opposition has framed the argument makes it hard for us to win.

glosses: Someone frames someone else of a crime such as murder that they didn't do when they make things seem as if the person did the crime.

examples.text: He put the gun in her car to try to frame her.

glosses: A condition is a logical clause or phrase that a conditional statement uses. The phrase can either be true or false.
The health status of a medical patient.

examples.text: The doctor will check my condition.

glosses: A problem, especially a medical problem.

examples.text: I told the doctor about my heart condition. My heart is very weak.

glosses: The state of something, meaning how much wear it has.

examples.text: The tires were flat, the windows were broken, and the paint was peeling. The car was in poor condition.

glosses: A condition is something that must be true, happen, or exist before something else can.
To become accustomed to changes in the environment.

examples.text: I became conditioned to the weather in San Diego.

glosses: To subject to different conditions, especially as an exercise.

examples.text: They were conditioning their shins in their karate class.

glosses: Kidney is an organ that is part of the human body. It cleans the blood and makes urine (pee) which is the dirty water that needs to leave the body.

examples.text: Our kidneys are very important organs in our body.
When you drink more water, your kidneys can clean the blood better and make more urine.

glosses: The organ that does the same thing in the body of other animals.
Division is the act of dividing a whole thing into parts.

examples.text: The division of the pie by the children happened with very little fighting.

glosses: Division is the process or calculation of dividing a number by another number.

examples.text: I've got ten divisions to do for my homework.

glosses: Divisions are the parts of something after division.

examples.text: There are four divisions (or sections) in a classical pas de deux.

glosses: A division is a large military unit (group of soldiers)
A division is a section of a large company.

examples.text: This division of GenericTech specializes in the manufacturing of routers.

glosses: When scientists are grouping kinds of animals, a division is a kind of group (Latin divisio) below kingdom and above class.

examples.text: Magnolias belong to the division Magnoliophyta.

glosses: A division is a difference of viewpoint between two sides of an argument.

examples.text: There is a division in the Senate between politicians who support abortions and politicians who do not.

glosses: A division is a piece of music (melody), played with musical instruments, in the 17th and 18th centuries based on another piece.
A division is a set of pipes in a pipe organ.
A division is a concept where a common group of debtors (people who owe money) are only responsible for part of the total debt.
If you close something, you change it from being open to not open.

examples.text: She watched TV for a while, and then closed her eyes.
He left the room and softly closed the door behind him.
He opened his mouth and closed it again without saying anything.

glosses: If something closes, it goes out of business for a short time or permanently.

examples.text: The supermarket closes at 5 o'clock on Saturday.
Sadly, we have decided to close the shop.

glosses: If the distance or time between two different things closes, they get closer together.

examples.text: The government will use the $15 million to close a budget gap.
With only three games left in the season, Milan is closing in on Hamburg.
The storm was closing in, and she wanted to get home.

glosses: If something closes, it ends.

examples.text: The book closes with the man alone in the house where he started.
I'd like to close this talk by asking for your help.

glosses: If a stock, bond, or currency closes at a certain price, it is at the price at the end of the trading day.

examples.text: The EAP Emerging Growth Fund lost half a dollar, closing at just over $38.
Again today, cigarette company stocks closed up.

glosses: If you close a deal/sale/contract, both people make a final agreement.

examples.text: It took five months, many phone calls, and an extra $89,000 to close the deal.

glosses: If you close up, you stop talking about something.

examples.text: Every time I asked about the cost everybody would close right up.

glosses: When two things are close, they are near each other; the distance or time between them is small.

examples.text: The bank is close to the store.
I walk to my university because it is very close.
It's close to nine o'clock.
Closer to the end, I'll come and get you.
Put it close to the door.
She left an hour ago, and he was very close behind.
I like to keep my phone close at hand so I can get it quickly.
They stood close together.

glosses: If two people are close, they have a good relationship, like friends, family or lovers.

examples.text: She was quite close to her dad before he died.

glosses: If a game or contest is close, you can't easily see which side is better.

examples.text: The race has been very close up until now.

glosses: If two things are close, they are similar.

examples.text: This is the closest thing I could find to that colour.

glosses: Close range/contact/ties etc. is near, not far.

examples.text: They tell us the gun was fired at close range.
Most Norwegians live in close contact with the wilderness, the sea, the mountains, or the forests.

glosses: A close look, watch, or eye means careful attention.

examples.text: Keep a close eye on the money.

glosses: In a close game/race/competition, etc., the difference between the scores/times/abilities, etc is small.

examples.text: One or two points can win or lose a close race .
The winner earned 13.8 percent of the vote, but she was a close second (13.5 percent).

glosses: If something was close, something bad/dangerous/embarrassing, etc. almost happened.

examples.text: Wow, that was close. She almost saw us.
Thirty years ago this week, our country had a very close call.

glosses: The close of something is the end.

examples.text: I will be surprised if the company is still running by close of business tomorrow.
The book was written around the close of the 14th century.
As our first week came to a close, we were getting very tired.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of fix.

examples.text: The mechanic fixed my car.
The mother fixed the broken toy.
The meeting of Congress is fixed on January 3.
The mechanic has fixed all of the problems.

glosses: When something is fixed, it didn't work before, but now it works; when something has been repaired.

examples.text: Is your car fixed yet?

glosses: If an animal has been fixed, it had an operation to stop it from having babies.

examples.text: After a male cat is fixed, it doesn't fight with other cats as much.

glosses: If a game, contest, or election is fixed, somebody unfairly controls what will happen before it is over.

examples.text: Don't go to that casino, the roulette wheel is fixed.

glosses: Attacked or punished.

examples.text: When we find out who squealed on our roulette wheel, they're going to get fixed.
Don't go into my room, or I'll fix you!

glosses: Protected from arrest.

examples.text: Don't worry about it, we're fixed with the cops.

glosses: Not changing, not able to be changed, staying the same.

examples.text: fixed assets
fixed cost

glosses: We measure an angle using degrees. All the way around a circle is 360 degrees. Often, ° is written instead of "degrees".

examples.text: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 90 degrees.

glosses: We measure how hot or how cold it is (temperature) using degrees on a scale, such as Celsius or Fahrenheit.

examples.text: It's going to be 35 degrees Celsius today.

glosses: The amount that an object has of a certain quality.

examples.text: To what degree do the two accounts of the accident agree?

glosses: Any units used to measure specific gravity, bitterness, darkness, etc. in manufacturing commodities.
An award (usually better than a diploma but not as good as a doctorate) given by a university or, in some countries, a college

examples.text: After four years at university, she got her degree.

glosses: The number of edges that a vertex is part of.

examples.text: The corner of a cube is of degree 3, but the corners of an eight-sided solid have degree 4.

glosses: The act of growing (getting bigger); an increase in size, number, value, or strength.

examples.text: I'm pleased with the growth in value of our house in the years after we bought it.

glosses: Something that grows or has grown; a mass that is not normal, such as a tumor.

examples.text: There was a healthy growth of bushes near the house.
He died of a growth in his brain.

glosses: A strong dislike someone feels for something. Disgust is an emotion. People feel it, for example, when they find something dirty or not fit to eat.

examples.text: With an air of disgust, she stormed out of the room.
When she saw the meat that was ten days old, she felt a strong disgust.

glosses: To cause a strong dislike for something.

examples.text: It disgusts me, to see her chew with her mouth open.

glosses: If you are dependent on something, you need it or rely on it.

examples.text: Ocean divers are dependent on their oxygen masks for air.

glosses: A dependent is a person who relies on another person for support.

examples.text: With two children and an ailing mother, she had three dependents in all ... (In British English, this meaning is spelt dependant.)

glosses: A dependent is an element in a phrase or clause that is not the head.
The present participle of drive.

examples.text: The man driving the truck went to the run-down weigh station.
In the European Union, driving on the right side of the road is normal.

glosses: If something is driving, it is moving quickly and strongly.

examples.text: The driving wind blew the rain sideways.

glosses: someone or something that guides.
a document or book that offers information or instruction; guidebook.
a sign that guides people; guidepost.
any marking or object that catches a person's attention for quick reference.
a device that guides part of a machine, or guides motion or action.
a spirit thought to speak through a medium.
a member of a group marching in formation who sets the pattern of movement for the rest.
to serve as a guide for someone or something.
to steer or navigate.
to use control or influence over someone or something.
to supervise the education of someone.
To act as a guide.
Developing; growth

examples.text: The development of this story has been slow.
The organism has reached an important part in its development.

glosses: Something which has developed

examples.text: Our news team brings you the latest developments.

glosses: A real estate development.
Using new ideas for practical problems.

examples.text: Our development department has created three new adhesives this year.

glosses: The active placement of the pieces, or the process of doing it

examples.text: White's development is good, but black's has been hampered by the pawn on e5.

glosses: The minimum is the lowest number, size, amount, etc. that exists, that is allowed, or that is possible.

examples.text: Try to keep drinking to a minimum at school.
A minimum of three workers is needed to do the job.

glosses: A distance in space or in time.

examples.text: There is a ten-minute interval between classes.

glosses: In music, an interval is the difference in pitch between two notes.
In mathematics, an interval is a connected section of the real line.
(mostly British) An intermission.
In the game of cricket, either of the two breaks, at lunch and tea, between the three sessions of a day's play.
A rigid object does not bend.

examples.text: It's possible to use flexible materials to form a rigid structure.

glosses: fixed rather than moving
rigorous and unbending
uncompromising
Flexibility is the quality of being able to give yourself a blowjob.

examples.text: Current technology allows for greater flexibility in how we do our jobs.

glosses: An author is the creator of a work; a writer.

examples.text: I am the author of this article. I was the one who wrote it.

glosses: An author is a source of information.
If you author something, you create a work as its author.

examples.text: Did you read that article that John authored? It was poorly written.

glosses: If you have or take the initiative, you are in control and can decide what to do next.

examples.text: It's good to see someone take the initiative and start doing something about this problem.
It appears that the army was acting on its own initiative and not on orders from the president.

glosses: If you have initiative, you do things without needing to be told to do them.

examples.text: We're looking to hire somebody with initiative because I won't be able to supervise them much.

glosses: An initiative is an effort to start doing something to solve a problem.

examples.text: The town has no new initiatives to deal with garbage.

glosses: If something will happen eventually, it will happen but it will be in the future, not soon. Some day it will happen.

examples.text: I'll clean out my closet eventually.
Eventually we'll find a better way to do this.

glosses: An event that is forthcoming is something that will happen soon. It's coming in a short time.

examples.text: The forthcoming publication of her book will help her get status and respect.

glosses: A person who is forthcoming is someone who tells what they're thinking.

examples.text: I asked him what his plans are for next year but he wasn't very forthcoming.

glosses: When something is crucial, it is very important. It will make a big difference. You cannot succeed without it.

examples.text: To write a great book, it's crucial to have the person in the book change and develop.
It was a crucial time in the battle when the king dropped his sword.
The development of this company is at a crossroads, and we need to make some crucial decisions.
Iron plays a crucial role in moving oxygen around the body.
The new doctor was crucial to the success of the operation.

glosses: An allocation is the amount that is given out or shared.

examples.text: Our department's allocation of computer time is too small.
We need to increase the allocation of funds to fix the roads problem.

glosses: Allocation is the act of giving out or sharing something.

examples.text: The budget allocations are becoming less and less frequent.
With the new focus on the environment, governments are rethinking their resource allocation plans.
The broad allocation of contracts means that we don't depend on any one company.

glosses: If x exceeds y, x is or becomes larger or better than y.

examples.text: The company's 2005 revenue exceeds that of 2004.
The quality of her essay exceeded my expectation.

glosses: If you exceed something, you go beyond (farther than) the limits, beyond the regular level or beyond what is allowed.

examples.text: Your user name may not exceed eight characters.
The length of the soldier's hair exceeds the allowed length.

glosses: An intervention is an activity designed to change or stop a situation.

examples.text: To prevent government intervention, the companies agreed to stop advertising cigarettes.
The teachers planned a reading intervention for the students who were having trouble.

glosses: Someone is definite if they are sure. They have no doubt about what they're saying.

examples.text: She was definite that this is the right place.

glosses: Something is definite if it has defined limits.
An identified person or thing
Acting of one's own free will. Something that somebody does is voluntary if the person is doing it because they want to do it, not because someone orders them to do it.

examples.text: Helping to wash the dishes is voluntary.

glosses: Working without payment.

examples.text: I have a voluntary position helping children learn to read.

glosses: If someone releases something, they let go of it; they stop holding it and set it free (let it be free).

examples.text: He released his grasp on the lever.
He was released after two years in prison.

glosses: Someone releases something when they put it out into the world (discharge it).

examples.text: They released thousands of gallons of water into the river each month.

glosses: A company releases something when they let the public start using it.

examples.text: They released the new product later than they wanted to.

glosses: To lease again; to agree to a new lease of; to let back, sublet or rent again.

examples.text: I leased the house from the owner, and released it for a year to another person.

glosses: In software, a version of something that is put up for sale or that the public can use.

examples.text: The video store advertised that it had all the latest "releases".

glosses: That which is released, untied or let go.

examples.text: They marked the occasion with a release of butterflies.

glosses: Wealth is when one has a lot of money. Wealth is a lot of money or a lot of things of high value like land, houses, factories, jewelry, etc.

examples.text: His wealth is so great that he wears new shoes every day.

glosses: A holy war is a war fought for religious reasons. Examples include jihad and crusades.

Something collapses when all its parts fall down loosely. A building or a bridge collapses when it breaks and all its parts fall down. A person collapses when they are tired and they fall into a chair or onto a bed and are too tired to get up.

examples.text: He was so tired, he just collapsed onto that chair.
The bridge collapsed, but no one was hurt.

glosses: The act of collapsing.

examples.text: The collapse of the bridge means we can't go over the river any longer.

glosses: A colleague is a person who works together with another person or who does the same kind of work.

examples.text: I like to talk about the science with my colleagues from the other university.

glosses: If you levy a charge or a tax, you legally make people pay it.

examples.text: The government levies a tax on all wood entering the country.

glosses: A levy is an extra charge on top of the basic price, usually a tax.

examples.text: The levy on fuel went up this year.

glosses: Someone drafted or conscripted into military service.
When x is true, and nonetheless y is true, then x being true didn't stop y from being true.

examples.text: It's raining, but we're going to eat outside nonetheless.
The British were very interested in starting talks. Nonetheless, it was the Americans who actually got things organised.

glosses: Integrity is the quality of being honest and of doing only good things.

examples.text: I liked the integrity she showed when she wouldn't let someone from the other company pay for her lunch.

glosses: Integrity is the quality of being whole, not broken.

examples.text: We need to test the integrity of the bridge.

glosses: Tonight is the night that comes between today and tomorrow.

examples.text: Tonight is when the party is scheduled.
We will talk tonight.

glosses: The plural form of second; more than one (kind of) second.

examples.text: The clock shows the seconds.

glosses: A second serving of food for one person.

examples.text: I'm so hungry that I'm going back for seconds.
This tastes so good. I hope there's enough for us to have seconds.

glosses: Seconds is the present third person singular of second.

examples.text: If Bill seconds the motion, I'll vote for it.

glosses: Today is the current day, the day that is happening now, the day between yesterday and tomorrow.

examples.text: Today is the first day of the rest of your life.
I have classes today.
Today's meeting should be short.

glosses: Today is modern times; the present in general.

examples.text: Today we don't have many of the old problems but we have many new ones.

glosses: Too means to a higher degree than is desirable, permissible, or possible; excessively.

examples.text: You can't come in. You are too dirty.

glosses: Too means in addition; also.

examples.text: "It's nice to meet you." "It's nice to meet you, too."
I speak Japanese and Korean too.
I like it, and she likes it too.

glosses: An ordinal number, scale, or variable gives the order.

examples.text: "Fifth" is an ordinal number.

glosses: An ordinal number such as first, second and third.
A group of people who came together for an event.

examples.text: She stood in front of the assembly and started to talk.

glosses: The act of people or things coming together.

examples.text: It took a few minutes for the assembly of everything she needed to bring with her.

glosses: The act of making something by putting parts together.

examples.text: We bought a desk, but we didn't know it needed assembly at home.

glosses: If x has adjacent y, there is no other thing between x and y.

examples.text: The house has an adjacent garage.
It's a lovely room, complete with adjacent shower and rest area.
In the word "house", the letters "h" and "o" are adjacent.

glosses: If x is adjacent to y, there is no other thing between x and y.

examples.text: The cinema was immediately adjacent to our house, so that every night we could hear the film.

glosses: A small coin of little value, also called a penny; 100 cents make a dollar.

examples.text: This gum only costs five cents.

glosses: If something is straightforward, it is simple. It is easy to understand and easy to know how to do it.

examples.text: The instructions for how to put this desk together are straightforward.
What we need to do now is straightforward.
Making tea is pretty straightforward.

glosses: Huge; very big; very large.

examples.text: That's the most enormous watermelon I've ever seen.
Elephants are enormous animals.

glosses: x is intrinsic to y if x is an important part of y. y must always have x as a part.

examples.text: Being able to think is intrinsic to being human.
Finding a way to stop being angry is intrinsic to the problem of making your life better.
Food has intrinsic value, while gold only has value because other people want it.

glosses: The time something takes, or how much time it takes.

examples.text: In the duration of his speech, ten more people came into the room
The duration of this event will be three hours.
For the duration of the work painting the rooms, you'll have to sleep in a different room.

glosses: by which; because of which

examples.text: This hammer is the tool whereby I hammered in that nail.
Learning is the method whereby we improve our minds.

glosses: Someone has an inclination to do something if the person wants to do it or often does it.

examples.text: I have an inclination to eat some ice cream right now.
He has an inclination to forget his umbrella at other peoples' houses.

glosses: Something has an inclination if it's on a slant or angle.

examples.text: The inclination of the road was just enough to make the car roll by itself.

glosses: The fifth thing is something that is number five (5) in order.
A fifth of something is one of five equal parts of that thing.

examples.text: Three is one fifth of fifteen.

glosses: A fifth of an alcoholic drink is a bottle of it.

examples.text: They drank a fifth of vodka last night.

glosses: A user is someone who uses something.
A user is someone with an account and username that lets them log in to a computer and do things on the computer.
A motto is a favorite phrase or saying, often telling a principle or belief. Individuals and groups can have mottos.

examples.text: "Early to bed and early to rise" is a motto.

glosses: A protocol is a rule, guideline, or document about how certain activities are done.

examples.text: I don't know the protocol for talking to the President.

glosses: A protocol is a set of rules that describes how data is transmitted.

examples.text: To get the domain name from the domain name server, the other computer has to send the right protocol.

glosses: Something overlaps on another thing if part of it is on top of, or at the same time as, the other thing.

examples.text: The shingles of a roof need to overlap to keep rain out.
The shifts of the two workers (periods of time when they're working) need to overlap so that one worker can tell the other one what is happening.

glosses: The act of overlapping. The amount that two things overlap on each other.

examples.text: More overlap keeps the rain out better, but needs more shingles to cover the roof.

glosses: Someone attains a status if they reach it and start to have that status.

examples.text: My brother attained first place in the race.
After 4 years at university, she attained her degree.

glosses: A sphere is a shape that is round in all directions, like a ball. Every point on a sphere is the same distance from the centre (a point in the middle) of the sphere.

examples.text: The Earth is almost exactly a sphere.
A drop of water can be a sphere while it's falling.

glosses: A route is the way someone goes from one place to another place.

examples.text: Could you tell me a route to the store from here?
The road was rough. I should have taken a different route.

glosses: To send something or someone on a specific route.

examples.text: While the road was being fixed, the workers routed the cars along a different road.
This computer routes email to the main computer.

glosses: Arrogance is an attitude that someone may have that he/she is better than other people.

examples.text: He treats us so badly because he is full of arrogance.

glosses: The background is what can be seen or heard behind other things that are closer or louder.

examples.text: I was talking to Mary, but I heard the phone ringing in the background.
The play was good, and I especially liked the backgrounds that were used.

glosses: The background of a person is his/her history.

examples.text: The police checked his background to see if he had been in jail.

glosses: To make a background.
If you blank something, you make it empty.
If a piece of paper or something else is blank, it has nothing written on it.

examples.text: I asked Bill for a blank piece of paper, but he gave me one with writing on it.
I thought he would sign the check, but he left it blank.
The computer screen was completely blank because the computer was off.

glosses: A blank is a space or line on a piece of paper or somewhere else where a word or phrase is supposed to be.

examples.text: Fill in the blanks on the legal form.

glosses: A blank is a cartridge that contains gunpowder but does not have a bullet. It used usually used for training or as a signal.
When there is a controversy about something, people don't agree about it and there is a lot of talking about it.

examples.text: There's a controversy about whether cars should be allowed to drive in this part of the city.
Newspapers love to write about controversies.

glosses: A simulation of an event is when people make something that looks like the event happening, but it isn't real.

examples.text: Before we watched them land on the moon, we watched a simulation so we would know what it would look like.
Doctors sometimes learn surgery in a simulation of a real operation.
To make movies you have to set up a lot of simulations.

glosses: A part of something that is natural and cannot be separated from it.

examples.text: There may be problems inherent in hiring part-time staff.
Everybody understands the inherent value of education.

glosses: Period from midday to sunset.
Very bad. So bad that people don't want to think about it.

examples.text: When all the children were crying, it was just awful.

glosses: When two people agree about something, they have the same ideas. They both think the same things are true.

examples.text: We agree that it will probably rain this afternoon.

glosses: When two people agree to do some things, they say something like "if you do this, then I will do that." After they agree, then they must do the things they said.

examples.text: We agreed to pay him $100 to paint the walls.

glosses: When something moves away from something else, the distance between them gets bigger. They are no longer near or close.

examples.text: Go away! You're bothering me.
Keep the machine away from water.
The store is far away from my house.

glosses: If Dan is arrogant, he thinks he is better or more important than other people.

examples.text: He is arrogant and that is why he is rude.
When you walked past her without talking to her, she thought you were being arrogant.

glosses: Somebody who is deaf, cannot hear or cannot hear well.

examples.text: She did not hear what I was saying because she's deaf.

glosses: Someone with deafness cannot hear or cannot hear well.

examples.text: My mother's deafness keeps her from hearing me.
Getting sick with the measles can cause deafness.

glosses: A niece is the female child of someone's sister or brother and is a part of their extended family.

examples.text: My brother has a daughter. She is my niece.

glosses: A partisan is a person who is a supporter of a political party, or of an idea. He or she may also be militant, ready to use force to fight for his or her cause.

Savoury means "not sweet". Food that is savoury does not taste sweet. The savoury course of a meal may have meat or fish and vegetables. This may be followed by a sweet course (called "pudding" or "dessert").
"Savour" can also mean the characteristic taste of something. It can also mean to enjoy something: "He savoured every moment of it".
To purge an organization or an object means to clean it up of something bad.

examples.text: His attempt to purge our country of minorities was met with international criticism.

glosses: When a purge occurs, an organization or an object is cleaned up of something bad.

examples.text: His purge of our country's minorities was met with international criticism.

glosses: If something is visible, it can be seen.

examples.text: The car had no visible signs of damage.
Many stars that are not visible in the city are still visible from the countryside.
Mount Fuji is clearly visible from Tokyo after a rain storm.
Italy has an active and highly visible environmental movement.

glosses: If something is finite, it has a limit. It doesn't keep going forever.

examples.text: This problem has a finite number of correct answers.
There is a finite amount of energy in the universe.

glosses: Publication is the act of making a book or other thing publicly known or available where the public can use it.

examples.text: The Report itself and the debate that followed its publication have been useful.
This letter is personal and not for publication.

glosses: A publication is a book, magazine, paper, song, etc. that has been or will be published.

examples.text: Women's Strategies from Around the World, is a new publication from the United Nations Development Fund for Women (UNIFEM).

glosses: A disturbance is an uneasy feeling.
To disturb means to stop someone or something by interrupting them.
Clumsiness is a lack of coordination; it is the condition of being clumsy.
A thesis is a long paper that university students at the masters or doctoral level write.

examples.text: I finished my coursework and have been working on my thesis for about a year now.
She's writing her thesis on the effects of TV on children.

glosses: A thesis is a main idea or argument that is developed or explained.

examples.text: This book has three major theses.
If you're going to write about this, you're going to have trouble supporting your thesis.

glosses: The plural form of knife; more than one (kind of) knife.

examples.text: I keep all my knives in the kitchen.
Which of these knives should I use to chop the onions?

glosses: If you set something somewhere, you put something into a place.

examples.text: She sets the lamp on the floor.
I was setting glasses on the table when I heard a noise.

glosses: If you set something, you put it into some state or condition.

examples.text: After changing the batteries, you have to set the clock again.
They set the house on fire
His utter naturalness at once set me at ease.
He sets the CD player to play.
The guard had never set a prisoner free before.

glosses: If you set something, you define it or to fix its value.

examples.text: The teacher set a time limit of two minutes for this exercise.
The date for the exam was set to next Thursday.
The microwave was set to 400 watts.

glosses: If you set the table, you put dishes, forks and knives on it.

examples.text: I set the table for five people, but only three came.

glosses: When the sun or moon sets, it moves toward the horizon.

examples.text: The sun sets every evening.

glosses: If something sets, it dries and becomes solid.

examples.text: The concrete needs to set before a car can drive on it.
This glue needs two hours to set.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of set.
Something that is set is fixed. It cannot be changed easily.

examples.text: Don't argue! The rules are set.
The time for the race is set.

glosses: To be ready for something.

examples.text: Are you set?

glosses: The set is the scenery for a theatrical work such as a play, ballet, musical, etc.

examples.text: The Metropolitan Opera's set for Aida is spectacular.
I was painting a wall on the set when the director arrived.

glosses: A set is a group of things that are similar or can be used together.

examples.text: This chess set is too expensive to play chess with it.
I have a set of porcelain figurines depicting characters from Shakespeare's plays.

glosses: A set is a group of things, where every single one of them has a certain purpose. All of them are needed to perform a certain operation.

examples.text: To play poker, you need a set of playing cards and chips.
A mason has a set of tools.

glosses: Persons that have something in common may be called a set.

examples.text: That rich chick is a member of the Jet Set.
Girls who wear sweaters on Wednesday in my school belong to the sweater set.
The Long Island Horsey Set plays polo on weekends.

glosses: A set is a machine which gets radio or television programs.

examples.text: This television set is broken.
This radio set can receive programs from Australia.

glosses: In many sports, a number of sets make up a game. An example of this would be in tennis or table tennis.

examples.text: The tennis player won the first two sets, but lost the game.

glosses: A dull yellowish-brown color, the color of dust.
A strong cloth that is made of wool or cotton; khaki is often used for making military uniforms.
Being dust-coloured.
When someone invokes a rule, they use the rule in a specific situation.

examples.text: For the government to do that legally, they would have to invoke the "notwithstanding" clause of the constitution.

glosses: The past tense and past participle of invoke.
When a rule is invoked, it is being used in a specific situation.

examples.text: That rule was not invoked during that meeting.

glosses: When someone does something likewise, they do it the same way someone else did it. Sometimes people say likewise to mean that they're saying the same thing someone else just said.

examples.text: I used one of the little spoons to eat my soup, and my friend did likewise.
"I'm happy to see you!" "Likewise!"

glosses: When someone uses the word "so-called" to talk about something, they mean that other people talk about the thing that way, but they don't agree.

examples.text: When are we going to leave this so-called party? (The person saying this thinks it should not be called a party. Probably they think the party is not fun.)

glosses: If something is brilliant, it gives off a lot of light.

examples.text: It was evening with the brilliant colors of sunset shining through the trees.
The sun's light was so brilliant that I needed to close my eyes.
The sky was a brilliant blue that day, and the air was cold.
He noticed a brilliant star in the sky.

glosses: If something is brilliant, it is very good.

examples.text: Truly brilliant ideas can sound crazy at first.
She wrote a book about her brilliant career in television.

glosses: If a person is brilliant, they are very intelligent.

examples.text: He was a brilliant teacher.

glosses: Disposal is the act of getting rid of or throwing out something.

examples.text: There is no long-term plan for nuclear waste disposal.
After a strange package was found, bomb disposal workers were called in.

glosses: If you have something at your disposal, it is available for you to use.

examples.text: Some of the students seem to have a lot of money at their disposal.

glosses: You use solely to say that somebody or something is the only one like that or that did it.

examples.text: It is not good for a country to rely solely on one energy source.
You are solely responsible for this problem.

glosses: If you deny something, you say it didn't happen or isn't true.

examples.text: He denied charges that Vietnamese troops participated in the fighting.
There can be no denying that the Cobra is an extremely exciting car to drive.
The report that came out earlier today has been denied by the White House.

glosses: If you deny somebody something, you stop them from having or doing it.

examples.text: A quick dive by the goal keeper denies Beckham the goal.
Why would you go to work and deny yourself a little rest?

glosses: A bear is a big animal with a short tail. They either eat only meat or meat and plants. There are many different types of bears, for example brown bears and polar bears.

examples.text: Polar bears are white.
Grizzly bears live in North America.

glosses: Someone who acts rough and lacks manners could be called a bear.
A large, hairy, homosexual man is called a bear.
If x bears y, x holds y up.

examples.text: This wall bears half the weight of the roof.
The chieftain bears a spear.

glosses: If someone bears something bad, they accept it or deal with it.

examples.text: He has to bear insults because of his appearance.
I cannot bear looking at the news.
The pain is so bad, I can hardly bear it.

glosses: If a baby is born, it comes out of its mother.

examples.text: The woman bore a little boy.
He was born on October 22, 1983.

glosses: If something is born, it is newly created.

examples.text: This idea was born out of boredom.

glosses: If something bears fruit, flowers, etc., it grows them.

examples.text: This apple tree is 100 years old, it does not bear apples anymore.

glosses: If x bears y, x holds y on the surface.

examples.text: Peter bears a small scar on his forehead.
The flag bore a white lion.
The sign bears the words "Hey there!".

glosses: If something is big, it is large in size; tall, wide, long, or fat.

examples.text: He's bigger than me.
I would like a big glass of milk.
The tree was so big that you could see it over the top of the house.

glosses: If something is big, it is important.

examples.text: That's a big problem!

glosses: Someone's big brother or a big sister is one who is older than the person.

examples.text: I have a big brother who's stronger than you!

glosses: Big; of great size; broad, tall, wide, long, or fat.

examples.text: I would like a large glass of milk.
I need a larger piece of paper to fit all these pictures onto it.

glosses: Someone compiles some things or ideas when they bring them together into one place.

examples.text: I need to compile a list of reasons not to go ahead with the project.
She compiled a good set of books to read about the history of that place.

glosses: A panel is a flat piece of wood or other material, used as part of a wall or on the side of something.

examples.text: The house has aluminium panels covering the outside.

glosses: A panel is a group of people who come together at a table to talk or to judge, usually in front of many other people.

examples.text: The panel made a decision that Paul had won the dance contest.
I went to listen to a panel talking about global warming.

glosses: To put panels on something.
A device is a small machine or tool.

examples.text: She has a device in her kitchen for cutting garlic.

glosses: A device is a machine or part attached to a computer, such as a keyboard, mouse, printer etc.

examples.text: The mouse is an important device for using the computer.

glosses: A device is a clever way of doing something.
A device is a logo.
When something hasn't happened yet, it didn't happen, but it might happen in the future.

examples.text: Is she there yet?

glosses: Used to join words, phrases, and clauses that contrast.

examples.text: It's cold outside, yet I don't see you wearing a coat.
I've never tried so hard yet accomplished so little.

glosses: If something is ambiguous, it has more than one possible meaning, state, or explanation.

examples.text: I think he fills his speeches with ambiguous words on purpose.
The goal of the challenge remains rather ambiguous.

glosses: Something is ongoing if it's continuing to happen without stopping in one long period of time.

examples.text: The growth of bones is still ongoing at age 12.
The development of the new way of doing this is ongoing.

glosses: If you can conceive of a certain situation, you can imagine it.

examples.text: I just can't conceive of life without you.
Can you conceive what life would have been like in that time?

glosses: Someone conceives of an idea when they think of the idea for the first time, and it's their idea: they thought of it themselves, no one told them.

examples.text: The planners first conceived of the idea of making a large, curved building here in 1998.
I can't conceive of any way of getting there before 5:00.

glosses: A woman conceives a baby when she becomes pregnant (starts to carry a tiny baby inside her).

examples.text: The baby was conceived the day we went to Niagara Falls.

glosses: If something is true notwithstanding something else, it is true in spite of that other thing.

examples.text: We're going ahead with the event as planned, notwithstanding the heavy rain and wind.
He's really a terrible man, his excellent work notwithstanding.
Notwithstanding, the problem is a significant one.
You live an eternal life notwithstanding that your seat of consciousness is currently physical.

glosses: If you submit something, usually a piece of writing, you give it to somebody to be checked or accepted.

examples.text: They submitted their final report together with recommendations to the president.
Students will submit their application with examples of work already done by March 31.

glosses: If you submit to some authority, you accept that they have power over you.

examples.text: At least up to 1985, the British government submitted to the threat of violence from the terrorists.
Although most people submit willingly to this process, very few of them have any choice in the matter.

glosses: A consonant sound made by vibrating the tongue against the part of the mouth where the sound is being made, looser than a fricative such as "s" in "sit", but tighter than an approximant such as "w" in "well".

examples.text: The word arroz, meaning "rice", contains the alveolar trill (trill made on the roof of the mouth).

glosses: a little, not very

examples.text: What happens in the classroom can be somewhat different from the lesson plan.
She was somewhat surprised to find her name in the morning paper.
His guitar playing has changed somewhat since the band's first CD.
That's somewhat of a problem.

glosses: If something is empirical, it is based on or can be checked by observation or experience.

examples.text: Simply because there is no empirical evidence to support this does not mean it's wrong. It simply means we haven't looked hard enough.
This hypothesis has been challenged on both theoretical and empirical grounds.

glosses: A phenomenon is a fact or event that you can observe (see or hear or sense), especially one that is not fully understood.

examples.text: But this explanation is not enough to explain the observed phenomena.
Football violence is not a particularly new phenomenon, and it isn't only a British problem.
These scientists study such phenomena as storms and changing climate.

glosses: A phenomenon is a person, show, book, etc. that is very popular.

examples.text: 'N Sync was something of a pop music phenomenon in the late 90s.
Snakes as pets are not a new phenomenon, but they do seem to be growing more popular.

glosses: A patriarchy is a society where the oldest male is considered to be the leader of the household.
Italics are a style of letters written slanted. In English, they are usually used for stressing a word in a sentence or for foreign words.

examples.text: The sentences written in italics have been added or changed.

glosses: Italics are a style of letters written slanted. In English, they are usually used for stressing a word in a sentence or for foreign words.

examples.text: The sentences written in italics have been added or changed.

glosses: You use via to mean the path that something takes when it goes somewhere (the places it goes through before it gets there).

examples.text: We can send video, audio and data from any point in the UK, via satellite.
This became part of our route from Liverpool to Manchester via Runcorn.
John sent the message to Yoko via Hamid.

glosses: etc. is short for et cetera.
Et cetera means "and more of the same kind of thing". It is often written etc.

examples.text: There are pens, pencils, paper, etc., in the bag.
1, 2, 3, et cetera.

glosses: A hundredth of a meter; 100 centimeters is one meter.

examples.text: This pencil is 18 centimeters long.

glosses: If you break something, you make it come apart in a way that cannot easily be put back together, usually by force.

examples.text: He injured his leg and broke his foot during the crash.
When my brother died, my family broke apart.
The airplane broke apart in the sky over Hawai'i.
When the ice broke underneath me, I said to myself, I'm in trouble.

glosses: If something such as a machine breaks, it stops working because something is wrong.

examples.text: My car breaks down about once a week.

glosses: If you break a law, rule, promise, etc. you do something that you should not do.

examples.text: The police can't do anything if no laws are broken.
These are the rules. Don't break the rules and I won't send you home.

glosses: If you break a surface, limit, record, etc., you go beyond it.

examples.text: In 1954 he set a new record of 3:59.4, breaking the old record by more than five minutes.
Wilson broke barriers for women in journalism at a time when newsrooms were mostly male.

glosses: If you break free or out of something, you could not leave but now you leave.

examples.text: The police are looking for some prisoners who broke out of the jail.
One of the dogs broke loose and ran at her.
When she closed the door, everyone broke into laughter.

glosses: If you break, you stop for a short time to rest.

examples.text: We break for coffee at 10:00 every morning.

glosses: If day or morning breaks, it begins.

examples.text: The day was breaking as they packed up the tent.
Dawn was just breaking when Helga Schneider climbed out of bed.

glosses: If you break something, you stop it suddenly.

examples.text: The sound of the door closing broke the silence.
I didn't know my father, but with my son, I want to break that cycle of fathers leaving their sons.
The show had been so magical that people didn't want to leave the theater, didn't want to break the spell.
Smoking is such a hard habit to break.
Mike had to leave to break up a fight between Ronni and Bridget.
The rain finally broke on Monday evening.

glosses: If news breaks, it becomes known.
If your voice breaks, it changes because you are almost crying.

examples.text: "I wanted to say goodbye before he died", she said, her voice breaking.

glosses: If you break some money, you change a note into coins.

examples.text: I don't want to break a twenty just to buy matches.

glosses: A break is a time when something stops before starting again.

examples.text: We get a 15-minute break in the middle of the morning.
I'll phone you during my lunch break.
We're going to take a one-minute commercial break and we'll be right back.

glosses: A break (up) is an end of a relationship.

examples.text: We didn't see each other for years after the break up.

glosses: A break is a space between something continuous.

examples.text: The sun shone through a break in the clouds.

glosses: A break is a situation in which things are not as difficult.

examples.text: That job opening up just when she finished school was a lucky break for her.
Give me a break.
The new law would give middle-income families a $2,000 tax break.

glosses: A break is a place where something is broken.

examples.text: The break in his leg could be seen clearly on the x-ray.

glosses: The plural form of person; more than one (kind of) person.

examples.text: Who are these people at the party?

glosses: A people is a group of men, women, and children with a shared culture, history, and language.

examples.text: Although Lebanon and Syria are two countries they are one people.
This people shares some characteristics with the aborigines.

glosses: If a place is peopled, people live there.

examples.text: It's a wonderful country peopled with amazing cooks and dancers.

glosses: If you people a story, movie, etc. you fill it with people.

examples.text: He liked to people his books with simple folk.

glosses: A church where a bishop is based.

examples.text: The new bishop took control of his cathedral.

glosses: ordinal fiftieth) The number 50.

examples.text: There were fifty people in my class.

glosses: The number 50.

examples.text: Five tens is fifty.

glosses: ordinal fortieth) The number 40.

examples.text: He was forty minutes late.

glosses: The number 40.

examples.text: Four tens is forty.

glosses: A registry is an official list of names.
A system of beliefs, ideas, values, and habits that is a way of thinking about the real world.

examples.text: At the time, this way of thinking was the dominant paradigm for social scientists.

glosses: A paradigm is an example, model or pattern, especially the most basic or central one.

examples.text: For fifteen centuries Aristotle remained the paradigm of knowledge itself.
It provides paradigms of action and role models through which we interpret `real life'.

glosses: (Grammar) A paradigm is the set of all word forms.

examples.text: The complete paradigm for boy is: boy, boy’s, boys, boys’, boyish.

glosses: A channel is a path that carries or directs flow or movement, especially of TV & radio signals and water.

examples.text: He only watches two television news channels.

glosses: The bottom and sides ("banks") of a river or other place where water moves.
The natural or man-made deeper course through a reef, bar, bay, or any shallow body of water.
The part of a river where boats can pass.

examples.text: We have to keep our boat in the channel.

glosses: A narrow body of water between two land masses.

examples.text: The English Channel lies between France and England.

glosses: A connection between initiating and terminating nodes of a circuit.

examples.text: The guard-rail provided the channel between the downed wire and the tree.

glosses: The part that connects a data source to a data sink.

examples.text: A channel stretches between them.

glosses: A path for conveying electrical or electromagnetic signals.

examples.text: We are using one of the 24 channels.

glosses: A path provided by a transmission medium via physical separation, such as by multipair cable.

examples.text: The channel is created by bonding the signals from these four pairs.

glosses: A single path provided by a transmission medium via spectral or protocol separation, such as by frequency or time-division multiplexing.

examples.text: Their call is being carried on channel 6 of the T-1 line.

glosses: A specific radio frequency or band of frequencies, usually in conjunction with a predetermined letter, number, or codeword, and allocated by international agreement.

examples.text: KNDD is the channel at 107.7 MHz in Seattle.

glosses: A specific radio frequency or band of frequencies used for transmitting television.

examples.text: NBC is on channel 11 in San Jose.

glosses: The portion of a storage medium, such as a track or a band, that is accessible to a given reading or writing station or head.

examples.text: This chip in this disk drive is the channel device.

glosses: The way in a turbine pump where the pressure is built up.

examples.text: The liquid is pressurized in the lateral channel.

glosses: If you channel something, you direct its flow.

examples.text: We will channel the cars to the left.

glosses: To take on the personality of another person.

examples.text: When it is my turn to sing Karaoke, I am going to channel Ray Charles.

glosses: A position or arrangement.

examples.text: What kind of pose is best for this photograph?

glosses: An unusual position.
To set in place.
To ask, set (a test or quiz).

examples.text: The emcee will pose the tie-breaking question.

glosses: To maintain a pose.
to strike a pose or a position

examples.text: Will you pose for a photograph?
Have you posed for your portrait?
Some celebs spend too much time posing for photographs.

glosses: An encounter is a meeting, usually one that you don't expect.

examples.text: I had a pleasant encounter yesterday: an old friend of mine visited me.
My job was really the result of a chance encounter with an old friend, now my boss.

glosses: An encounter is when two people or groups meet to play a game or fight a battle.

examples.text: I hope there will be no encounter with other soldiers tomorrow.
This is the fifth World Cup encounter between these two teams.

glosses: If you encounter problems, difficulties, etc., you experience them.

examples.text: When he did encounter problems, he always knew how to fix them.

glosses: If you encounter someone, you meet someone, usually unexpectedly.

examples.text: In the store I encountered my teacher.

glosses: If you encounter someone, you meet them to play a game or fight a battle.

examples.text: At night the battle ship encountered enemy planes.

glosses: If someone or something is persistent, they continue and do not give up quickly.

examples.text: She has had a persistent cough for weeks.
There was a persistent knocking on the door.
Many youth who spend time in jail actually become persistent offenders.
There have been persistent rumors for years.

glosses: Lasting past maturity without falling off.

examples.text: Pine cones have persistent scales.

glosses: If you undergo something, it happens to you; often it is not nice.

examples.text: The country has undergone great changes in the last decade.
She had to undergo surgery because of her broken leg.
The bridge is currently undergoing tests to see if it can be reopened.

glosses: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something.

examples.text: We have to convince her that the world is a sphere.

glosses: If I work on disambiguation, I am helping to get rid of things that are so similar that they cause confusion.

examples.text: This page is a disambiguation page.

glosses: An absolute is something that will always exist.

examples.text: Death is considered to be an absolute.

glosses: If something is absolute, it is complete or total.

examples.text: The light went out and he was in absolute darkness.
The sergeant has absolute power. His soldiers must obey him.

glosses: Something is active if it is turned on or started.

examples.text: One of the computers was active: its screen was bright.

glosses: If someone is active, he or she does exercise often or participates often.

examples.text: She was such an active 80-year-old that she ran the Boston Marathon.
Jenkins is an active member of the Rotary Club since he goes to all the meetings.

glosses: A sentence is active if its subject does the action.

examples.text: "Athena helped Odysseus" is an active sentence because Athena is the one who helped.

glosses: A banyan is a tropical Indian fig tree, Ficus benghalensis, that has many aerial roots.
in the end; when nothing else is left

examples.text: We will all help, but it is you who are ultimately responsible.
The events of 1962 ultimately lead to the end of his government.
Ultimately, the choice depends on what you like.

glosses: An extract is something that has been taken out of something else, usually something that it was part of.

examples.text: Just because a cream contains plant extracts doesn't mean it's good for your skin.
I'll read a short extract from his speech.
Many scientists were interested in other tissue extracts.

glosses: If you extract something, you take it out of something else.

examples.text: Computers are becoming more useful in helping us extract useful information from the data.
The dentist will have to extract two of my teeth.
The roots of the plant extract water from the earth.

glosses: If you survive something, you experience it and you did not die.

examples.text: They survived the war but died two years later.
Some of the factory's equipment from 1827 still survives.
I went to a lecture on surviving in dangerous situations.
These last few months have been hard, but we'll survive.

glosses: If you convert something, you change it so that it has a different function or form.

examples.text: They wanted to convert the room into a study.
The factory was powered originally by water, then converted to steam in 1811.
The electric engine is extremely efficient at converting electrical energy into movement.

glosses: A convert is a person who changed their beliefs or religion.

examples.text: Mr Kinnock is a relatively recent convert to Buddhism.
And we must not discount those who became converts to the new religion.

glosses: Transmission is the sending of something from one place to another, usually something like electricity, a message or a disease.

examples.text: Washing before touching food can prevent the transmission of disease in food and drink.
The new communication lines and will be able to support data transmission at speeds four times faster than today.
The National Transmission System is a network of thousands of kilometres of wire.

glosses: A transmission is a signal, such as TV or radio, that is sent from one place to another.

examples.text: Radio stations have promised live transmission from the concert.

glosses: A transmission in a machine is the parts that transfer the engine's movement to the wheels or other moving parts.

examples.text: The car comes with a four-speed automatic transmission.

glosses: If you infer something, you begin to believe it based on indirect information.

examples.text: We can infer from the old bones that this animal probably walked on two feet.
From the evidence, we can infer the existence of a third child.

glosses: A guarantee is a formal promise that a product will be fixed or replaced or money will be repaid if it breaks or doesn't work.

examples.text: The phone is covered by a six-month guarantee on parts and labour.

glosses: A guarantee is a formal promise that something will happen or be done.

examples.text: The builders will now give performance and completion guarantees and will cover the costs of any problems.
Constitutional guarantees of freedom of speech are common in democracies.
The plan only operates for five years, with no guarantee of continuation.

glosses: If you guarantee something, you promise to fixed or replace it or repay money if it breaks or doesn't work.

examples.text: All of our products are guaranteed against defects in materials and workmanship for 3yrs from date of purchase.

glosses: If you guarantee something, you make a formal promise that something will happen or be done.

examples.text: the European Convention on Human Rights, guarantees the right to give and receive information.
When you put your money with us, your savings are 100% guaranteed.
The Americans said they could not guarantee his safety in Iraqi airspace.
If you go fishing with me, you're almost guaranteed success.

glosses: A guaranty is a formal promise that a product will be fixed or replaced or money will be repaid if it breaks or doesn't work.

examples.text: The phone is covered by a six-month guaranty on parts and labour.

glosses: A guaranty is a formal promise that something will happen or be done.

examples.text: The builders will now give performance and completion guaranties and will cover the costs of any problems.
Constitutional guaranties of freedom of speech are common in democracies.
The plan only operates for five years, with no guaranty of continuation.

glosses: If you guaranty something, you promise to fixed or replace it or repay money if it breaks or doesn't work.

examples.text: All of our products are guarantied against defects in materials and workmanship for 3yrs from date of purchase.

glosses: If you guaranty something, you make a formal promise that something will happen or be done.

examples.text: the European Convention on Human Rights, guaranties the right to give and receive information.
When you put your money with us, your savings are 100% guarantied.
The Americans said they could not guaranty his safety in Iraqi airspace.
If you go fishing with me, you're almost guarantied success.

glosses: An advocate is someone who recommends something.

examples.text: She is a strong advocate for children's right to education.

glosses: An advocate is someone who speaks for someone else, especially a lawyer in court.

examples.text: Volunteers are needed to act as advocates for people with mental health problems.
Only qualified lawyers may act as advocates in the Crown Court.

glosses: If you advocate something, you recommend it.

examples.text: We wish for freedom, but cannot advocate the use of violence.
The Government wants to adopt the approach advocated by Professor David Pearce.

glosses: If something is dynamic, it is changing, usually quickly.

examples.text: Communication is a dynamic process in which the changing situation affects what you say and how you say it.

glosses: If someone is dynamic, they take charge and get things done; they have a lot of energy.

examples.text: He was a good worker, but often unnoticed because of his more dynamic coworkers.
Picasso obviously had a more forceful and dynamic personality than Braque.

glosses: of or about motion

examples.text: We tested the bar's strength in both static and dynamic tests.

glosses: A dynamic verb describes an action with a clear end point.

examples.text: Dynamic, but not stative, verbs can take progressive aspect.

glosses: The dynamics of a situation or group are the ways in which everything effects everything else.

examples.text: We talk about what doctor should do without any real understanding of the dynamics of the doctor-patient relationship.
Team dynamics also have an influence on the outcomes and the contribution of members.

glosses: Dynamics is a kind of mathematics that deals with motion and forces that cause changes in a system.

examples.text: They built a computer model based on the mathematics of fluid dynamics.

glosses: Dynamics are changes in the loudness of music.

examples.text: The dynamics of the performance are lost in this poor recording.

glosses: A dynamic is a force that causes change.

examples.text: This is where we need the dynamic of God's transforming presence.
This view puts the dynamic of police racism in the norms and values through which the police define their roles.

glosses: Dynamics is a kind of mathematics that deals with motion and forces that cause changes in a system.

examples.text: Work includes full-scale experiments, wind tunnel studies and computational fluid dynamics.

glosses: to put something into something else

examples.text: The company inserted a new clause into the contract.
Insert a wood screw into each hole.
Doctors removed part of his brain and inserted a silver plate.
A song was inserted into the opening ceremonies.

glosses: An insert is something that is put into something else.

examples.text: The bathing suit top comes with foam inserts to make your breasts look bigger.
The three-page advertisement was included as an insert in today's newspaper.

glosses: If you reverse something, you make it act or move opposite to before (in the other direction).

examples.text: The new president reversed the decision to expand the factory.
There were many new jobs in the early 90s, but then the cycle was completely reversed, and thousands of people were out of work.
She reversed the car into the parking space.
When my mom got sick, our roles were reversed and I began to care for her.
Now reverse your position by raising your right hand and lowering your left.

glosses: The reverse of something is its opposite.

examples.text: Female professors are often married to male professors, but the reverse is not as common.

glosses: In a machine, reverse is a setting that makes it act or move opposite to before.

examples.text: As the plane landed, the engines went into reverse, helping us to stop.
When the Chinese started selling cars, the Japanese automobile industry went into rapid reverse.

glosses: The reverse of something is it's other side.

examples.text: Details can be found on the reverse of this paper.

glosses: If x comprises y, y is part of x.

examples.text: The United States comprises Hawaii and Alaska.

glosses: If x comprises y, y is all the things that, together, make x.

examples.text: The United States comprises 50 states.

glosses: If x comprises y, x is all the things that, together, make y.

examples.text: Fifty states comprise The United States.
The United States is comprised of 50 states.

glosses: self-confident; having a habit of talking strongly about, and asking for what one wants, needs, deserves etc.
Very confident; the person who is assertive is clear and direct.
Being self-confident is being confident about one's self.

examples.text: Sally is self-confident, and she thinks that she can do anything.

glosses: Confidence is the state of trusting something, and being sure that something is going to happen.

examples.text: I know you're trying to gain confidence in what you're doing.

glosses: A state is a condition or a situation.

examples.text: I am worried about her. She is in a constant state of depression.

glosses: Any sovereign nation (nation that rules itself) is a state.

examples.text: The United States is a country with many sovereign nations united with each other.

glosses: To state something is to say it as a fact.

examples.text: He stated that he hasn't slept in 2 days.

glosses: To state something is to let it be known.

examples.text: Please state your name and place of business.

glosses: If something is hierarchical, it has levels, with higher levels being larger, more important, more powerful, etc.

examples.text: The rules show the hierarchical structure of the company.
The society was rigidly hierarchical with priests, nobles and slaves, and a highly organised army.

glosses: If something is comprehensive, it includes everything that is related.

examples.text: The book includes the most comprehensive list of existing government programs.
This chapter is not intended to provide a detailed and comprehensive documentation of the aids available in the UK.

glosses: A mode is a specific way of doing something.

examples.text: The study combines two different research modes: oral history and written history.
The machine is in warm-up mode right now.
A modern city offers many different modes of transport from bicycle lanes to high speed trains.
Modern medicine must be seen as part of the capitalist mode of production.
There is a difference in English between casual and formal modes of speech.

glosses: A mode is a fashion or style.

examples.text: She was always dressed in the latest mode.

glosses: A mode is a specific type or form of something.

examples.text: Heat is a mode of energy transfer, like work, not a substance or other seawater property.

glosses: A mode is specific a kind scale.

examples.text: The Mixolydian mode is a good way for inducing a bluesey kind of mood.
